message.content: When you build the Garden of Demeter, she will transform the land around her Garden into fertile meadow, perfect for supporting farms, livestock and orchards. To find out more about constructing a Sanctuary, click @110here. @PIn order for the Garden of Demeter to provide benefits to the city, its priests must perform regular sacrifices. Priests will search for goats, cattle or sheep to sacrifice. If they can find none, they will sacrifice food to Demeter. @PIn addition to providing fertile land, Demeter will also occasionally manifest herself in the city. As she passes farms, she sanctifies them, causing the next harvest to be more plentiful than usual. @PYou can also offer up prayers to Demeter. If she hears your prayers, she will bless you with a gift of food. If Demeter notices that you are in need, she might grant this blessing of her own accord.

message.title: Grove of Dionysus
message.content: When you build the Grove of Dionysus, the god will plant a vineyard of @36Grapevines, which can be tended and harvested by growers from a @37Growers'&Lodge. Also, no one in your city will feel the need to turn to a life of crime, and become an outlaw. To find out more about building a Sanctuary, click @110here. @PIn order for the Grove of Dionysus to bring benefits to the city, a priest from the Grove must conduct regular sacrifices in honor of Dionysus. The priest will search for a sheep, cattle or goat to sacrifice to the god. If he can't find any, he'll sacrifice food instead. @PSometimes, Dionysus himself will make an appearance in your city, sanctifying any Wineries he encounters. While sanctified, a Winery will produce more wine than usual. @PDionysus is also receptive to prayers. When he answers your prayer, he will grant you a gift of wine from his own stock. If Dionysus notices that you are running low on wine, he might grant this blessing without your having to ask.

message.title: Gates of Hades
message.content: When you erect the Gates of Hades, the great god will induce silver ore to come out of the earth around his Sanctuary. Build a @44Mint, and you can mine this ore to strike coins. In addition, his beloved three-headed hound, Cerberus, will patrol the city, attacking any enemies of yours he runs across. For more information on building a Sanctuary, click @110here. @PIn order for the Gates of Hades to bring benefits to the city, its priests must perform regular sacrifices in honor of the god. Priests from the Gates of Hades will go out in search of sheep, cattle or goats to sacrifice. If they can find none, they'll sacrifice food from the city's Granaries instead. @PEvery now and then, Hades himself will stroll the city's streets, sanctifying @44Mints and @43Foundries, to multiply the wealth of the earth. Hades can also sanctify @26Tax&Offices. While sanctified, the houses around the Tax Office will pay more taxes than they usually do. @PYou can also offer up prayers to Hades. If he answers your prayers, he'll bring a sum of drachmas and deposit it in your city's coffers. If Hades notices that you are in dire need, he might give the city drachmas unsolicited.

message.title: Forge of Hephaestus
message.content: The Forge of Hephaestus yields copper ore that can be mined to produce bronze. While the Forge is functioning in your city, none of the city's buildings will catch fire - the god of fire is handy to have on your side. To learn more about building a Sanctuary, click @110here. @PThe Forge of Hephaestus will only bring benefits to the city if its priests conduct regular sacrifice. Priests from the Forge will look for a sheep, cattle or goat to sacrifice. If they can find none, they will sacrifice food from a Granary instead. If the priests fail to find any sacrifice for an extended period of time, Hephaestus will turn his back on you, and the Forge will no longer benefit the city. @PProvided that Hephaestus' priests are making regular sacrifices to the god, Hephaestus himself might make an appearance in your city, and sanctify some of your Armories and Sculpture Studios. While sanctified, these industries will produce more weapons or sculptures than usual...assuming, of course, that they have sufficient raw materials. @PHephaestus will also respond to your prayers. If Hephaestus answers your prayer, he will assign Talos, his man of bronze, as guardian of the city for a short time. If Hephaestus notices that your city is going to be invaded by a particularly strong force, he might grant you the use of Talos completely unsolicited.

message.title: Hermes' Refuge
message.content: With Hermes' Refuge working in the city, the god of travel and commerce will speed the city's deliverymen, trade ships and trade caravans on their ways. In addition, the traders will visit more frequently. To learn more about building a Sanctuary, click @110here. @PFor Hermes' Refuge to bring benefits to the city, its priests must perform regular sacrifices. A priest from Hermes' Refuge will go in search of a sheep, cattle or goat to sacrifice. If he can find none, he'll take some food from a Granary for the sacrifice instead. @PHermes will also listen to your prayers. If he chooses to answer your prayer, he will fulfill an outstanding request for goods by another city, at no cost to you. Sometimes, if he sees that you can't fulfill an outstanding request on time, he'll fulfill it for you on his own.

message.title: Promontory of Poseidon
message.content: When the Promontory of Poseidon is in your city, Poseidon will assign his fearsome Kraken to patrol your city's waters, protecting you from waterborne threats. Poseidon will also increase the bounty of the sea, making your @38Fisheries&and&Urchin&Quays more productive. @PIn order for the city to receive benefits from the Promontory of Poseidon, priests from the Promontory must perform regular sacrifices. The priests will go out in search of goats, cattle or sheep for the sacrifice to the god. If they can't find any, they will sacrifice food from a @9Granary instead. @PSometimes, the great Poseidon himself will meander through your city, sanctifying Urchin Quays and Fisheries. While sanctified, Urchin Quays and Fisheries will yield more seafood than usual. He may also sanctify a Horse Ranch, adding more livestock to the corral. @PYou can also pray to Poseidon for help. If he answers your prayer, he'll bless you with a gift of seafood deposited into one of your Granaries. If Poseidon notices that you are in dire need of food, he might decide to help you on his own. Please note that your city's waters must have fish or urchins living in them for Poseidon to fulfill your prayer or offer you a blessing.

message.title: Zeus' Stronghold
message.content: When Zeus' Stronghold is in your city, Zeus himself will protect you from any other angry god. Leaders of other cities react more favorably to a leader who has Zeus' Stronghold in his city. Zeus will also grant you the use of his oracle. @PIn order for Zeus' Stronghold to provide benefits, its priests must conduct regular sacrifices. The priests will look for sheep, cattle or goats to offer up to Zeus. If they can find none, they will offer food from a Granary. @PSometimes the almighty Zeus himself will appear in your city. He can sanctify many of the city's buildings, if he so chooses. Zeus can perform any sanctification that any other god can perform. @PZeus will also heed your prayers. If he grants your prayer, he will personally repel the next enemy army that invades your city. If Zeus notices that a particularly strong army is coming to attack your city, he may take it upon himself to crush it on your behalf. @PFinally, the oracle at Zeus' temple will help you predict the future. If the priestesses at the oracle respond to your inquiries, they will alert you to an event that will happen in one year's time. Sometimes, the priestesses offer up a prediction completely unsolicited.

message.title: Achilles' Hall
message.content: Before the great Achilles will come to your city, you must build a Hero's Hall for him. From the Mythology Tab, click the Hero's Hall button and choose Achilles' Hall from the list that appears. Achilles' Hall must be built along a road. @PSimply building Achilles' Hall isn't enough to lure him to your city. Achilles prizes military achievements above all, and therefore demands that you meet several conditions before he'll come to your city. You'll see these conditions, and whether you've attained them, listed when you right-click on Achilles' Hall. When you've met all the conditions, a button that reads 'Send for Achilles' will appear on the right-click panel. @PThere are many reasons you might need to summon Achilles. You might need to send him on a quest, or you might need him to battle a @92monster, like Hector or the Maenad. Heroes are in high demand, so you will not be able to build Achilles' Hall unless you really need his help. Once you've drawn Achilles to your city, he'll stick around for the rest of the episode, even after he's completed the task you have for him. @PAchilles is also willing to fight other @92monsters, but he might need some of your warriors to help him out. He'll help to defend your city from an invading army and will even try his best to defeat an invading god. You can also send him abroad to fight with your forces.

message.title: Hercules' Hall
message.content: Before Hercules will set foot in your city, you must first build his Hall. Select the Mythology Tab, and click on the Hero's Hall button. Choose Hercules' Hall from the list that pops up. Hercules' Hall must be built along a road. Heroes are much needed throughout the world, so you will not be able to build Hercules' Hall unless you really need his help. @PSimply building Hercules' Hall is not enough to get him to come to your city. Hercules enjoys the best of whatever the land has to offer. While in Greece, Hercules finds an athletically minded and cultured city to be to his taste, so you first have to meet several criteria to make the city worthy of his presence. While in Atlantis, he thirsts for the latest scientific knowledge and won't come to the city until he knows his needs will be satisfied. Right-click on Hercules' Hall to see what Hercules expects, and whether or not you've met his expectations. Once you've met them, a button that reads 'Send for Hercules' will appear on the panel. Click this button, and Hercules will come to your city. @PThere are several reasons you might need Hercules in your city. You might need him to complete a quest, or you might need him to battle a @92monster like Hydra or Cerberus. Once he has completed the task you have for him, Hercules will stay in the city for the remainder of the episode. @PHercules is also willing to fight other @92monsters, but he might need some help from your warriors. He'll help to defend your city from an invading army and will even try his best to defeat an invading god. You can also send him abroad to fight.

message.title: Jason's Hall
message.content: To summon Jason to your city, you must first build his Hall. Select the Mythology Tab, and click on the Hero's Hall button. From the list that appears, choose Jason's Hall. Jason's Hall needs to be built along a road. Heroes are always in high demand, so you will not be able to build Jason's Hall unless you really need his help for a specific task. @PJason loves to explore and seek adventure, and therefore expects your city to meet certain conditions before he will come to help you. To see these conditions, right-click on Jason's Hall. You'll see which conditions you've met and which you still need to meet. Once you've fulfilled all the conditions, a button that reads 'Send for Jason' will appear. Click this button, and Jason will come to your city. @PJason is particularly valuable in certain quests and for battling Talos and the Dragon. He's also willing to fight other @92monsters, but he might need help from your warriors. He'll help to defend your city from an invading army and will even try his best to defeat an invading god. You can also send him abroad to fight.

message.title: Odysseus' Hall
message.content: Before Odysseus will come to your city, you must build Odysseus' Hall. To build the Hall, select the Mythology Tab, and then click on the Hero's Hall button. From the list that appears, choose Odysseus' Hall. Make sure you give Odysseus' Hall access to a road. Heroes are always in high demand, so you will not be able to build Odysseus' Hall unless you really need him to perform a specific task. @PPlacing Odysseus' Hall is just the first step in drawing him to your aid. A leader himself, Odysseus will not feel you are worthy of his assistance unless your city is quite well developed. You must therefore meet several requirements before you can summon the hero. You'll see these requirements listed when you right-click on Odysseus' Hall. As you complete the requirements, they will be checked off the list. When you have met them all, a button that reads 'Send for Odysseus' will appear. Click this button, and Odysseus will come to your city. @POdysseus is most effective on certain quests and for battling Scylla or Cyclops. He's also willing to fight other @92monsters, but he might need help from some of your warriors to be successful. He'll help to defend your city from an invading army and will even try his best to defeat an invading god. You can also send him abroad to fight.

message.title: Perseus' Hall
message.content: Before Perseus will come to your city, you must first build a Hall for him. Select the Mythology Tab, and click the Hero's Hall button. From the list that appears, choose Perseus' Hall. Make sure that Perseus has access to a road. Heroes are always in high demand, so you will not be able to build Perseus' Hall unless you need his help for a specific task. @POnce you've built Perseus' Hall, you'll need to meet fulfill several requirements before Perseus will come to the city. Perseus is always wrapped up in the affairs of the gods, so he expects your city, too, to honor the gods. Right-click on Perseus' Hall to see what you need to do to make your city worthy of the hero's presence. Once you've fulfilled all the requirements, a button that reads 'Send for Perseus' will appear. Click on the button, and Perseus will come to the city. @PSome quests may only be achieved by Perseus. Perseus can also effectively protect your city against attacks by Kraken and Medusa. He's also willing to fight other @92monsters, but some of your warriors may need to join in the fight if he is to be successful. Perseus will help to defend your city from an invading army and will even try his best to defeat an invading god.

message.title: Theseus' Hall
message.content: To lure Theseus to the city, first build Theseus' Hall. Choose the Mythology Tab, and click the Hero's Hall button. From the list that appears, choose Theseus' Hall. Heroes are always in high demand, so you will only be able to build Theseus' Hall if you need his help for a specific task. Theseus' Hall must have access to a road, and he will only live in the best neighborhoods, so be sure his Hall is near the city's Palace. To see if you've placed Theseus' Hall close enough to the Palace, right-click on the Hall. A list of requirements will appear. If Theseus' Hall is close enough to the Palace, that particular requirement will be checked off. @PBefore Theseus will come to your city, you must meet all of the requirements listed on the Hall's right-click panel. When you've met them, a button that reads 'Send for Theseus' will appear. Click on this button, and Theseus will come to the city. @PCertain quests can only be achieved by Theseus. Theseus is also quite effective in fighting the Minotaur and Calydonian Boar. He's willing to fight other @92monsters, but may be defeated without help from some of your warriors. Theseus will help to defend your city from an invading army and will even try his best to defeat an invading god. You can also send him abroad to fight.

message.title: Hunting Lodge
message.content: Hunters from a Hunting Lodge go out in search of @102wild&boar, @151deer or both. @PTo build a Hunting Lodge, choose the @77Husbandry&Tab and click on the Land and Sea button. Choose Hunting Lodge from the list that appears. @PThe Hunting Lodge must have access to a road so that it can access the city's labor pool. Once the Hunting Lodge has a staff, it sends out hunters who slay prey and bring it back to the lodge to be carved into sides of meat. Once the meat is ready, the Hunting Lodge's deliveryman will take the meat to a @9Granary or, if you are exporting the item, a @12Pier or @11Trading&Post. Make sure the Hunting Lodge is connected by a road to the meat's destination. @PYou don't necessarily need to build a Hunting Lodge close to the prey. The closer the Lodge is to the animals, however, the more efficient the hunt will be.

message.title: Pillar of Atlas
message.content: When you honor Atlas by building his Sanctuary, he watches over your construction industry, making it more efficient. Stonecutters are able to chisel both @42white and @131black&marble more quickly, and each @45Artisans'&Guild sends out twice as many artisans to construction sites. @PIn order for the Pillar of Atlas to fully function, priests must perform regular sacrifices. Atlas prefers to receive goats, sheep or cattle as sacrifice, but will settle for food from your Granary if no animals are available. @PAtlas himself may wander your city's streets from time to time. As he strolls along, he may sanctify the @41Timber&Mills and @127Refineries that he passes. A sanctified Timber Mill or Refinery will be more productive than usual. @PYou can also pray to Atlas. If Atlas answers your prayer, he will speed up a construction project in your city. After he blesses a construction site, any materials that were en route to the site will magically appear, and the materials will last longer. Artisans will not have to wait for goods to be delivered to the construction site as long as the effects of your prayer continue. Once the effects wear off, construction returns to normal. Atlas may grant this blessing of his own accord if he notices that he can be of service.

message.title: Orchard of Hera
message.content: After the Orchard of Hera is complete, a stand of @149Orange&Trees will appear in front of her Sanctuary. These Orange Trees can be tended and harvested by tenders from an @109Orange&Tenders'&Lodge. If you honor Hera with a Sanctuary, she will also cause an increase to the birth rate, and your population will grow even if no one is immigrating to your city. And, if your city is the unfortunate target of Zeus' wrath, Hera will stand up to her husband and turn him away, saving your city from hardship. @PPriests must offer up sacrifices to the goddess if the Orchard of Hera is to function properly. Priests prefer to offer Hera goats, sheep or cattle, but will offer her food from a Granary in a pinch. @PSometimes, Hera may visit your city. As she walks the city's streets, she may sanctify the @108Corrals and Orange Tenders' Lodges that she passes. While these buildings are sanctified, they will produce more food than usual. @PFinally, you can offer up a prayer to Hera. If Hera answers your prayer, she will add supplies to all of the city's Agoras. If she notices that your Agoras are running low on supplies, she may grant this blessing on her own.

message.title: Citadel of Poseidon
message.content: Without Poseidon, Atlantis would have been some lonely continent in the middle of the ocean instead of a thriving powerhouse. When Atlanteans honor Poseidon with a Sanctuary, they build the Citadel of Poseidon. @PThe Citadel of Poseidon is a large and elaborate structure and features a gorgeous statue of the Ruler of the Sea. When the Citadel of Poseidon is complete, the god sees to it that workers from Fisheries and Urchin Quays have no problems finding seafood. When the god's Sanctuary is in the city, both of these industries work faster. The great god also sends Kraken, the ferocious monster, to guard the city's waters from enemies. @PIn order for the Citadel to function properly, priests must conduct regular sacrifices. Priests will go in search of sheep, goats or cattle to sacrifice to the god. If they can't find any suitable animals, they will take food from the Granary. @PPoseidon may decide to pay your city a visit after you've constructed his Citadel. As he walks...er, paddles...around your streets, he may sanctify the city's Fisheries, Urchin Quays and Horse Ranches. While a building is sanctified, it is more productive than usual. @PIf you lack food, pray to Poseidon. If he answers your prayer, he will bring a bountiful supply of seafood to a Granary. If the god notices that you are low on food, he may bring you food of his own volition.

message.title: Building Pyramids of all Types
message.content: Large and beautiful buildings are a testament to the advancements of Atlantean culture. Generically, all these buildings are called Pyramids. The types of Pyramid are @153Pyramids, @155Monuments&to&the&Sky, @154Shrines to a specific god, the @156Altar&of&Olympus, the @157Temple&of&Olympus, the @158Pyramid&of&the&Pantheon, the @159Observatory&Kosmika and the @160Museum&Atlantika. @PAll of these buildings are built in a similar way, though each requires different resources. Click on the name of a specific edifice above to find out what resources you need to build it. In addition to the proper supplies, you also need artisans from an @45Artisans'&Guild. @PTo place one of these buildings, select the Aesthetics Tab and then click the 'Pyramids' button. Choose the building you would like to construct, then guide the building's footprint to the spot in the city where you'd like to place it. If the footprint turns green, you've picked a suitable location. Click the mouse button to set the foundation of the building in place. If the footprint is red, then something is preventing you from building in the selected location. You can either try clearing away any obstructions or find a new location. @PYou can rotate the footprint by pressing the 'r' button. You can also freeze the footprint if you press the 'm' button. While the footprint is frozen, you can scroll your view normally. You'll be able to see if there is something obstructing the building and see how it fits in with its surroundings. @PAfter you place the structure, you'll notice that there is a plank on one of the edges. This plank must be connected to a road so that artisans and the needed supplies can reach the building. @PYou can halt construction at any time by right-clicking on the construction site and clicking the 'Halt Construction' button. Artisans will finish up their current tasks and then return to the Guild or find another construction project that needs their services. @PAs long as you have artisans and the materials that you need, construction should run smoothly. The workers will take it upon themselves to build necessary support structures, like Lifts, to aid their progress. If you notice that construction has stopped, right-click on the Pyramid to find out what the problem is. You can also see a general Pyramid construction status report by selecting the @85Aesthetics&Tab. Click on the small magnifying glass to see even more information about your construction projects.

message.title: Atalanta's Hall
message.content: Before Atalanta will set foot in your city, you must build her Hero's Hall and outfit it with her favorite accoutrements. You'll see the list of her demands when you right-click on the Hero's Hall. As you meet each demand, it will be checked off. @POnce you've met the requirements, right-click on the Hero's Hall and click on the 'Summon Atalanta' button. The famed huntress will make her way to your city. @PYou'll need Atalanta's services to fulfill certain quests. She is also quite adept at fighting the Harpies and the Sphinx. You can also send Atalanta to fight abroad.

message.title: Overview Tab
message.content: The Overview Tab highlights the general state of affairs in your city. You can see at a glance how @122popular you are with your citizens, the city's stored @116food levels, the @121employment situation, the city's @118hygiene and @123unrest levels, how your @120finances are fairing compared to last year, and whether there are any military threats to the city. You can also see if any other leaders have made @111requests of you, and how many more months you have to fulfill them. Any Quests that gods have issued will also be listed here. For a closer look, click on the Magnifying Glass button and you'll see more detailed information on the state of your city. @PAt the top of the Overview Tab are two buttons that will give you special views of your city. Click on 'See Roads,' and all the buildings in the city will flatten, leaving just the roads behind. The 'See Roads' button helps you plan your road network and can help you to see if there are any problems with the current arrangement of roads. @PThe 'See Problems' button will reveal any building or walker in the city that is not working properly. It will show which of the city's houses are at risk for a range of problems, including whether it is vacant, about to devolve, about to catch fire or collapse, or about to produce a criminal. This view will also show which of the city's industries are lacking sufficient raw materials, don't have enough workers or are about to become damaged. You'll also see which Sanctuaries need sacrifices. In addition to identifying problems with buildings, this view highlights deliverymen who are stuck for some reason, whether it be because they cannot get to their destination by a road, or because their destination cannot accept their goods. Any buildings that have already collapsed or are on fire will also be highlighted when you press the 'See Problems' button. @PThe Overview Tab always displays a small overview map of your city, so that you can see more of your city at one time. To display this map on all tabs simultaneously, click the overview map tab at the top the @86Control&Panel.

message.title: Population Tab
message.content: The Population Tab helps you to manage the city's population levels. @PWhen you've selected the Population Tab, you will see two buttons that you can use to designate housing plots, one for @6common&housing and one for @7elite&housing. You'll also see information on the current trends in immigration. The summary tells you how many more people the city's housing can accommodate. It also tells you whether or not people want to come to your city, and how many immigrants arrived in the last month. If people are leaving the city or if immigration is being limited, the summary will tell you so, and why. @PYou can see which houses are in danger of running out of supplies - and thus in danger of devolving - by clicking the 'See Supplies' button at the top of the @86Control&Panel. When you click this button, icons representing each house's supplies appear. If a house lacks an item or is in danger of running out of it, the icon for that item will have a flashing red background. @PFor a closer look at the city's population, click on the Magnifying Glass button. A graph will appear that shows how the city's population has grown or shrunk over time. Click on the 'View Society Graph' button, and a graph that shows the city's population by soldier type will appear.

message.title: Husbandry Tab
message.content: The Husbandry Tab provides information on food availability in your city, and helps you manage the city's farms and other agriculture buildings. You can build husbandry buildings using the build buttons located on the bottom third of the Control Panel. For more information on any of the husbandry buildings and livestock, consult the @1Table&of&Contents and look up a specific building or animal. @PThe Husbandry Tab shows you at a glance how many people your current food production and importation can support, and whether you are producing enough food to feed your current population. It also shows you how many months worth of food you have stored in the city's @9Granaries. @PFor a closer look at food production, click on the Magnifying Glass button. You will see a list of each type of food-producer, how many cartloads of food each produces per month, and how many people the food can feed. @PTo see all the Husbandry structures in your city, click on the 'See Husbandry' button at the top of the Control Panel. All non-husbandry structures will be temporarily flattened. If there is a problem at any of your husbandry structures, an icon will appear next to the building. Hold the mouse over the icon, and balloon help will describe what the issue is.

message.title: Industry Tab
message.content: From the Industry Tab, you can manage all of the city's industries. To build an industrial building, use the build buttons located in the bottom third of the Control Panel. If you have questions about a specific industry, consult the @1Table&of&Contents for the entry on that specific industry. @PFrom the Industry Tab, you can set the wage level you wish to pay your workers. By default, wages are set to Normal. You can adjust the wages to Very High, High, Normal, Low, Very Low, or None. Be aware, though, that if you set wages too low, your workers will become upset, and your @122popularity could plummet as a result. The Industry Tab also tells you how many workers the city employs and how many more, if any, are needed. If there is unemployment in the city, the unemployment rate is shown here. @PFor more in-depth control over your city's industries and workers, click on the Magnifying Glass. The screen that appears is divided into two sections. In the upper section, you can dictate which categories or 'sectors' of the city's working buildings are staffed first, in the case of a labor shortage. Decide which sectors are most important to suit your current needs, and assign a priority accordingly using the scroll buttons. The priorities you can assign are very high, high, moderate, low and none. As you adjust the priority levels, you'll see the number of workers assigned to each sector shift. @PThe industries currently in your city are displayed in the lower section of the panel. You can shut an industry down by clicking on it. This can be especially helpful in times of worker shortages. When you shut down an industry, the workers from that industry find new jobs in other sectors of the city. Click on the shut down industry again to reactivate it. @PFinally, click the 'See Industry' button to see all the industries in your city. If any of them are not functioning properly, an icon will appear over the building. Hold your mouse over the icon, and balloon help will describe the problem.

message.title: Distribution Tab
message.content: The Distribution Tab provides information about the various commodities currently in your city, or obtainable by your city. This tab gives valuable information on your imports and exports, and can also help you manage your city's distribution system. @PThe bottom third of the Control Panel contains the Distribution Tab's build buttons. To learn more about a specific Distribution Building, consult the @1Table&of&Contents. @PIn the top section of this tab, items obtainable by the city and not currently being imported or exported are shown. Items being imported or exported are shown in the two areas below this. Clicking on an item instructs the city's storage facilities to stockpile the item, making it unusable for any purpose. Stockpiled items will not be exported, nor delivered to industries that might need them. Also, the city's @8Agoras will not be able to pick up the stockpiled item, although peddlers can still distribute any that the Agoras already have in stock. You might want to stockpile an item if you need it to save it up to meet a request or to draw a hero to the city. When an item is being stockpiled, it appears in yellow, and in parenthesis. @PFor a closer look at your trade relations, click on the Magnifying Glass button. All the items obtainable in your city are listed in the panel that appears. Alongside each item is the price for which the good can be bought or sold. The panel also shows which items you are importing and exporting, and with which cities you are trading. If you click on a city name, the panel will close and your view will be centered on that city's trade facility. @PTo see all the city's Distribution structures, click on the 'See Distribution' button. You'll see all of the city's Agoras, Granaries, Storehouses, and trading facilities, as well as the city's housing. You'll be able to see if any Distribution buildings aren't working properly. If they aren't, an icon will appear next to the building. Hold the cursor over the icon, and balloon help will describe the problem. You'll also see the city's housing and icons of the items each household can use. If the background of the icon is flashing red, then the house has run out of or is about to run out of the item.

message.title: Hygiene and Safety Tab
message.content: The Hygiene and Safety Tab helps you keep an eye on your citizens' hygiene and personal safety. The Hygiene and Safety buildings are the @50Infirmary, @49Fountain, @27Watchpost and @25Maintenance&Office. Click on any of these building names for more information on them. @PThe Hygiene and Safety Tab provides an update on the city's @118hygiene, and the @123unrest levels of the city's houses. For more detailed information, click on the Magnifying Glass. At the top of the panel you'll see a description of the current level of hygiene in the city, followed by summaries of how many people have access to the services of a healer, and how many people are able to eat regularly. It also tells whether plague has broken out recently, as well as how many houses are currently infected by plague. The lower half of the panel lists how many Maintenance Offices and Watchposts are working in the city. It also lists how many outlaws have wreaked havoc on the city recently. @PTo track a particular safety threat, use one of the four buttons located at the top of the Control Panel. Click on the 'See Water' button to watch your city's water bearers at work. You'll also notice blue columns in front of the city's housing. The higher the column, the more recently the house has been supplied with water by a water bearer. If a household runs out of water, their house may devolve. @PClick on the 'See Hygiene' button to see the city's healers walking through the streets and to see which houses practice good hygiene. The higher the column in front of a house is, the more recently a healer has visited. @PClick on the 'See Hazards' button to see which of the city's buildings are at risk for catching fire or collapsing. You'll also see the city's superintendents making their way through the city, fixing buildings. As a superintendent passes a building, he makes sure the building won't catch fire or collapse. @PFinally, click the 'See Unrest' button to make sure that the city's residents are well-behaved and to watch the city's watchmen make their rounds. When you select 'See Unrest', you'll see a columns in front of each of the city's houses. The higher the column, the more likely it is that the house will produce an @123outlaw. As a watchman passes by housing, he makes sure the people inside are keeping on the straight and narrow, and prevents outlaws from hitting the streets.

message.title: Administration Tab
message.content: The Administration Tab helps you to manage your city's finances and control taxation. On the lower third of the Control Panel, you'll see the Administration buildings that you can construct. The buildings are the @24Palace and @26Tax&Office. In Greece, you can also build the @28Water&Crossing. In Atlantis, buttons for @161Bridges and @139Hippodromes. For more information on any of these buildings, click on the links in the previous sentences. @PThe Administration Tab shows you at a glance the city's tax collection practices. You can see the city's current tax rate and how many tax drachmas you are currently collecting. It also shows you how many people in the city are registered for the tax, and how many drachmas have gone uncollected due to people not being visited by a clerk. You can adjust the tax rate by using the scroll buttons at the top of the panel. The tax rate levels are outrageous, very high, high, normal, low, very low and none. While setting a higher tax rate will obviously yield more drachmas, the city's residents will tire quickly of paying exorbitant taxes. Your popularity could plummet, and your citizens could emigrate. @PTo see which houses are currently paying taxes, click on the 'See Taxes' button. You'll see the city's clerks walking through the streets. You'll also see columns in front of the city's housing, indicating how recently a clerk has passed by. The higher the column, the more recently the clerk has visited, indicating that you don't need to worry about the house missing a tax payment. If a household has paid any taxes, you'll see a stack of coins in front of its dwelling. The higher the stack of coins, the more taxes have been paid. You can hold the cursor over the column or stack of coins for more specific information. If you notice that a particular neighborhood has not been paying taxes, you might want to build a Tax Office in the area. @PThe Administration Tab also briefly updates you on your income and expenditures for the year to date. For more detailed information, click on the Magnifying Glass button. A complete financial report appears in the screen that pops up, comparing the previous year's financial performance to the current year's. If you're losing money, this report can reveal the city's largest expenditures. Then, you can adjust your spending policies accordingly. @PFor more information, consult the @120money entry.

message.title: Culture Tab
message.content: The Culture Tab will help you keep an eye on your city's cultural centers, all of which may be built from the Culture Tab. For more information on a particular building, consult the @1Table&of&Contents. @PIf the @112Pan-Hellenic&Games have begun in Greece, then the Culture Tab shows you at a glance how you are likely to fare in each of them. If the Pan-Hellenic Games have not begun, then the Culture Tab will show how good the city's access is to the various forms of cultural diversions. If you notice that your city is lacking in a particular type of cultural pursuit, or is likely to fare poorly in one of the Pan-Hellenic Games, use the buttons at the top of the tab to see which areas of the city could benefit from more culture centers. The 'See Philosophers' button, on the Culture tab, shows you all your philosophers at work. Columns in front of the city's housing indicate whether or not a philosopher has visited lately. The higher the column, the more recent the philosopher's visit. The 'See Athletes' button lets you see the city's athletes and identify which houses they have recently visited. Click on the 'See Actors' button to see the city's actors walking through the streets, bringing the joys of the theater to the houses they pass. Columns in front of housing indicate how recently a house has been entertained by an actor. The 'See Competitors' button shows you the city's competitors and which houses have benefited from their amazing skills. Finally, the 'See All Culture' button combines each of the three above views, and shows how much overall culture each house has access to. @PClick on the Magnifying Glass button for a more detailed look at culture in your city. You'll see how good city-wide coverage is for each culture type. If the Pan-Hellenic Games have begun in Greece, then you'll also receive advice on how to increase your chances doing well in next Pan-Hellenic Games.

message.title: Mythology Tab
message.content: The Mythology Tab helps you keep track of @93gods, @94heroes and @92monsters in your city. To build Sanctuaries, Hero's Halls and Artisans' Guilds, use the buttons that appear on the lower third of the Control Panel. For specific information regarding any of these buildings, consult the @1Table&of&Contents. @PThe Mythology Tab lists which Sanctuaries you've built or are building in the city. While you are building a Sanctuary, the Mythology Tab will let you know which supply it needs next to continue construction. When the Sanctuary is complete, the Mythology Tab will update you on the Sanctuary's current activity. Click on the activity to go to the Sanctuary and see for yourself what is going on. If you click on the god's name, and the god is currently in your city, you will be taken directly to the god so you can see what the Olympian is up to. @PThe Mythology Tab also updates you on the less-than-friendly gods and monsters in your city. When they arrive in your city, their names will be listed in yellow. Click on their names, and you will be taken to where they are wreaking havoc. @PYou can also click the 'See Immortals' button to view all of the gods, monsters, heroes and Sanctuaries in your city. @PFor more information on the gods and heroes in your city, click on the Magnifying Glass button. You will see which gods are currently being worshiped in the city, and whether they are willing to answer your prayer. There is also a list of the other gods you can worship, but haven't built a Sanctuary for yet. You'll also see which heroes are in the city. Finally, gods unfriendly to your city are listed. Click on any name to go directly to that personage.

message.title: Military Tab
message.content: The Military Tab helps you to keep track of your soldiers and ships. Consult the @1Table&of&Contents to learn more about the specific military buttons. @PThe Military Tab updates you at a glance to your military's current activities. Each of the city's companies and ships is represented by an icon. The Military Tab will tell you which of your companies and ships have been called to arms and are ready to defend the city, which are abroad and which are standing down. To find out the name of each company, hold your cursor over an icon and the name will appear. Click on an icon to go directly to the company's standard or to the ship. @PYou can also call all of your soldiers to arms from the Military Tab, provided you've positioned their standards in the field. Simply click the 'Call All' button. The button will change to read 'All called', and all your soldiers will leave their homes and go to their standards. To send them home, click the same button, which now reads 'All Called'. If all the companies' standards are at the Palace, then the phrase 'At Palace' will appear. You can issue similar orders to your ships and @31Towers. Click on 'Crew Ships' to call the crews to their vessels. Click the same button, now called 'All Crewed', to send them back home. If you don't have ships, the phrase 'No Ships' will appear. For Towers, click 'Not Manning' to call the sentries to their posts. The button's label changes to 'Manning', which sends the Tower guards back home if clicked. 'No Towers' will appear if you haven't yet built Towers. @PAbove the Magnifying Glass button is a button with a helmet on it. Click on this helmet to toggle auto-defend on and off. When auto-defend is on, your generals will handle all the tactical decisions for you in battle. With auto-defend off, you are in complete control of giving orders to your troops. For more on the orders you can give, choose a soldier type: @104rabble, @105hoplites @106horsemen, @145archers, @146spearmen and @147charioteers. @PClick on the Magnifying Glass button for a closer look at your military. In the screen that pops up, all of your companies are listed by type, and your ships are listed as well. In addition, if any mercenary troops have been loaned to you by other cities for defense, they are listed here. Finally, if Ares' or Artemis' warriors are helping you, they will be listed here as well. @PNext to each company name is a description of its current status. The statuses for companies are At Home, Still, Marching, Going Home, Fleeing, Fighting and Abroad. Sometimes, the statuses are displayed on a button. In such cases, clicking the button issues an order. If a company is At Home, you can click on 'At Home' to call them to arms. A Still company has been called to arms, but is not yet fighting. To send this company home, click on 'Still'. If a company is Marching, you can click on the 'Marching' button to send them home. If a company is under orders to return home, you can click the 'Going Home' button to re-muster the soldiers. Finally, you can send home a company that is Fighting by clicking on the 'Fighting' button. @PSimilarly, some of the ship statuses double as orders. When a vessel is without a crew, clicking on 'unmanned' will call the crew to the ship. If a ship has a crew but is still anchored at its Wharf, clicking on 'Anchored' will send the crew home. If a ship is sailing, clicking on the 'Sailing' button will send the ship's crew home. If a ship is disembarking its crew and sending them home, clicking on the 'Disembarking' button will call the crew back to the ship. Finally, if the ship is currently fighting, clicking on the 'Fighting' button will send the crew home. A vessel can also be returning to the Wharf, under repair or abroad.

message.title: Aesthetics Tab
message.content: The Aesthetics Tab helps you to manage how visually appealing the city's different neighborhoods are and helps you keep track of an Atlantean city's Pyramids and other monumental structures. At the bottom of the Control Panel, you'll see buttons for the types of aesthetic structure you can build. The buttons are the Beautification Structures button, the Recreational Areas button and the Commemorative Monuments button. The Commemorative Monuments button appears only when you have been awarded a Commemorative Monument but haven't built it yet. For specific information on each of the aesthetic structures, consult the @1Table&of&Contents. @PIf you are in Atlantis, you may also see the Pyramid button here. For more on Pyramids and other large structures, click @73here. @PThe Aesthetics tab also lists all the Commemorative Monuments you currently have in the city. In addition, in Atlantis the tab lists the pyramids that you are building in the city. The information on the Control Panel will give you a brief overview of the current status of your pyramids. For more information on your pyramids and Commemorative Monuments, click the small Magnifying Glass button. More specific information regarding the current state of your pyramids will appear. You can also click on the name of a Commemorative Monument to center your view on a representative example of the monument in your city. @PAt the top of the Control Panel is the 'See Appeal' button. Click it, and the land in your city will be replaced with colored blocks. The lighter the block, the more appealing the area is. How appealing an area is has no effect on your city's industries, but makes a big difference in your city's residential areas. @PFor more on aesthetics in general, click @119here.

message.title: Control Panel
message.content: The Control Panel provides all the tools you need to build and run a city. Each of its tabs deals with a different facet of building and running a city. As you click on each tab, the information on the Control Panel changes. @PThe Control Panel changes depending on if you are ruling an Atlantean city or a Greek city. If you are leading a Greek city, the @82Culture&Tab will appear on the Control Panel. In an Atlantean city, the @150Science&Tab appears instead. The other tabs on the Control Panel are the @76Population&Tab, the @77Husbandry&Tab, the @78Industry&Tab, the @79Distribution&Tab, the @80Hygiene&and&Safety&Tab, the @81Administration&Tab, the @83Mythology&Tab, the @84Military&Tab, the @85Aesthetics&Tab and the @75Overview&Tab. @PAt the top of the Control Panel, you'll see two other tabs. Click on the left tab, and the above mentioned category tabs will each display information to help you manage your city. Click on the right tab, and the Control panel will always display a small @75Overview&Map of your city. @PIn the lower portion of the Control Panel, (right next to the Overview Tab) are four buttons that are always available to you. They are the Build @5Roads button, the Place Roadblock button, the Clear Land button and the Undo button. Click on the Build Roads button to build roads in your city. With the Place Roadblock button, you can place roadblocks to guide your city's roaming walkers. Use the Clear Land button if you want to demolish a building or remove other obstructions from the land. The Undo button allows you to undo your most recent action. You can only undo your last action while the button is lit. @PBelow these buttons is a space for four 'Go To' buttons that appear when certain situations occur in your city. Clicking on a button will bring you to the site of the occurrence. The first slot is reserved for hazards and catastrophes. Clicking it will bring you to the site of the most recent trouble. The @97Hazard&buttons include fire, earthquake, tidal wave, landslide, lava, collapsed building and blocked road. The second slot is reserved for outbreaks of plague. If someone or something invades the city, then an @99Invasions&button appears. A button will appear here if an enemy, monster or unfriendly god invades the city. Finally, if a hero or friendly god has come to the city, an @100Arrival&button will appear. This button will also appear when a hero returns to a city after a quest or soldiers return from a campaign abroad. @PYou'll also see a @87Messages button on the Control Panel. Click on this button, and a list of all the messages you've received will appear. Click on any message name to read it, or right-click on it to erase it. @PBeneath the Messages button and Go To buttons is the Condensed Message Box. As messages arrive, a brief synopsis of the message will be displayed in the Condensed Message Box. Use the up and down arrows to scroll through the brief synopses of all your messages. To read the full version of the currently displayed message, simply click anywhere on the Condensed Message Box. @PBelow the Condensed Message Box are three more buttons that will help you manage your city. The first button is the Review Goals button. Clicking on this button will bring up a list of objectives required to complete the current episode. You also use this screen to set aside goods for a colony or the parent city. Next to the Review Goals button is the Rotate City button. Click on the left side of the button to rotate the city counter-clockwise. Click on the right side of the button to rotate the city clockwise. Clicking on the center of the button will reorient your view due north. Next to the Rotate City button is the @88View&World&button. Clicking this button will bring up a map of the world.

message.title: Messages
message.content: When a significant event happens in your city or around Greece, you will be sent a message. A synopsis of the message will appear in the Condensed Message Box, at the bottom of the Control Panel. Use the up and down arrows next to the Box to scroll through the synopses for all your messages. You can read a full version of the currently selected message by clicking on the Condensed Message Box, or by clicking on the Message button. When you click on the Message button, a list of the messages you have received will appear. Click on the title of any of the messages to read it, or right-click on it to erase it from the list. @PYou can control how you receive messages by selecting Messages from the Options Menu. A list of the types of messages you receive appears in the panel that pops up. You can choose to receive messages in each category in their 'Full' form, as pop-up messages, in their 'Condensed' form only, or to not receive them at all. When you receive a message as a 'Full' pop-up, a panel will appear when the message arrives, pausing the game, and drawing your attention directly to the message. A condensed version of the message will also appear in the Condensed Message Box. If you choose to receive a message as Condensed only, you will not immediately see the full pop-up, play will continue unimpeded, and a synopsis of the message will appear in the Condensed Message Box. Finally, you can turn a message category off completely to not receive its messages at all.

message.title: World View
message.content: Clicking the World View button brings you to the World Map. From the World Map, you can engage in a variety of activities with other cities and leaders in the world. @PThe World Map shows you the cities in the world, including your own. The icons around the cities on the map reveal basic information about them. The number of shields indicates how large a military force the city has. The more shields, the larger the city's military power. The coins stacked by the city indicate how strong its economy is. If the city can trade with you, you'll see a route drawn to your city. Sea routes are shown in blue, land routes in brown. If the city is a rebelling colony or vassal, you'll see a flickering torch. @PYour relationship with each city is also indicated on the map. The city you are currently governing, whether it be your @111parent&city or a @111colony you are establishing, displays a large square banner. Your @111vassals and established colonies each fly a smaller version of this standard. Your @111allies fly a small banner, while @111rivals and @111distant&cities don't display any banners. If a city has been tragically destroyed by a @92monster, you'll see the ruins of the former city. Enchanted places, the dank lairs that monsters call home, also appear on the map. @PIf there are armies or navies on the move, you'll see them on the World Map. In addition, if heroes are out and about, you'll see them on the world map, too. @PClicking on a city will display more detailed information about it in the panel to the right. At the top of the panel, the city's name will be displayed, along with the city's relationship to you, and the name of its leader. Just below the leader's name is the City History button, which looks like an open scroll. Click on this button to see a history of your interactions with this leader. Most entries are marked by a 'thumbs up' or 'thumbs down' icon, telling you whether the event raised the leader's opinion of you, or caused it to fall. Below the open scroll is a button which shows the leader's current attitude toward you. Click on the attitude button for specific advice on how to improve the leader's attitude. @PIn the center of this panel you'll see any goods the selected city needs or produces. If you are engaged in trade with the city, you will see how much of each good the city wishes to buy and sell, and how much of each you have exported or imported for the year. If you click on the Orders button, you'll see the selected city's @12Pier or @11Trading&Post panel, where you can issue trade instructions. If you are not trading with the city, you can still see which goods the city needs and produces. These tell you what kinds of gifts the city would appreciate receiving from you, and what items you may be able to obtain from the city via requests, raids, demands or even conquest. @PIf you've selected an active colony, ally or rival, you'll see several Action buttons at the bottom of the panel, which you can use to interact with the city. Click the button with the pair of hands on it to make a request or demand of another city. Demands are made of rivals; requests are made of all other cities. When you click the button, a list of the items you can request or demand from the city pops up. Make your choice, and when you return to your city you will be notified whether are not your request or demand was met. @PClick on the button with the pack donkey on it to fulfill the city's outstanding request. If there is more than one outstanding request, a panel will appear when you click this button. Choose the request you would like to fulfill. If the outstanding request is for military assistance, a panel listing your available forces will pop up. You'll see the action that the requesting city wants your troops to take. Select the forces you want to enlist by clicking on them, then click the Dispatch button. @PTo give a gift to a city, click the button with the coins on it. Choose a gift from the list that pops up. Leaders most appreciate gifts of items that their city needs, and don't care all that much for gifts of items their city already produces. @PClick on the button with the soldier hiding behind some brush to raid a city. It's easier to successfully raid another city than it is to conquer it, but the rewards aren't as great. After you click on the button, you'll see a panel allowing you to select the raiding party, and give orders regarding what item you would like it to plunder. Click on the Select Plunder button to choose what you want your soldiers to steal from the city. Then, select which forces you want to carry out the deed, and click the Dispatch button to send them on their way. Each soldier or ship can only carry a certain amount of plunder back to your city, so the more forces you send, the more rewarding the raid will be. If the city cannot be accessed by water, you cannot dispatch ships as part of the raiding party. @PFinally, click on the button that has soldiers on it to attempt to conquer the selected city or, in the case of a vassal or colony, to quell a rebellion. When you click the attack button, you'll see a panel allowing you to enlist military forces for the attempted conquest. From this panel, select the companies and ships you'd like to enlist for your military campaign, and click dispatch. If the city cannot be accessed by water, you cannot dispatch ships as part of the attack force. @PTo cycle through the cities on the world map, click on the arrows that are to the right and left of the City History button. And, to return to your city, click on the Back to City button.

message.title: Rotate View
message.content: Click this button to rotate the view of your city. Click on the left side to rotate the view counter-clockwise, and click on the right side to rotate it clockwise. Clicking on the center of the button reorients your view due north. Rotating the city can be very helpful if any particularly tall buildings in the city are obscuring your view.

message.title: Goals
message.content: Click on the Review Goals button to see what you need to do to complete the episode you are playing. Each of your goals will be listed as well as an update on your progress of each goal. If you've completed a goal, it will be checked off. You also use this screen to set aside goods for a colony or the parent city and send a hero on a quest, if they are episode goals.

message.title: Walkers
message.content: The people moving around in your city are called walkers. Walkers emerge from the buildings you place, and are generally guided by the road network you create. There are several different walkers, but just about all of them can be grouped into two categories: roaming walkers and destination walkers. @PRoaming walkers patrol the city with no particular destination in mind. Generally these are service walkers who provide some benefit to every house or other building they walk by. The city's roaming walkers are the nobleman, peddler, water bearer, healer, watchman, superintendent, athlete and clerk. Roaming walkers have no way of knowing where you want them to go, but you can guide them with @30Roadblocks. Roaming walkers cannot pass through Roadblocks. @PMany walkers, such as deliverymen carting goods to and from buildings, have a specific destination in mind, and are called destination walkers. These walkers include the food vendor, fleece vendor, oil vendor, arms vendor, wine vendor, horse trainer, chariot vendor, shepherd, goatherd, grower, tender, hunter, stonecutter, metallurgist, miner, lumberjack, artisan, soldier, immigrant, emigrant, vagrant and deliveryman. These walkers do not need you to guide them, so they pass right through Roadblocks. @PSome walkers have specific destinations in mind sometimes, but are roamers at other times. For example, an actor is a destination walker when going from the @16Drama School to the @17Theater, but is a roaming walker the rest of the time. @PMost walkers need roads to walk upon, but in order to do their jobs effectively some need to leave the road and walk across open terrain. These walkers are the goatherd, shepherd, grower, tender, hunter, stonecutter, metallurgist, miner, lumberjack, artisan, soldier, immigrant, emigrant, vagrant, deliveryman getting supplies, and superintendent putting out a fire.

message.title: Monsters
message.content: Monsters can cause significant trouble if they are your enemies, but can also help protect you if they are your friends. In all, there are sixteen monsters that you'll encounter in your travels through Greece and Atlantis. @PSometimes, monsters are in the service of @93gods, but other times they operate independently. Any hero can fight a monster, but each hero has a better chance against certain monsters than others. You can also use your military forces to battle monsters. The monsters you may encounter are: @L@LCYCLOPS @PThe hulking, one-eyed Cyclops uses a club as a weapon against his enemies, and he can also throw fire balls. If he is not working independently, his master is Zeus. Odysseus has the best chance of defeating the Cyclops. @L@LKRAKEN @PThe foul Kraken rises up from the sea to wreak havoc on you or for you. He uses his poisonous tentacles to attack and can also spit magic bolts. He usually works for Poseidon, but he can also work independently. Perseus is the Kraken's most feared foe. @L@LCERBERUS @PCerberus, the three-headed hound of the Underworld, uses his sharp bite to attack his enemies. He can also spit fireballs. If he's not working on his own, he will be in the service of Hades. Hercules has the best chance of defeating him. @L@LMEDUSA @PMedusa, the Gorgon, turns people to stone just by looking at them. She can also launch magic bolts from her eyes. If she's not causing trouble on her own, Medusa may be in service of Demeter. Perseus is skilled at doing battle with her. @L@LHYDRA @PThe many-headed Hydra attacks using his stinging bites and can also spit magic bolts. He usually takes his orders from Athena. Hercules has the best chance of vanquishing the beast. @L@LCALYDONIAN BOAR @PThe Calydonian Boar gores people with his tusks and will also spit fireballs. He most often works for Artemis. The hero Theseus has the upper hand against the Calydonian Boar. @L@LSCYLLA @PThe six-headed Scylla bites and launches magic bolts. She usually works for Apollo, and the hero Odysseus has the best chance of defeating her. @L@LDRAGON @PThe fierce Dragon breaths fire and bites when attacking. Generally, he takes orders from Ares. Jason has the best chance of defeating an angry Dragon. @L@LTALOS @PTalos, a bronze man fashioned by Hephaestus, fights using his sword and can also throw fireballs. He most often takes orders from his maker. He is most vulnerable to the hero Jason. @L@LHECTOR @PHector, the famous Trojan warrior, fights with a spear and can also shoot arrows from his bow. He generally does Aphrodite's bidding. Achilles has the best chance of defeating him. @L@LMINOTAUR @PThe half-man, half-bull Minotaur fights with a big axe and magic bolts. He most often works for Hermes. Theseus has the best chance of defeating him. @L@LMAENADS @PMaenads are women who have gone mad from indulging in Dionysus' cult of the vine. They fight with their bare hands and can also throw magic bolts. Achilles has the best chance of defeating them. @L@LSPHINX @PThe deadly Sphinx kills anyone who cannot answer her mysterious riddle correctly. She can also fire magic bolts. She does Hera's bidding, but will also work independently. Atalanta is clever enough to solve the riddle and kill the Sphinx. @L@LCHIMERA @PThe hideous Chimera is a mish-mash of different creatures, combined together into one ugly monster. She enjoys breathing fireballs to kill things. She works in the service of Atlas, but she'll also destroy things on her own. Bellerophon knows what to do to kill this monster. @L@LECHIDNA @PEchidna, the mother of some of the most dastardly monsters, always works on her own. Her magic bolts are the death of many. Bellerophon knows how to dispatch this monster. @L@LHARPIES @PThe Harpies are ravenous, winged monsters fond of firing magic bolts at unsuspecting people, animals and things. No one, not even a god, can control the Harpies, so they always work independently. Atalanta has the best chance of defeating them.

message.title: Gods
message.content: The Gods are everywhere. Sometimes, they are your friends and other times they are a little less than friendly. Here are the gods that you're bound to run into sooner or later, in order of their strength: @L@LZEUS @PZeus, the Ruler of Heaven, is the most powerful of all the gods. To find out how he can help you, read the entry on @62Zeus'&Stronghold. Zeus can also be a formidable enemy. He can curse many of your buildings, rendering them useless. He might even employ his Cyclops to wreak havoc on your city. @L@LPOSEIDON @PPoseidon, Ruler of the Sea, presides over buildings that depend on water. To see how he can help you, read the entry on @61Promontory&of&Poseidon. If Poseidon is your enemy, watch out for his Kraken. He can also curse your @38Fisheries and @38Urchin&Quays. In Atlantis, he can curse your @143Frigate&Wharves, and in Greece he can curse your @32Trireme&Wharves. And, just to make things even more interesting, he also interrupts sea trade. @L@LHADES @PHades is the Ruler of the Underworld, and can provide many benefits to your city should you choose to worship him. To see what benefits Hades can bring you if you worship him, click @58here. If Hades ever has a reason to invade your city, he'll curse your @43Foundries and @44Mints and will carry off all the walkers on the city's streets to the Underworld with him, depriving the city of their services until they can be replaced. Hades is also not above unleashing @92Cerberus on your city. @L@LHERA @PHera, Queen of Heaven, can be a wonderful friend if you choose to worship her. To find out how she expresses her friendship, read the entry on the @71Orchard&of&Hera. If Hera views you as a threat, then she is sure to cause trouble. One of her favorite tricks is to turn people into cattle. Continuing with the bovine theme, she also likes to curse @108Corrals. To top things off, she will also make everyone else in the world think less of you. She can also unleash the @92Sphinx on your city. @L@LDEMETER @PDemeter, Goddess of Fertility, rules over all fertile land. Click @56here to see how Demeter can benefit you if you decide to worship her. If she has a reason to cause you harm, she will render your farms infertile for a few months. She also might enlist @92Medusa to attack your city, and turn your citizens to stone. @L@LATHENA @PAthena, Goddess of Warriors, Crafts and Wisdom, can be a tremendous aid to cities that worship her. Click @55here to see how Athena can help your city, should you decide to worship her. If she is your enemy, Athena can cause a world of hurt for your city. She will weaken your city's @31defenses and curse your @35olive&trees. She could also unleash the @92Hydra upon your city, if she is truly out to get you. @L@LARTEMIS @PArtemis is the Goddess of Hunters. To see how she can help you if you choose to worship her, click @54here. If Artemis ever has reason to lash out at you, she will attack your city with an army of Amazons, curse your @69Hunting&Lodges, and restore any wolf packs in the area to full strength. She also could unleash the @92Calydonian&Boar to attack your city. @L@LAPOLLO @PApollo, the God of Prophecy and Healing, can bring many benefits your city, should you decide to worship him. Click @52here to find out what Apollo can do for you. If Apollo opposes you, he may invade your city, cursing your @50Infirmaries, and causing widespread plague. If you are ruling in Greece, he may also curse your cultural institutions, rendering them temporarily inactive. In Atlantis, he may curse your science buildings. He might also choose to unleash @92Scylla upon your city. @L@LATLAS @PAtlas, the Bearer of the World and First High King of Atlantis, can be extremely helpful if you choose to worship him. Click @70here to read about the benefits that Atlas can bring. If the strong god decides to be your enemy, then your construction-related industries are in trouble. He curses @131Black&Marble&Workshops and @42Masonry&Shops, making all the marble that they have on hand too brittle to use. Plus, no more marble can be quarried while the buildings are cursed. As if that weren't bad enough, he also curses @45Artisans'&Guilds. All the artisans mysteriously disappear, and they won't reappear until the curse is lifted. Plus, any citizens that he lays eyes upon will be turned to stone. If he doesn't feel like rampaging himself, Atlas will send @92Chimera to wreak havoc. @L@LARES @PAres, God of War, can be a powerful friend. Click @53here to see how Ares can help you, should you decide to worship him. If he is your enemy, Ares may invade your city with some of his fiercest warriors, or even unleash his @92Dragon to do you harm. @L@LHEPHAESTUS @PHephaestus, Smith of Heaven, can be a great benefit, when he feels warmly towards you. Click @59here to see how Hephaestus might help you, should you choose to worship him. If Hephaestus is your enemy, he may invade your city, setting buildings on fire, and crippling your @33Armories and @48Sculpture&Studios with his curse. He could also unleash his hideous man of bronze, @92Talos, to attack your city. @L@LAPHRODITE @PAphrodite, Goddess of the Tender Passions, can be a wonderful boon to any leader. Click @51here to see what good she can do for you. Aphrodite isn't always friendly, though. If her interests differ from yours, she may attack your city, and lead away all the walkers that provide benefits to your city. She even lures away a portion of the city's population. If she doesn't feel like punishing your city herself, she'll enlist @92Hector to attack. @L@LHERMES @PHermes, Messenger of the Gods, can be a wonderful friend. Click @60here to learn about the benefits Hermes can bring to your city. If he opposes you, however, Hermes may appear in your city, stealing money and disrupting trade. He might also unleash the @92Minotaur to cause trouble for you. @L@LDIONYSUS @PDionysus, God of the Vine, can be a fun guy to have as a friend. To find out just what he's willing to do for you, click @57here. If, however, Dionysus has reason to oppose you, and invades your city, he'll invite all your walkers to a party that they just can't resist. When the walkers leave your city, all the people and buildings that rely on their services will have to go without until they can be replaced. Dionysus will also curse your @36Grapevines, making grapes wither and die. Sometimes, Dionysus will unleash one or two @92Maenads, crazy women, on the city. @L@PImmortals often need help from a mortal to achieve a goal or retrieve a certain item. When a god needs your help, he or she may ask you to undertake a quest.

message.title: Heroes
message.content: Heroes roam the world in search of adventure, always looking to help out when they're needed. If one hears that you are facing a troublesome situation, the hero will probably be willing to help you out if you build a Hero's Hall. The Heroes you may encounter are @63Achilles, @64Hercules, @67Perseus, @68Theseus, @66Odysseus, @65Jason, @74Atalanta and @107Bellerophon. @PHeroes' services are in great demand throughout the world, so you can only build a Hero's Hall if you truly need the hero's help. Additionally, Hero's Halls are dismantled at the end of an episode, when the hero is no longer needed in the city. @PIf there is a monster in your city, the hero will fight the foul foe without orders from you. If you need to send a hero on a Quest to retrieve an item, click on the @75Overview Tab. You'll see the Quest listed. If the needed hero is in the city, a green light will appear next to the quest. Click on this light, select the appropriate hero on the 'Enlist Forces' panel, and click 'Dispatch' to send the hero on his or her way. You can also send a hero on a Quest by right clicking the appropriate Hero's Hall. If the hero is needed for a Quest, the quest will be listed there on a button. Click the button to send the Hero. Alternatively, you can click the Goals Button on the @86Control&Panel. Click on the button that appears next to the Quest on the Goals panel to send the hero.

message.title: Sheep and Goats
message.content: Sheep and goats live in meadows, where they are tended by shepherds and goatherds. @PTo begin raising sheep or goats, you first need herders. Shepherds, who tend sheep, come from a @39Carding&Shed. Goatherds come from a @40Dairy. Once the appropriate building is in place, you can begin raising livestock. Choose the animal you want to raise from the list that appears after you click on the Husbandry Tab's Herding button. Then, guide your cursor to a meadow, which is you can identify by its purple flowers. When you see a green ghost of the animal, you'll know you've chosen a good spot. Click to place a single sheep or goat. @PSheep and goats graze on a certain section of meadow until they've eaten all the edible vegetation on it. They then move to an adjacent area of meadow, provided it has vegetation for them to eat. All meadow vegetation eventually regrows. Because meadowland always remains fertile, you can still place farms and other husbandry structures on meadowland that has been consumed by animals. @PEspecially lucky sheep and goats will be sacrificed to the gods. Priests from a Sanctuary will come into the fields to retrieve the sheep and goats destined for greater glory.

message.title: Greek Soldiers
message.content: Citizen soldiers defend your city from invaders, and undertake your military campaigns abroad. They'll also try their best against monsters, and if you have enough of them, they just might succeed against these supernatural foes. @PThere are three types of soldiers in most Greek cities: rabble, hoplites and horsemen. Rabble come from @6common&housing. They wear no armor and use whatever they can find around them as weapons - they normally just throw rocks. To learn about the tactics they use, click @104here. Hoplites live in @7elite&housing and are the mainstay of the military. They are armored, carry spears, and fight in phalanxes. To learn how to maneuver your hoplites, click @105here. Finally, horsemen come from your most elite housing. For information on the tactics they use in battle, click @106here.

message.title: Hazard 'Go To' button
message.content: This slot on the @86Control&Panel is used to displays the Hazard 'Go To' button. When a catastrophe occurs in your city, clicking on the icon that appears in this slot takes you directly to the site of the problem. The icons that can appear here include @25Fire, @125Earthquake, @125Tidal&Wave, @125Landslide, @125Lava, @25Collapsed&Building and @126Blocked&Road.

message.title: Hygiene 'Go To' button
message.content: When your city experiences a significant @118hygiene problem, specifically an outbreak of plague, a button appears on the @86Control&Panel. Clicking on the button will bring you directly to ground zero of the plague.

message.title: Invasions 'Go To' button
message.content: When someone or something unfriendly invades your city, a button showing the invader appears on the Control Panel. Clicking on the button will bring you directly to the site of the problem. The types of invaders you may see here are enemy soldiers, monsters and unfriendly gods.

message.title: Arrivals 'Go To' button
message.content: When a hero arrives, your soldiers return home or a friendly god pays your city a visit, a button appears on the Control Panel. Clicking on the button takes you directly to the site of the arrival.

message.title: Wolf
message.content: Wolves prey on sheep, goats and cows that are not well-guarded. Shepherds are responsible for guarding sheep, goatherds look after goats, and bulls keep a watchful eye on cows. As long as your flocks and herds are vigilantly watched by shepherds, goatherds and bulls, wolves won't dare to make off with a sheep, goat or cow. But, if a wolf senses that an animal is vulnerable, he'll help himself to a tasty snack.

message.title: Boar
message.content: The wild boar can be hunted for food. To hunt the wild boar, you'll need to build a @69Hunting&Lodge. @PThe city's hunters are always very careful when stalking the wild boar. While they are tasty, they are also quite dangerous. Sometimes, a wild boar will take a hunter completely by surprise and attack him.

message.title: Trireme
message.content: The trireme is a powerful, quick and agile war vessel that helps to defend your city's shores, and can be used on some of your military campaigns abroad. @PTo move the Trireme, click on it and then click on the location you would like it to move to. To issue the Trireme orders, click on it, then use one of the orders buttons that will appear on the Control Panel. The orders are: @L@PCALL CREW TO SHIP/SEND CREW HOME. This order tells the ship's crew to come aboard, or to go home, depending on what they are currently doing. Keep in mind that while issuing the 'Send Crew Home' command returns the trireme to the wharf, and disbands its crew, it does not instruct the trireme's Wharf to repair the ship. If you want repairs performed on the ship, you'll have to issue the 'Carry Out Repairs' order. @L@PDEFEND LOCATION. When given this order, the ship's captain will hold his vessel in one location, and defend this location against any attackers that come near. @L@PATTACK ALL ENEMIES. When given this order, the ship's captain will aggressively seek out any enemy and attack it. The captain chooses which enemies to attack following a fixed set of priorities. First he'll seek out enemy transports which are currently carrying soldiers, to try to destroy them before their soldiers can reach land. If there are no such vessels, he looks for enemy warships to attack. Failing that, he'll order his trireme close to shore to attack any enemy soldiers that might have landed. Finally, if there are no enemy soldiers within his reach, he'll attack empty enemy transports. @L@PPATROL AREA. When given this order, the trireme's captain will patrol your city's waters, attacking any enemies he encounters. @L@PCARRY OUT REPAIRS. Clicking this button will send the trireme back to its Wharf to be repaired. If the ship is severely damaged, the trireme captain will take it upon himself to return to the Wharf for repairs. @L@PGO TO SHIP. Clicking this button centers your view on the trireme. @PYou cannot issue military commands while the game is @3paused. @PYou can select more than one trireme at a time and issue all of them the same orders. First, select a single trireme. When the cursor changes, click and drag your mouse. You'll notice that a box appears.
