Adjust this box by clicking and dragging your mouse so that the box contains all the triremes you want to select/ Then, let go of the mouse button and order away! @PAfter you've selected a fleet of triremes, you can assign a hotkey to the fleet. With the fleet selected, hold down the CTRL and press 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5. When you want to recall the fleet, simply press the ALT key plus the number you assigned it to.

message.title: Rabble Orders
message.content: Rabble come from the city's @6common&housing. Residents of common housing will begin fighting for the city as soon as they are living in houses that are at least at the Hovel level, and you have erected a Palace. @PTo select a company of Rabble, click on its standard or click on any of the men in the company. When you do, the @86Control&Panel will change, displaying the company's status. You'll see the company's name, along with the current morale of its men. If a company's morale dips too low, its men will refuse to fight. You'll also see a brief description of what the company is currently doing. @PAbove the status information is a series of buttons that you use to position the company and give it orders. The buttons you'll see are: @PGO TO COMPANY BUTTON. Clicking on the Go To Company button will center your view on the company's standard. @PROTATE COMPANY BUTTON. The Rotate Company button indicates which direction the company is currently facing. Clicking on the button will rotate the company. @PMUSTER COMPANY/SEND HOME BUTTON. The Muster Company/Send Home button lets you call your soldiers to arms (muster) or send them home, depending on which they are currently doing. @PUSE DEFENSIVE TACTICS. When Rabble have been told to defend an area, they hold their position and throw rocks at a distant enemy. If the enemy comes close to them, they find whatever primitive weapon they can and fight hand-to-hand. @PUSE OFFENSIVE TACTICS. When told to employ an offensive tactic, Rabble will attack any nearby enemy. @PEMPLOY SPECIAL TACTICS. The special tactic employed by Rabble is the skirmish. Rabble will throw rocks at a distant enemy. When that enemy comes too close, the Rabble will fall back and continue throwing rocks. If no enemies are nearby after the skirmish, the Rabble company returns to its standard. @PSHOW ALL FORCES. Clicking on the Magnifying Glass brings up a list of @84all&your&military&forces. From there, you can issue general instructions to all of your military forces. @PYou cannot issue military commands while the game is @3paused.

message.title: Hoplite Orders
message.content: @PHoplites come from the city's @7Mansions and @7Manors. @PTo select a phalanx of hoplites, click on its standard or click on any of the soldiers in the company. When you do, the Control Panel will change, displaying the company's status. You'll see the company's name, along with the current morale of its men. If a company's morale dips too low, its hoplites will refuse to fight. You'll also see a brief description of what the company is currently doing. @PAbove the status information is a series of buttons that you use to position the company and give it orders. The buttons you'll see are: @PGO TO COMPANY BUTTON. Clicking on the Go To Company button will center your view on the company's standard. @PROTATE COMPANY BUTTON. The Rotate Company button indicates which direction the company is currently facing. Clicking on the button will rotate the company. @PMUSTER COMPANY/SEND HOME BUTTON. The Muster Company/Send Home button lets you call your soldiers to arms and send them home. What the company is currently doing governs which command clicking this button will issue. If the company is already mustered, then clicking the button will send the men home. If the company is at home, then clicking the button will call the soldiers to arms. @PUSE DEFENSIVE TACTICS. When employing defensive tactics, hoplites will stand their ground, and attack anything that comes close to them with their spears. @PUSE OFFENSIVE TACTICS. When told to use offensive tactics, hoplites move together, attacking with their spears. @PEMPLOY SPECIAL TACTICS. The hoplites' special tactic is the wedge, which is good for breaking defensive formations. The soldiers organize themselves into a wedge shape to attack enemies. @PSHOW ALL FORCES. Clicking on the Magnifying Glass brings up a list of @84all&your&military&forces. From there, you can issue general instructions to your entire military. @PYou cannot issue military commands while the game is @3paused.

message.title: Horsemen Orders
message.content: @PHorsemen come from the city's @7Estates. @PTo select a company of horsemen, click on its standard or click on any of the soldiers in the company. When you do, the Control Panel will change, displaying the company's status. You'll see the company's name, along with the current morale of its men. If a company's morale dips too low, its men will refuse to fight. You'll also see a brief description of what the company is currently doing. @PAbove the status information is a series of buttons that you use to position the company and give it orders. The buttons you'll see are: @PGO TO COMPANY BUTTON. Clicking on the Go To Company button will center your view on the company's standard. @PROTATE COMPANY BUTTON. The Rotate Company button indicates which direction the company is currently facing. Clicking on the button will rotate the company. @PMUSTER COMPANY/SEND HOME BUTTON. The Muster Company/Send Home button lets you call your soldiers to arms or send them home, depending on which they are currently doing. @PUSE DEFENSIVE TACTICS. When horsemen have been told to defend an area, they remain on their horses and fight from horseback if an enemy comes within range. @PUSE OFFENSIVE TACTICS. When told to use offensive tactics, horsemen will charge the enemy in an attempt to break their formations, after which they'll stay and fight from horseback. The horsemen will charge as often as they can, but the horses do need to rest between attacks. If engaged directly, the horsemen will fight on horseback. @PEMPLOY SPECIAL TACTICS. The horsemen's special tactic is to harass. When told to harass, horsemen charge the enemy, fight for a little bit, and then retreat. When the horses are rested, they repeat the maneuver. @PSHOW ALL FORCES. Clicking on the Magnifying Glass brings up a list of @84all&your&military&forces. From there, you can issue general instructions to your entire military. @PYou cannot issue military commands while the game is @3paused.

message.title: Bellerophon's Hall
message.content: Bellerophon, the famed horseman, will come to your city if you build his Hero's Hall and outfit it with the required items. To find out what Bellerophon wants, right-click on the Hall. His demands will be listed there, and each one will be checked off as you meet it. @POnce you have met all of Bellerophon's requirements, you can bring the hero to your city by right-clicking his Hall and clicking the 'Summon Bellerophon' button. The hero will begin his journey to your city. @PYou may need Bellerophon's services to fulfill a @130quest. He is also the only hero who can defeat @92Echidna and @92Chimera. If you don't have any heroic duties for Bellerophon, you can also send him to battles abroad.

message.title: Corral
message.content: Build a Corral to raise cows for meat. Corrals must be built along a road. @POnce you build a Corral, you can place some cattle in a meadow. As you place the cattle, you'll notice that some of the cattle are bulls. Bulls watch over the herd, safeguarding the cows, and are not used for food. All cattle can be sacrificed to the gods. @PWhen a cow is old enough, a rancher herds it back to the Corral, where it is killed and carved into meat. As soon as enough meat is stored at the Corral, a deliveryman brings the food to a Granary, or to a trading facility if you are exporting the good. @PCorrals aren't just places of death. Calves are born at the Corral and, after they have been weaned, are put out to pasture with the other cattle. Because calves are born frequently, you don't need to worry about replacing slaughtered cattle yourself. You do, however, need to replace any cattle that priests take for sacrifice.

message.title: Orange Tenders' Lodge
message.content: To harvest the succulent oranges that grow on @149Orange&Trees, build an Orange Tenders' Lodge. Orange Tenders' Lodges must be built along a road. @POnce an Orange Tenders' Lodge has employees, it sends out tenders to take care of the trees. Tenders prune and maintain the trees to ensure that the oranges growing upon them are healthy. Harvest time arrives in November. The tenders will pick fruit for two months. After two months, any oranges that have not been picked will go to waste. @PAfter the oranges are harvested, the tenders bring the food back to the Orange Tenders' Lodge, where it is cleaned and prepared for storage. When enough oranges are ready, a deliveryman will bring them to a Granary or to a trading facility if you are exporting the food. Make sure that the Orange Tenders' Lodge is connected by a road to the oranges' destination. Otherwise, the deliveryman will get stuck.

message.title: Sanctuary Construction
message.content: To build a Sanctuary, you must first have marble stored in the city. Each Sanctuary requires a different amount of marble in order to place its base and steps. @PTo build a Sanctuary, choose the Mythology Tab and click on the Sanctuaries button. Choose the Sanctuary you want to build from the list, and a red footprint will appear. Move the red footprint to the spot where you want to build the Sanctuary. If you want to rotate the footprint, press the 'r' key. When you've positioned the Sanctuary where you want it, and when the footprint turns green, click to place it. @PPressing the 'm' key when placing a Sanctuary can also be helpful, because it will freeze the Sanctuary's footprint, and allow you to move the mouse to scroll your view, and make sure the Sanctuary is placed where you want it. Provided the footprint is green, click to place the Sanctuary. Or, press 'm' again to unfreeze the footprint and look for a better location. There can be no more than four Sanctuaries in any city. Some cities can support even fewer Sanctuaries, so choose which you want to build carefully. If you find yourself in need of a different Sanctuary, but the city cannot support any additional Sanctuaries, you'll have to demolish an existing Sanctuary to build a new one. @PIn order for Sanctuary construction to begin, you need artisans from an @45Artisans'&Guild. You also must make sure that the Sanctuary is connected by road to the Artisans' Guild, and to the storage facility from which it will draw materials for its construction. Artisans will wait at the construction site for a delivery of supplies, either marble, wood or sculpture. If the requisite construction materials are available in a Storehouse, @12Pier or @11Trading&Post, the Storage building's oxcart will bring the material to the construction site. When the material arrives, the artisans will use it to construct the Sanctuary. @PIf you would like to halt construction on a Sanctuary, right-click the Sanctuary and click the 'Halt Sanctuary Construction' button. The artisans will finish up their current tasks and then go home or look for another construction project that needs their services. To resume construction, right-click the Sanctuary and click the 'Resume Sanctuary Construction' button. @PTo find out about the benefits a particular Sanctuary will bring, click on the desired god: @62Zeus, @61Poseidon, @58Hades, @71Hera, @56Demeter, @55Athena, @52Apollo, @54Artemis, @70Atlas, @53Ares, @59Hephaestus, @51Aphrodite, @60Hermes or @57Dionysus

message.title: Diplomacy and the World
message.content: Greece and Atlantis are very active places, and leaders of its city-states are always interacting with each other. The quality of the relationships you have with other cities and leaders can have direct consequences for your own city. Most of the rules of world etiquette apply to both Greece and Atlantis. Atlantis, however, has some special rules that apply only to Atlantean rulers. Click @148here for more details. @L@LCITY TYPES @PSeveral different types of relationships can form between you and other leaders. They are: @L@PALLIES. Allies are your peers and equals. They expect to be treated with respect and are more than willing to help you out if you treat them well. Of course, they won't hesitate to turn their backs on you if you betray their trust in you, or fail to help them when they need it. Allies are normally very interested in conducting trade with you. @L@PRIVALS. Rivals, though not necessarily openly hostile, view you as a competitor, and are rarely interested in helping you at all. If a rival has something you need or want, asking him nicely isn't going to do you any good. In such cases, your only options are to demand what you need, raid his city, or even attempt to conquer it. Rarely, a rival will respond to a normal request if you have done so much for him that he thinks extremely highly of you. Don't be surprised if rival leader try to make excessive demands of you. Whether you meet these demands or not is entirely up to you. Of course, if you fail to meet a rival leader's demands, he is likely to become upset. @PIf a rival leader attacks and conquers your city, he has a right to demand annual @129tribute from then on. If you refuse to pay tribute, the rival leader is likely to attack you for this. Conquering the rival leader's city in return, or defeating his army on your own soil are the only ways you can break free of this obligation. If the same rival defeats you twice on your own soil, the episode is over. @L@PVASSALS. When you attack and successfully conquer another city, it becomes your vassal, and must pay you annual @129tribute from then on. Your vassals will happily conduct trade with you, and try their best to do everything you ask of them. If you push a vassal too hard, though, he may become fed up, and lead his city to rebel against your lordship. @L@PCOLONIES. Colonies you establish remain extremely loyal to you. Your colony leaders regard themselves as your governors, and will do everything in their power to satisfy your needs. Like vassals, colonies are your subjects, and have an obligation to pay @129tribute annually. Colony leaders are happy to conduct trade with your city, and in many cases rely on your support. Of course, even leaders of loyal colonies have their limits. If you push them too far, they just might rebel against you. @L@PDISTANT CITIES. Distant cities do not involve themselves in political activity, but do conduct trade with you when it is beneficial to them. @L@PTHE PARENT CITY. When you're personally establishing a colony, one of your trusted governors will administer the parent city on your behalf. @L@PINACTIVE CITIES. Some cities will become inactive from time to time, for various reasons. Inactive cities are marked with a small bronze disc on the World Map, but you cannot interact with them in any way. @L@LHOW OTHER LEADERS FEEL TOWARD YOU @PThe leaders of other cities form opinions of you based on their interactions with you in the past. When you first begin interacting with the leader of another city, he or she doesn't really have an opinion of you. As other leaders learn more about you, they will begin to form ideas about you and will adjust their actions accordingly. So, if you do things to please another leader, like giving a gift of a much needed item, or fulfilling his or her request, the leader will be predisposed to do nice things for you. Of course, if you greet another city with an attack, its leader won't think too highly of you. @PTo learn how a given leader feels toward you, go to the World Map by clicking the @88View&World&button on the Control Panel. Select a city by clicking on it on the World Map, and its name will appear in the panel on the right. You'll also see a button that describes how its leader currently feels about you. Below the leader's name is an open scroll. Click on it, and you'll see a list of all your interactions with this leader, and even some interactions you've had with other leaders, that have contributed to the selected leader's current opinion of you. @PTo find out how a leader might react to you given his current opinion of you, click on the Attitude button, located just below the Scroll button. You'll see a panel giving pointers on how to improve or maintain your standing with the given leader. @L@LACTIONS @PTo initiate activity with another city, use the buttons that appear at the bottom of the panel. If a particular option isn't available to you, the button will be grayed out. The buttons you will see are: @L@PMAKE REQUEST/DEMAND. The types of requests or demands you can make of another leader depends upon what type of relationship you have with his or her city, and the leader's current attitude toward you. Clicking on the request/demand button will display your choices. @PIf you have an average to good relationship with an ally, you can request goods and food from him or her. If an ally thinks highly of you, his or her own citizens' will be willing to risk their lives on your behalf. You'll be able to request that the leader send military forces to defend your city. If an ally thinks very highly of you, he or she will even send soldiers to attack and conquer another city on your behalf. @PRival leaders are unwilling to fulfill simple requests for food and goods, unless your relationship with them is excellent. Normally it won't be, so if you need food or goods from a rival you'll have to demand it. If the rival leader feels you have the military might to back up your threat, he or she will probably fulfill your demands. @PAs loyal, obedient subjects, your vassals and colonies will respond to your requests for goods and food even if they aren't particularly fond of you. If your relationship with them is good, they'll even send soldiers to attack another city on your behalf. They'll also send soldiers to help you defend your city, as long as your relationship with them is good. Be aware, though, that if their opinion of you sinks too low, they won't entertain any requests from you at all. @L@PFULFILL REQUEST. Click on this button to fulfill the selected city's outstanding request. A panel listing the outstanding requests from the city's leader will appear when you click this button. Choose the request you would like to fulfill, and click the Dispatch button to send the requested items. If the outstanding request is for military forces, a panel listing the forces you can enlist will appear. You'll also see the action that the requesting leader wants your forces to take. If you want to send forces, select the companies, ships, or even heroes you want to send by clicking on them, then click the Dispatch button. You cannot send rabble on military campaigns abroad, and you cannot use forced loaned to you from another city to fulfill requests. @L@PGIVE GIFT. Giving gifts can be a good way to mend poor relationships. Some gifts, however, are more appreciated than others. Cash is always appreciated, though a leader whose city has a very weak economy will appreciate a gift of cash more than a leader whose city is economically powerful. All leaders appreciate gifts of items their city needs. Gifts of items a city doesn't need aren't appreciated much. You can tell what a city needs by clicking on it. If the city trades with you, the items it needs, if any, are the items it imports. If the city isn't trading with you, the items it needs will appear in the panel below the Attitude button. @PGifts are most appreciated if they are not given too often. If you give a city too many gifts in a short amount of time, its leader will appreciate them less and less, and may even refuse to accept the gift. @L@PRAID. Raiding cities, especially rivals, is a very good way to get things you need without having to pay for them. To do this, click the Raid button, then use the panel presented to enlist forces to conduct the raid. Click on the Select Plunder button to choose which item you want the raiding party to steal from the targeted city. When you're done setting up the raid, click the Dispatch button to send the raiders on their way. @PCONQUER CITY/QUELL REBELLION. Click on this button to attempt to conquer the selected city or, in the case of a vassal or colony, to quell a rebellion. When you click this button, a panel will appear allowing you to select which of your forces you would like to enlist for the assault. Rabble can never be sent on military campaigns abroad. When attacking a rival, some of your allies may even be willing to provide support, joining in the assault with you. Only one ally will join you at a time, though. Select the forces you wish to enlist, then click the Dispatch button. When the fighting is over, a message will notify you of the results. If you successfully conquer an ally or rival, it will become your vassal, and start paying you tribute. If you quell a rebellion, the vassal or colony will resume any tribute payments its leader was making. @PClick here for information on @117Trade with other cities.

message.title: Pan-Hellenic Games
message.content: Every year, Pan-Hellenic Games are held in Greece, and contestants from all over the land gather to see who is the best. There are four Games in all: the Isthmian, Nemean, Pythian and Olympian. The Isthmian Games test a philosopher's wit and intelligence. The more @14Podiums and @13Colleges you have, the better your philosophers' chances are of faring well in the Isthmian games. The Nemean Games are a showcase for Greece's athletes and competitors. Remember to build plenty of @15Gymnasiums and a @18Stadium to give your contestants the best chance of winning these Games. Actors compete in the Pythian Games, and having plenty of @16Drama&Schools and @17Theaters in your city will help your actors to victory. Finally, the Olympian Games are a test to see which city is the greatest center of overall culture. Actors, philosophers, athletes and competitors all compete in the Olympian Games. @PWinning any of the Pan-Hellenic Games is beneficial. Other city leaders can't help but be impressed by this, and their opinions of you will increase. You'll also be able to honor your contestants' achievements by building a @23Commemorative&Monument. And, if you win the Olympian Games, your city will have the honor of hosting its own Games in four years, as long as there is a functioning Stadium to host the event. Other leaders will think more favorably of you when you host your own games, regardless of how your contestants do in them.

message.title: Terrain Types
message.content: There are several different types of terrain in the Greek world, and some of them have special qualities. @L@PGRASSLAND. You can build most buildings on grassland, but it is not fertile enough to support farms or livestock. People can walk over grassland. @PMEADOW. Meadowland is marked by purple tufts. It is the only land fertile enough to support all types of farm and orchard crops, and is the only land with enough natural vegetation to support livestock. People can walk over the meadow without any problem. @PFOREST. Forests can be harvested by lumberjacks from a @41Timber&Mill. You can also clear a forest by clicking the @86Clear&button and clicking on the forest, or on individual trees. Once trees are cleared, however, they will never regrow. @PMARSH. Nothing can be built upon the murky marsh. People can pass through it, but the ground is too soft to support buildings, but people can walk on it. @PBEACH. Sandy beaches abut some areas of water. The sands shift far too much to support buildings. @PROCK. Ordinary rock cannot be built upon, and people have difficulty walking across it. They can only pass through where there are small passes or stairways. @PORE-BEARING ROCK. You'll see metallic nuggets embedded in some rocks. Rocks with the copper nuggets contain copper ore, which can be smelted to create bronze at a @43Foundry. Rocks with silver nuggets contain silver ore, which could be smelted and struck into coins called drachmas, at a @44Mint. Rocks with red nuggets contain orichalc ore, which is converted to orichalc at a @127Refinery. @PQUARRY. There are two types of quarry: black marble quarry and white marble quarry. If you see a flat, grayish-white surface, stonecutters from a @42Masonry&Shop will be able to hew white marble. Flat, dark gray rocks indicate the presence of black marble, which can be quarried by stonecutters from a @131Black&Marble&Workshop. @PWATER. Sea urchins and edible fish dwell in some bodies of water. Some structures must be built along the water's edge. Specifically, these structures are the @12Pier, @28Water&Crossing, @38Urchin&Quay, @38Fishery, @32Trireme&Wharf and @143Frigate&Wharf.

message.title: Industry
message.content: The city's industries produce goods for the city's residents, and materials needed for the @110construction&of&Sanctuaries. @PThere are two main types of industry: raw materials producers and workshops. The raw materials producers are the @43Foundry, @44Mint, @127Refinery, @42Masonry&Shop, @131Black&Marble&Workshop and @41Timber&Mill. Grapes grown on a @36Grapevine and olives grown on an @35Olive&Tree are raw materials of sorts, because they are used by workshops to make wine and olive oil respectively. The industrial workshops are the @47Winery, @46Olive&Press and @48Sculpture&Studio. Click on any of the above links to read about a particular industry. @PAll industries share a few things in common. All must have access to a road so that they can access the city's labor pool. All of them also operate much more efficiently when they fully staffed with workers. An understaffed industry will still function, but it will turn out its product at a much slower rate. @PYour city's road system is important if industries are to run smoothly. All your industries must be connected by a road to a building that can receive their final products. This building can be a @10Storehouse or, if you are exporting the product, a @12Pier or @11Trading&Post. Raw materials producers can also take their supplies directly to a workshop that needs them. @PA workshop must not only have access to a storage facility that can receive its final product, but it must also be connected to a source of the raw material it requires. A workshop can connected to the raw materials producer on which it depends directly, by a road, or it can be connected to a Storehouse that is storing the raw material it needs. The closer the workshop is to its source of raw materials, the more efficient production will be. @PClick on the @78Industry&Tab for more information on the city's industries.

message.title: Migration and Population
message.content: Your city won't be able to operate at all without people. You need commoners to fill jobs that keep the city's services running, to man the oars of your ships, and to defend the city as mobs of @104rabble if necessary. You need the elite warrior class to fight for you as @105hoplites and @106horsemen. @PWhen a city is new, immigrants generally come willingly, looking for a better life. As your city becomes established, would-be immigrants will expect certain things from your city, or else they won't come. If your city fails to meet the needs of its current residents, these people will move out to look for a better situation. @PTo keep residents in your city and to keep new immigrants coming, make sure you provide basic services. If there isn't enough food in the city to feed its current population, new immigrants will be discouraged from coming, and some of the city's current residents might leave. High unemployment, low wages and high taxes are all deterrents to immigration. When you go into debt, you cannot pay your workers. If you are in debt for too long, immigrants will not want to come to your city. Excessive military service, especially when unnecessary, will lower your popularity and hinder immigration. If you have a history of charging high taxes, paying low wages or requiring a lot of unnecessary military service, or if you have a history of prolonged debt, immigrants will be reluctant to come to your city. Their memories are long, and they will fear that you might return to your old, stingy ways. Finally, even if people wish to come to your city, they won't be able to if the city lacks vacant housing, because they will have nowhere to live. The same problems that limit immigration can also cause emigration. @PIn addition to immigration and emigration, your city's population grows and shrinks due to births and deaths. In cities with good @118hygiene practices, more babies will be born, and fewer deaths will occur, and your population will grow as a result. If, however, hygiene is poor in your city, deaths could outnumber births, and your population will likely shrink. @PClick on the @76Population&Tab for more information on the city's residents.

message.title: Food Production
message.content: Keeping your population fed is extremely important, so planning efficient farms and other food-producing structures, or acquiring food from other cities, is vital. @PAll your @29Farms, @38Urchin&Quays, @38Fisheries, @40Dairies, @109Orange&Tenders'&Lodges, @108Corrals and @69Hunting&Lodges must have access to a road so that they can access the city's pool of workers. In addition, they are at their most efficient when they are fully staffed. If understaffed, they will still produce food, but at a slower rate than usual. In addition, all of these buildings need to be connected by road to a @9Granary or, if you are exporting food, to the appropriate @11Trading&Post or @12Pier. @PTo increase the efficiency of Hunting Lodges, Urchin Quays and Fisheries, place them as close as possible to their prey. The shorter the distance the hunter, urchin gatherer or fishing boat has to travel, the quicker it will return with food. The closer a corral is to the herd of cattle, the more efficient it will be, too. @PGood land management is key to planning your Farming system. Your Farms have to share the city's usable meadowland with @36Grapevines, @35Olive&Trees, @95Sheep, @95Goats and @152Cattle, and finding room for everything can be tricky if you have limited meadowland. Remember that only one portion of a Farm needs to be on meadowland for the farm to be productive. @PMaking sure that your people get the food produced or imported by your city is the job of your @128distribution&system. @More information on food production can be found by clicking on the @77Husbandry&Tab.

message.title: Trade
message.content: Trade with other cities can be extremely profitable. It can also help you provide the goods that your people can't produce for themselves. @PEach @11Trading&Post and @12Pier is dedicated to a particular city. To open trade with another city, simply build the Trading Post or Pier associated with it. Then, right-click on the building to tell it how much you want to import or export. @PTo import an item, click the button next to the good you want to import until it reads 'Buying'. Then, tell the trading facility how much of the good you want to import by setting a stock limit. Each time a trader visits, the trading facility will buy the good until the stock limit is reached, as long as it has sufficient storage space, and as long as the trader has enough goods to sell. @PTo export an item, click the button next to the item you want to export until it reads 'Selling'. Then, set the stock limit. The trading facility uses the stock limit as a guide to how much of the exported item it should keep on hand at all times, should a trader visit to make a purchase. The trading facility will send out a deliveryman to get the item for export, until it is storing the limit you've specified. @PTo see what a city trades before building its trading facility, click the @88View&World&button. When the World Map appears, click on the city with which you'd like to trade. The goods that it can import and export will be displayed on the panel on the right. In addition, you'll see how much of each good the city can trade in a year. If you have already built the city's trade facility, you can give trade instructions by clicking on the Orders button. @PWhen giving trade instructions, keep the needs of your citizens in mind. Deliverymen place a high priority on bringing exportable goods to trading facilities. They will always bring exportable goods to a trading facility before delivering them to the city's Storehouses or Granaries. If you export too much, your people might end up having to go without. If you notice that your citizens are running out of a good you are exporting, consider decreasing the trade facility's stock limit for the exported good. Remember that vendors from an @8Agora cannot procure goods intended for export, currently stored in a trade facility set to 'Selling'. @PKeep an eye on your treasury when you are importing goods. The cost of importing items can add up quickly, so make sure you are importing only as much as your city needs. @PPiers and Trading Posts employ deliverymen to help facilitate trade. With imports, deliverymen seek to distribute the goods as soon as they are dropped off. Normally he'll deliver imported goods to the nearest Storehouse that is accepting the item, but if it's a raw material, the deliveryman will look for a workshop that needs it. If he can't find one, he'll take the goods to a Storehouse. If the import is a food, the deliveryman will transport it to a @9Granary. Make sure the trading facility is connected by a road to the imported goods' final destinations. The quicker a deliveryman can move goods out of the trading facility, the more you'll be able to import. @PClick on the @79Distribution&Tab for more information on trade.

message.title: Hygiene
message.content: Wise leaders encourage their citizens to adopt good hygiene practices. Poor hygiene practices can lead to plague, which can lead to the deaths of your hard-working and elite citizens alike. @PTo keep hygiene practices sound, make sure all your people are able to eat regularly, and are visited regularly by a healer from an @50Infirmary. If you fail to provide these things, hygiene will fall, and plague could break out. @PWhen a home is infected with plague, some of its citizens unfortunately die. The remaining people of the household will concentrate on getting healthy for the next two months, so no new people can move into an infected house during this time. Once the two months have passed, though, the residents of the infected house will welcome new residents. @PFor more information on the city's hygiene practices, click the @80Hygiene&and&Safety&Tab

message.title: Appeal
message.content: Appeal is a measure of the beauty of a particular location. People who live in areas of high appeal appreciate their surroundings and pay more in @120taxes. @PMost buildings have an effect on the appeal of the surrounding area. Buildings that people want to live near, such as Sanctuaries, the @24Palace and @17Theaters, tend to increase an area's appeal. @85Aesthetic&Structures are specifically designed to raise an area's appeal. Noisy or foul-smelling buildings, like Farms, industries, @16Drama&Schools and @13Colleges, are a detriment to an area's appeal. Boulevards and Avenues increase the appeal of any area. @PLook at an area's @5roads for an indication of its appeal. The nicer an area, the nicer the roads will be. You can also click on the 'See Appeal' button on the @85Aesthetics&Tab to gauge an area's attractiveness. How appealing an area is has no effect on your city's industries, but makes a big difference in your city's residential areas.

message.title: Money and Taxes
message.content: In order to be a successful leader, you must be able to make money. In fact, if you are in debt too long, causing your workers to go without pay, they will even forcibly remove you from your position. @PYou have several sources of income, the two main sources being taxation and money earned from @117exports. You also might be able to mint your own coins if there are any deposits of @44silver&ore in and around your city. In Atlantis, you can earn revenue from a thrilling @139Hippodrome. Furthermore, other leaders may have an obligation to pay you annual tributes in cash, or sometimes give you gifts of money. You can also ask other leaders for money. There are, of course, several ways to spend money, too. The key to turning a profit is to keep expenses as low as possible while taking full advantage of all your sources of income. @L@LTAXES @PTo collect taxes, you need a functioning @24Palace as well as some @26Tax&Offices. Clerks from the Tax Office will circulate through the streets, collecting money from the houses they pass. @PTo set a tax rate, select the @81Administration&Tab. You'll see the city's current tax rate displayed. Use the scroll buttons to adjust the tax rate up or down. You have several choices of tax rate to levy, anywhere from no tax at all to an outrageous tax rate. The higher you set taxes, however, the less popular you will be among your citizens. Of course, if you set a low tax rate, your popularity will increase. As you adjust the tax rate, you'll see how much money the new rate will bring in for the year. You can also set the tax rate by right-clicking on a Tax Office. @PResidents of @7elite&housing pay more in taxes than those who live in @6common&housing. Also, those who live in areas of high @119appeal pay more taxes than those that live in areas of low appeal. Those who live in beautiful surroundings appreciate the work the city has put into the area and are willing to pay more. @PTo maximize your tax receipts, make sure as many of your citizens as possible are registered for the tax. To see which areas of the city might not be paying their fair share, select the Administration Tab and click on the 'See Taxes' button. You'll see the city's clerks going about their duties. You'll also see columns and stacks of coins in front of the city's housing. The higher the column, the more recently the house has been visited by a clerk. The stack of coins indicates how much money the household has paid in taxes for the year so far. You might want to build more Tax Offices in any areas containing houses that are not regularly visited by a clerk. @L@LEXPORTS @PProfits from exports tend to be the most lucrative source of income for a city. Generally you'll earn more exporting manufactured goods than raw materials. Some raw materials can be quite valuable, however. To see which goods fetch the highest prices, select the @79Distribution&Tab and click on the Magnifying Glass button. You'll see the prices for goods in the screen that pops up. @L@LKEEPING COSTS DOWN @PWhen trying to control costs, keep the following in mind: @L@PBUILD ONLY WHAT YOU NEED, ONLY WHEN YOU NEED IT. When you're just beginning to build a city, it can be very tempting to place building after building to fill the empty terrain. Resist this temptation. Building lots of buildings quickly before you've established any sources of income can be a surefire way of going into debt. Not only do the buildings cost money to build, but you also have to pay the wages of any employees the building requires. Furthermore, if you don't have all the workers you need, you might find yourself building more houses to draw more workers to the city. Those houses will cost money, and you'll have to pay even more wages to the new workers that arrive. @L@PKEEP THE COST OF IMPORTS DOWN BY IMPORTING RAW MATERIALS. Generally, raw materials cost much less to import than manufactured goods. When you can, import the appropriate raw material and build a workshop that can manufacture the finished good from it. @L@PBE CAREFUL NOT TO IMPORT MORE THAN YOU NEED. Import costs can spiral out of control if you do not keep a close watch on them. Trading facilities only import up to the stock limit you set, but they only take into consideration the amount of the imported item currently stored in the trading facility. And, as soon as an imported item is dropped off at a trading facility, deliverymen try to take the good elsewhere. So, even though you might not have any of the imported good stored in the trading facility, you might have plenty stored in the city's Storehouses. If you do, you might want to stop buying goods for awhile. @L@LIF YOU STILL CAN'T KEEP YOUR CITY SOLVENT, by all means, ask other cities for money. For more on how to ask for money, click @111here.

message.title: Employment
message.content: Your city won't run very well at all if it doesn't have any workers. Workers live in the city's @6common&housing, but not all of the residents of a common house work. Some stay home because they are too young or too old to work, and others stay home simply because they can. @PThere are two employment problems you may experience: unemployment and worker shortage. @L@PUNEMPLOYMENT. A high unemployment rate can cause your citizens to become quite frustrated with you. If you have unemployment problems, you can try to solve them by creating new jobs. This could be your chance to give a boost to certain sectors of your city that might be lacking. For example, if you are deficient in one type of cultural pursuit, unemployment can give you the chance to solve the problem. Before you begin constructing new buildings to create more jobs, make sure you can afford the cost of the building plus the expense of employing the workers. You don't want to replace your unemployment problem with a debt problem. @PAnother way to solve an unemployment problem is to encourage emigration by demolishing common housing. Though this measure is a little Draconian, it is effective. @L@PWORKER SHORTAGE. A worker shortage can be a very serious problem. Buildings that do not have a full staff of workers do not run efficiently. The best ways to solve a worker shortage problem are to either get rid of some building that employ workers, or to draw more people to the city. @PThere are a few things you can do to ease the effects of a worker shortage. You can assign a high priority to certain labor sectors of the city, to ensure that your most important services continue uninterrupted. To assign priorities to the various labor sectors in the city, choose the @78Industry&Tab and click on the Magnifying Glass button. In the screen that appears, you'll see listed all of the different employment sectors in your city. Set a priority level for each by using the scroll buttons to the left. In the case of a labor shortage, the sectors that you designate as a high priority will be staffed first. Sectors with a low priority will be last in line to receive workers. If you don't currently have enough workers to staff all buildings that need them, as you change priorities you'll probably see the number of workers assigned to a sector change. @PYou can also completely shut down particular industries. Workers previously employed by an industry that has been shut down will find work elsewhere. This can be a good temporary fix to a worker shortage problem. @PAlso, remember that @32Trireme&Wharves and @143Frigate&Wharves require a significant number of people in order to function. If you are experiencing a worker shortage, consider sending the Wharf's crew home so that they can find jobs in other parts of the city. You can send the crews of all of your Wharves home by choosing the @84Military&Tab and clicking on the 'All Crewed' button so that it reads 'Crew Ships'. You can also send the crew of a particular ship home. Click on the Magnifying Glass button in the Military Tab. In the screen that appears, click on the Status button of the ship whose crew you want to send home. Or, click on the individual vessel itself then click the orders button for 'send crew home.'

message.title: Popularity
message.content: Many of the things you'll have to do as leader of a city-state can make you unpopular among your people. The people in your city watch your actions very closely and are quick to form opinions of you. If their opinion of you sinks to low levels, they might start causing trouble in your city. At the very least, they'll tell others how much of an ogre you are and discourage new immigrants from coming to your city. Of course, if you are very popular amongst your people, they'll be less inclined to cause trouble, and they'll tell all their friends in other lands how great it is to live in your city. @PSeveral factors affect your popularity. High taxes, low wages, and high unemployment are all certain to make you less popular. If you are in debt for a prolonged period of time - which means that workers haven't been paid - your popularity could plummet. Your citizen soldiers also do not like to be called to arms too much, especially when it is unnecessary. Lack of food also angers people. Of course, you can make your people quite happy if you pay them well and charge a low tax rate. They will also like you if you make sure that they are always well-fed and that most of them have jobs to go to. @PIn Atlantis, @139Hippodromes also affect your popularity. Having a thriving Hippodrome in your city increases your popularity with your people - to a point. If your Hippodrome is extremely large, your people will begin to resent having to share their city with dirty, dusty horses and jockeys of questionable repute. Your popularity with them will decline. To find out how your citizens are feeling about the races, right-click on the Hippodrome.

message.title: Unrest
message.content: Unrest in the city occurs when conditions aren't satisfactory to some of your residents. Residents of lower-quality houses may turn to a life of crime if you fail to provide jobs or adequate food. They also become unhappy if they aren't paid well, if they have to pay too much in taxes or if you call them to arms too much. They really don't like it when the city goes into debt, because this means they might not be paid. @PWhen unrest is too high, disgruntled citizens and outlaws will hit the streets, potentially causing a lot of trouble. As an immediate solution, watchmen from a @27Watchpost can help to keep unrest in check. As they pass by housing, they reduce the chance that an angry outlaw or disgruntled citizen will emerge. To see which areas are most likely to produce an outlaw, choose the @80Hygiene&and&Safety&Tab and click on the 'See Unrest' button. The higher the column in front of the house, the more likely it is that one of its residents will turn to a life of crime. @PUnrest can result in four different types of unsavory citizen. The disgruntled citizen wanders the city's streets, complaining to whomever comes close enough to hear him. He won't cause any damage, but he is still a pest. The mugger is more violent than the disgruntled citizen. He wanders the city, attacking and killing people for whatever possessions they might have. The thief, dissatisfied with his lot in life, steals things from the city's @7elite&housing. Finally, the vandal, by far the most angry of the outlaws, will completely destroy an elite home. @PRight-click on any of these unhappy people to find out just what is making them mad. If a nobleman or watchman happens upon an outlaw, he will see to it that the outlaw is removed from the streets.

message.title: Invasions and Combat
message.content: Sooner or later, your city will be invaded by an enemy. Foreign enemies include the Persians, Centaurs, Amazons, Oceanids, Mayans and Egyptians. Some of these enemies come to your city by boat, others come over land, and some could even launch a two-pronged attack, coming to your city by land and sea. The Oceanids approach your city in a very clever way: they swim under water. You can tell that they are approaching by the air bubbles that rise to the surface. Your own boats can do nothing to attack the Oceanids while they are swimming to your city. Only the Kraken can dive to the depths necessary to stop the Oceanids from coming to shore. @PYou have several ways of handling attacks, and not all of them involve combat. @L@PBRIBERY. When an enemy invades, you may be able to bribe the attacking army. The larger the invading army, the more expensive it will be to buy them off. It is a great victory for your city when your bribery attempt succeeds, because it means that your city has been saved without loss of life. @L@PSURRENDER. You can also, of course, surrender to the invader. If you do, your city will be conquered, and you will have to start paying tribute to the conqueror. On the bright side, however, your city won't suffer any casualties. @L@PFIGHT. Of course, you can choose to fight the enemy. If you would rather your generals run the battle, turn on Auto-Defend, by clicking the small helmet icon on the @84Military&Tab. With Auto-defend off, you must command your own soldiers and boats. Click on the following links to learn about the orders you can give to your @104rabble, @105hoplites, @106horsemen, and @103triremes. If Atlantis is your domain, click on the following links to learn about the orders you can give to your @145archers, @146spearmen, @147charioteers and @144frigates. @POnce your companies are in the field, you can select one company at a time to give it orders. You can also select more than one company and issue them all the same order at one time. To select more than one company, first select one of them. Then, hold down the mouse button and drag a box around all the companies you wish to select. You can remove individual companies from the selection by shift-clicking on them. Then, issue an order, and all of the selected companies will carry it out. @L@PCombat can also take place outside your city. Your generals always handle combat abroad. For more information on military campaigns abroad, see the entry on @111Diplomacy&and&the&World.

message.title: Disasters
message.content: Greece and Atlantis can be unforgiving lands, where disasters can strike your city, ruining portions of the terrain. Sometimes these disasters are initiated by gods, but they can also happen for no discernible reason. The disasters your cities may experience are landslides, earthquakes, tidal waves and lava. @PWhen the ground is unsettled, a landslide can occur. Massive boulders come cascading out of the mountains and spread across the landscape. These rocks demolish anything in their paths. Once they settle, they cannot be cleared away and you cannot build anything on them. @PEarthquakes shatter the land, leaving it cracked and broken. Any buildings that were standing on the land affected by the earthquake will be destroyed. The cracks left behind by an earthquake are permanent, so reusing the land becomes challenging. You can build roads across these cracks; road crews automatically erect a small bridge in such circumstances. @PTidal waves assault the land and knock down anything in their path. When the wave ebbs, you can build on the land again. Sometimes, though, the tide doesn't recede, and the coastline is changed forever. @PLava erupts from the ground and burns down the structures it flows over. When the lava cools, it leaves the land burnt and useless. @PIf a city is truly unfortunate, parts of the land may break off and sink into the ocean. All that was on the land is lost, and the coastline will change shape.

message.title: Road to the World
message.content: A road connects every city in Atlantis and Greece to the rest of the world. Sometimes, the road runs completely through the city, and other times it is marked by only a small road at the entrance and exit to your city. You can destroy and rebuild this road however you want. But, if you ever block the entry and exit point of the original road with buildings or other obstructions, you will be cut off from the rest of World, and land trade and immigration will cease. If you cut off the Road to the World, you'll be notified by a message. On the message is a button you can click to go directly to the site of the problem. Once you restore access to the world by removing the obstruction, land trade and immigration will resume. If necessary, superintendents will clear the obstruction.

message.title: Refinery
message.content: Metallurgists at the Refinery convert orichalc ore into orichalc metal. Orichalc is used in the construction of Pyramids and is also used to make Atlantean Fire launchers at @31Towers and @143Frigate&Wharves. @PIn order for a Refinery to function, it must be built along a road. You also need to make sure that the metallurgists can reach the ore. If there is some impassable terrain in the way - an unbridged body of water, for example - the metallurgists won't be able to mine anything. @PAssuming nothing is blocking the way, the metallurgists make their way to the ore, mine some from the ground and return it to the Refinery. Once the Refinery has converted enough ore to make a cartload, a deliveryman will first look for a @31Tower or @143Frigate&Wharf that needs the metal. If he can't find any, he'll then take the metal to a trading facility if you are exporting the good. If you aren't exporting the metal, or if the trading facility cannot accept any more, than the deliveryman will bring the orichalc to a Storehouse. @PA deliveryman never brings orichalc directly from the Refinery to a construction site. If orichalc is needed for a Pyramid, it is procured from a Storehouse.

message.title: Distribution
message.content: In order for citizens to benefit from all the food and goods you procure for them, you must have an efficient distribution system. The building blocks for the city's distribution system are the @9Granary, @10Storehouse and @8Agora. @12Piers and @11Trading&Posts also play a role in distribution. @PThe Agora is the centerpiece of the distribution system. Vendors come from the Agora and seek out Granaries and Storehouses to procure goods needed by the households the Agora serves. When the Agora is stocked, peddlers emerge to bring the food and goods to the city's residents. The closer the Agora is to its supply sources, the more efficient it will be. If an vendor is too far away from its source of supply, he won't even bother to make the journey. @PStorehouses and Granaries need to be connected to the Agoras that they supply. Storehouses and Granaries must also be connected to the farms and other industries that produce goods to be later distributed to the city's households. @PIf you are importing goods that your citizens need, deliverymen from your trading facilities will deliver the goods to your Storehouses and Granaries, provided they are connected to the Storehouses and Granaries by a road. @PFor more on Piers and Trading posts, read the entry on @117trade.

message.title: Tribute
message.content: All of your subject city's have an obligation to pay you annual tribute. Subject cities include vassals obtained primarily through conquest, and colonies that you have established. Of course, if you yourself are conquered by another city, you will be expected to pay annual tribute to the conqueror. It is quite possible to find yourself collecting tribute from some cities, while simultaneously paying tribute to others. Tribute is paid every year and can take the form of food, goods or money. If you fail to pay the tribute you owe, your overlord will likely become very angry with you. If your relationship with any of your subject cities deteriorates, its leader will stop paying you tribute.

message.title: Quests
message.content: Sometimes, the gods will send you on special errands. These special errands are called Quests. @PAll Quests must be completed by a @94hero. When a god issues a Quest, the appropriate Hero's Hall will be made available to you. After you prepare the Hall, the hero will come to your city. @PTo send the hero on the Quest, click the @75Overview&Tab. You'll see the Quest listed there. If the correct hero is available, you'll see a green light next to the Quest. Click this light, then select the proper hero from the Enlist Forces panel. Click 'Dispatch' to send the hero on the quest. You can also send a hero on a Quest by right-clicking the Hero's Hall and clicking the 'Dispatch' button. Or, you can click the @86Goals&Button and click the 'Dispatch' button that appears on the Goals Panel.

message.title: Black Marble Workshop
message.content: Stonecutters chisel out huge blocks of stone from a @113black&marble&quarry and take it back to the Workshop. At the Workshop, the huge block of marble is broken down into usable slabs. @PA Black Marble Workshop must be built along a road to function properly. And, the stonecutters must be able to get to the black marble quarry. If anything is blocking their way - like an unbridged body of water - the stonecutters will stay inside the Workshop. @PProvided that they can get to the quarry, the stonecutters will make their way there and bring back a huge block of marble. As soon as a slab of marble is cut from the block, a deliveryman will bring the marble to a Storehouse or, if you are exporting the good, to a trading facility. @PBlack marble is used in the construction of @73Pyramids&and&other&huge&buildings. Black marble is never brought directly from a Black Marble Workshop to the artisans at the construction site. Artisans receive shipments of marble from a Storehouse.

message.title: Science
message.content: In Atlantis, science is king. Atlanteans attribute much of their success as a culture to science. @PBecause science is so important, citizens demand that scientists roam their neighborhoods before they will improve their houses. Citizens living in the best homes expect to be schooled by several different scientists. If scientists fail to pass their homes for a period of time, residents will stop taking care of their homes, which will devolve into more primitive states. @PThe types of scientists in Atlantis are the scholar, astronomer, inventor and curator. The scholar studies at the @133Bibliotheke and roams the city's streets when he has made a discovery in his books. Astronomers are trained at @135Universities and then dispatched to @134Observatories to track the paths of the stars. Inventors apprentice themselves to experts at the @136Inventors'&Workshop. When their practice inventions pass muster, they move on to a @137Laboratory where they continue to devise the most ingenious contraptions. Like astronomers, curators also receive training from a University. When their schooling is complete, they proceed to a @138Museum, where they oversee the collections and spread word of the latest exhibits to nearby neighborhoods. @PWhen in Atlantis, science is also important to the hero, @64Hercules. He requires that scientists pass by his Hall and deliver news of the latest advancements before he'll come to the city.

message.title: Bibliotheke
message.content: The Bibliotheke is lined with shelves of books from around the world. Scholars devour the information found in the books and spread news of what they've learned to neighboring residents. @PTo build a Bibliotheke, select the @150Science&Tab and click the Bibliotheke button. Guide the cursor to the spot in the city where you'd like to build the Bibliotheke. If you see a green ghost of the building, you've chosen a suitable location. Click the mouse button to place the building. If you see a red square, then something is preventing placement. Either clear the obstruction or find a new spot for the Bibliotheke. To function, the Bibliotheke must be built along a road. @POnce the Bibliotheke is functioning, scholars begin their studies. Periodically, a scholar will leave the Bibliotheke to teach neighboring residents what he has learned. Residents of the housing he passes benefit from the knowledge that the scholar brings and may improve their homes as a result. @PA scholar is a roaming walker and will turn around if he encounters a @30Road&Block.

message.title: Observatory
message.content: Astronomers keep watch over the skies at an Observatory. @PTo build an Observatory, select the @150Science&Tab and click the 'Astronomy' button. Choose 'Observatory' from the list provided, and guide your cursor to the spot in the city where you'd like the Observatory. If you see a green ghost of the building, click the mouse button to put the Observatory in place. If the cursor is red, either clear the land of obstructions or find a new spot for the Observatory. @PIn order to function properly, an Observatory must be built along a road. You also need a working @135University in your city to train the astronomers. Once the astronomers learn about the stars at a University, they make their way to an Observatory to begin work. @PWhen an astronomer discovers something new in the skies, he walks the city's streets to tell people the news. The residents of each house he passes benefit from the knowledge. @PWhen an astronomer is making his way from a University to the Observatory, he passes through @30Roadblocks. Astronomers that leave from an Observatory, however, will turn around when they encounter a Roadblock.

message.title: University
message.content: Professors at the University train students to become @138curators or @134astronomers. @PTo build a University, select the @150Science&Tab and click the 'University' button. Move the cursor to the spot in your city where you'd like to place the building. If you see a green ghost of the building, click to place the University. If the cursor is still red, something is preventing you from building the University in the selected location. It may be possible to clear the obstruction. Otherwise, you'll need to find another spot for the University. @PMake sure to build the University along a road so that it can function properly. Once the University is operating, professors begin teaching students and sending them to Observatories or a Museum. @PCurators and astronomers who are walking from the University to the Museum or Observatory ignore @30Roadblocks.

message.title: Inventors' Workshop
message.content: An Inventors' Workshop is an incubator for new inventors. Once these new inventors have mastered some basic techniques and developed a good understanding of patent law, they proceed to a @137Laboratory. @PTo build an Inventors' Workshop, first select the @150Science&Tab. Then, click the 'Technology' button and select 'Inventors' Workshop' from the list provided. Move the cursor to the place in the city where you'd like to place the Inventors' Workshop. If the cursor turns into a green ghost of the building, you've chosen a suitable location. Click the mouse button to build the Inventors' Workshop. If the cursor is still red, then something is preventing you from placing the building in the selected location. See if you can clear away any obstructions. If you can't, then you'll need to select a different location for the Workshop. Make sure to build the Workshop along a road. @POnce the Workshop is functioning, it will begin to train new inventors and send them to Laboratories. Inventors that are going from an Inventors' Workshop to a Laboratory ignore @30Roadblocks.

message.title: Laboratory
message.content: Inventors work on their latest inventions at the Laboratory. When they have devised something truly extraordinary, they excitedly leave the Laboratory to tell neighboring residents about the invention. @PTo build a Laboratory, select the @150Science&Tab and click the 'Technology' button. Choose 'Laboratory' from the list and guide the cursor to the spot where you'd like to build the Laboratory. If you see a green ghost of the building, click the mouse button to set the Laboratory in place. If the cursor is red, something is in the way. If you cannot clear the obstruction, you'll have to find another spot for the building. @PTo function properly, the Laboratory must be built along a road. It also needs skilled inventors from an @136Inventors'&Workshop.

message.title: Museum
message.content: The Museum holds the mysteries of the Atlantean past. A city can have only one Museum. @PTo build a Museum, select the @150Science&Tab and click the 'Museum' button. Guide the cursor to the spot where you'd like to place the Museum. If you see a green ghost of the building, click to place the Museum. If the cursor is red, something is preventing you from placing the Museum in the chosen spot. If you can't clear the obstruction, you'll have to find a new location. @PThe Museum must be built along a road to function. Curators who have graduated from a @135University must also make their way to the Museum. As new exhibits are developed, curators leave the Museum to tell residents of the city about the latest show. @PCurators from a Museum will turn around when they encounter a @30Roadblock. If a curator is on his way from the University to the Museum, he'll ignore Roadblocks.

message.title: Hippodrome and Crosswalk
message.content: Atlanteans enjoy watching the speed and grace of horses at a Hippodrome. Each city can have only one Hippodrome. @PHippodromes are built one segment at a time. They can be as big or small as you want. They can be a simple oval or a more free-form design. To place a segment of Hippodrome, select the @81Administration&Tab and click the Hippodrome button. Select 'Hippodrome' from the list and guide your cursor to the spot in the city where you'd like to start the Hippodrome. If you've chosen a suitable spot, the cursor will turn green. As you hold the cursor in place, the different types of segments you can build will cycle through. When you see the type of segment you want to build, click the mouse button to build the segment. @PRepeat the process to build additional segments of Hippodrome, making sure to attach the new segment to the end of an existing segment. Or, you can build multiple straight sections of Hippodrome at one time by clicking the mouse button and dragging the mouse until the Hippodrome is the desired length. A Hippodrome is considered complete when you have a closed loop. @PBefore races can begin, a handler from the Hippodrome must retrieve some horses from a Horse Ranch. The longer the Hippodrome is, the more horses will be needed. Right-click on the Hippodrome to find out how many horses the Hippodrome needs, and how many are already in the Hippodrome's paddock, ready to race. @PThe longer the Hippodrome is, the more benefits it brings to your city. The bigger your Hippodrome, the more money it will generate for you. You'll also become more respected by other leaders, and your own people will admire you more. Your people do have their limits, though. If your Hippodrome is exceptionally large, they'll begin to resent your dedication to the races, and your popularity with your citizens will plummet. @PHippodromes can pose some interesting city design questions. To help fit a Hippodrome into your city, use the Crosswalk. @PTo build a Crosswalk, select the Administration Tab and click the 'Hippodrome' button. Then, choose Crosswalk from the list. Guide the cursor so that it is adjacent to the section of Hippodrome you want your citizens to cross. Make sure that there is either clear land or a road on both sides of the selected segment. If you have chosen a good spot, you'll see a green ghost of the Crosswalk. Click the mouse button to place the Crosswalk. If the cursor is red, then the spot you've chosen isn't suitable. If you can, clear obstructions on both sides of the Hippodrome. Otherwise, you'll have to find a different spot for the Crosswalk. @PThe city's residents treat a Crosswalk just like they do a road or bridge.

message.title: Water Park
message.content: People love to play in Water Parks. @PThere are several variations of Water Park. To see your choices, select 'Water Park' from the list of Recreational Areas. Hold the cursor over some clear land, and you'll see your choices cycle through. When you see the type of Water Park you want, click the mouse button to place it. You can also click your mouse button and drag the mouse to place more than one Water Park at a time.

message.title: Chariot Factory
message.content: With a supply of @41wood and @34horses, workers at a Chariot Factory build and outfit chariots. Chariots are used by the most elite of Atlantean soldiers. @PTo build a Chariot Factory, select the Military Tab and click the 'Military Workshops' button. Choose 'Chariot Factory' from the list provided and move the cursor to the area where you want to build the Factory. If you see a green ghost of the building, click the mouse button to put the Chariot Factory in place. If the cursor is red, there is something preventing you from placing the building in the chosen location. If you cannot clear the obstruction, you'll need to find another spot for the Chariot Factory. @PMake sure to build the Chariot Factory along a road, and make sure that this road is connected to a supply of wood and horses. Otherwise, the Chariot Factory will be unable to make chariots. @PWhen the Chariot Factory needs wood, deliverymen from a @41Timber&Mill, Storehouse or trading facility will deliver a supply. When the Chariot Factory needs horses, a hostler from the Factory will personally go to a @34Horse&Ranch to retrieve some horses. @PCompleted chariots are stored at the Chariot Factory until a chariot vendor from an Agora picks them up. Chariots cannot be traded.

message.title: Atlantean Soldiers
message.content: The Atlantean army is made up of three types of soldiers: archers, spearmen and charioteers. @PErstwhile archers are the most basic soldier in the Atlantean military. They come from @6common&housing and supply their own bows and arrows. Their strength is long-range combat. Archers may only be used for city defense and cannot be sent abroad. For information on the specific orders that you can issue archers, click @145here. @PSpearmen come from the city's @7elite&housing. Once a peddler from an @8Agora supplies a house with armor, some of its residents will gladly take up arms in the interest of their city, both at home and abroad. Their strength is short-range combat. Click @146here to learn about the orders you can give spearmen. @PCharioteers are the most elite soldiers in the Atlantean military. Only residents from the city's best elite housing can become charioteers. For more information on charioteer orders, click @147here.

message.title: Frigate Wharf
message.content: Each Frigate Wharf serves an associated frigate. Frigates only sail the seas in Atlantis. @PTo build a Frigate Wharf, select the Military Tab and click on the Military Workshops button. From the list that appears, choose Frigate Wharf. A red footprint of the building will appear. @PFrigate Wharves must be placed along the water, on a straight section of coastline. Run the red footprint along the coastline until you see a green ghost of the Frigate Wharf. Click to put the building into place. Make sure to build the Wharf along a road. @PIn order for workers at the Frigate Wharf to build a frigate, there must be a @24Palace in the city. The Frigate Wharf must also have a supply of wood and armor to build a frigate and to outfit its marines. Once these conditions have been satisfied, the Frigate Wharf's workers will build and later man the frigate. @PAfter the frigate has been built, it can be equipped with a deadly Atlantean Fire launcher. To arm a frigate with this deadly weapon, a load of @127orichalc must be delivered to the Frigate Wharf. Frigates that launch Atlantean Fire are stronger than boats that can not fire this dangerous weapon. @PIt requires a lot of people to build and man a frigate. If you're not ready to build the frigate yet, because, for example, you lack the necessary wood or armor, you may release the Wharf's workers so that they may be employed by other industries. To do this, right click on the Wharf, then click the 'Send Wharf workers home' button at the bottom of the panel. To recall the workers to build the frigate, click the same button, which now says, 'Staff this Frigate Wharf'. @PClick @144here to find out which orders you can give to a frigate.

message.title: Frigate Orders
message.content: The agile frigate is adept at defending your Atlantean city's shores and can be sent abroad on some military campaigns. When equipped with Atlantean Fire, the frigate becomes even stronger. Read the entry on the @143Frigate&Wharf to learn more about the manufacture of frigates and how to arm them with Atlantean Fire. @PTo move the frigate, click on it and then click on the location you would like it to move to. To issue the frigate orders, click on it, then use one of the orders buttons that will appear on the Control Panel. The orders are: @L@PCALL CREW TO SHIP/SEND CREW HOME. This order tells the ship's crew to come aboard, or to go home, depending on what they are currently doing. Keep in mind that while issuing the 'Send Crew Home' command returns the frigate to the Wharf and disbands its crew, it does not instruct the frigate's Wharf to repair the ship. If you want repairs performed on the ship, you'll have to issue the 'Carry Out Repairs' order. @L@PDEFEND LOCATION. When given this order, the ship's captain will hold his vessel in one location, and defend this location against any attackers that come near. @L@PATTACK ALL ENEMIES. When given this order, the ship's captain will aggressively seek out any enemy and attack it. The captain chooses which enemies to attack following a fixed set of priorities. First he'll seek out enemy transports which are currently carrying soldiers, to try to destroy them before their soldiers can reach land. If there are no such vessels, he looks for enemy warships to attack. Failing that, he'll order his frigate close to shore to attack any enemy soldiers that might have landed. Finally, if there are no enemy soldiers within his reach, he'll attack empty enemy transports. @L@PPATROL AREA. When given this order, the frigate's captain will patrol your city's waters, attacking any enemy ships he encounters. @L@PCARRY OUT REPAIRS. Clicking this button will send the frigate back to its Wharf to be repaired. If the ship is severely damaged, the frigate captain will take it upon himself to return to the Wharf for repairs. @L@PGO TO SHIP. Clicking this button centers your view on the frigate. @PYou cannot issue military commands while the game is @3paused. @PYou can select more than one frigate at a time and issue all of them the same orders. First, select a single frigate. When the cursor changes, click and drag your mouse. You'll notice that a box appears. Adjust this box by clicking and dragging your mouse so that the box contains all the frigates you want to select. Then, let go of the mouse button and order away! @PAfter you've selected a group of frigates, you can assign a hotkey to them. With the group selected, hold down the CTRL and press 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5. When you want to recall the group of ships, simply press the ALT key plus the number that you assigned it to. @PWhile the frigate is an extremely effective weapon, it can be eluded by the crafty Oceanids. When Oceanids attack, they swim toward your city under the cover of deep water. Not even Atlantean Fire can harm them while they are approaching your city.

message.title: Archer Orders
message.content: Atlantean archers come from the city's @6common&housing. Residents of common housing will begin fighting for the city as soon as they are living in houses that are at least at the Hovel level, and you have erected a Palace. @PTo select a company of archers, click on its standard or click on any of the women in the company. When you do, the @86Control&Panel will change, displaying the company's status. You'll see the company's name, along with the current morale of its women. If a company's morale dips too low, its women will refuse to fight. You'll also see a brief description of what the company is currently doing. @PAbove the status information is a series of buttons that you use to position the company and give it orders. The buttons you'll see are: @PGO TO COMPANY BUTTON. Clicking on the Go To Company button will center your view on the company's standard. @PROTATE COMPANY BUTTON. The Rotate Company button indicates which direction the company is currently facing. Clicking on the button will rotate the company. @PMUSTER COMPANY/SEND HOME BUTTON. The Muster Company/Send Home button lets you call your soldiers to arms (muster) or send them home, depending on which they are currently doing. @PUSE DEFENSIVE TACTICS. When archers have been told to defend an area, they hold their position and fire arrows at any enemy within range. @PUSE OFFENSIVE TACTICS. When told to employ an offensive tactic, archers will seek out and attack any nearby enemy. @PEMPLOY SPECIAL TACTICS. The special tactic employed by archers is the skirmish. Archers will shoot arrows at a distant enemy. As the enemy approaches, the archers will fall back and continue firing arrows. After the skirmish ends, archers will return to their standard if there are no other enemies nearby. @PSHOW ALL FORCES. Clicking on the Magnifying Glass brings up a list of @84all&your&military&forces. From there, you can issue general instructions to all of your military forces. @PYou cannot issue military commands while the game is @3paused.

message.title: Spearmen Orders
message.content: @PSpearmen come from the Atlantean city's @7Mansions and @7Manors. @PTo select a phalanx of spearmen, click on its standard or click on any of the soldiers in the company. When you do, the Control Panel will change, displaying the company's status. You'll see the company's name, along with the current morale of its men. If a company's morale dips too low, its spearmen will refuse to fight. You'll also see a brief description of what the company is currently doing. @PAbove the status information is a series of buttons that you use to position the company and give it orders. The buttons you'll see are: @PGO TO COMPANY BUTTON. Clicking on the Go To Company button will center your view on the company's standard. @PROTATE COMPANY BUTTON. The Rotate Company button indicates which direction the company is currently facing. Clicking on the button will rotate the company. @PMUSTER COMPANY/SEND HOME BUTTON. The Muster Company/Send Home button lets you call your soldiers to arms and send them home. What the company is currently doing governs which command clicking this button will issue. If the company is already mustered, then clicking the button will send the men home. If the company is at home, then clicking the button will call the soldiers to arms. @PUSE DEFENSIVE TACTICS. When employing defensive tactics, spearmen will stand their ground, and attack anything that comes close to them with their spears. @PUSE OFFENSIVE TACTICS. When told to use offensive tactics, spearmen move together as a unit, attacking with their spears. @PEMPLOY SPECIAL TACTICS. The spearmen's special tactic is the wedge, which is good for breaking defensive formations. The soldiers organize themselves into a wedge shape to attack enemies. @PSHOW ALL FORCES. Clicking on the Magnifying Glass brings up a list of @84all&your&military&forces. From there, you can issue general instructions to your entire military. @PYou cannot issue military commands while the game is @3paused.

message.title: Charioteer Orders
message.content: @PCharioteers come from the Atlantean city's @7Estates. @PTo select a company of charioteers, click on its standard or click on any of the soldiers in the company.
