When you do, the Control Panel will change, displaying the company's status. You'll see the company's name, along with the current morale of its men. If a company's morale dips too low, its men will refuse to fight. You'll also see a brief description of what the company is currently doing. @PAbove the status information is a series of buttons that you use to position the company and give it orders. The buttons you'll see are: @PGO TO COMPANY BUTTON. Clicking on the Go To Company button will center your view on the company's standard. @PROTATE COMPANY BUTTON. The Rotate Company button indicates which direction the company is currently facing. Clicking on the button will rotate the company. @PMUSTER COMPANY/SEND HOME BUTTON. The Muster Company/Send Home button lets you call your soldiers to arms or send them home, depending on which they are currently doing. @PUSE DEFENSIVE TACTICS. When charioteers have been told to defend an area, they remain in their chariots and attack any enemy that comes within range. @PUSE OFFENSIVE TACTICS. When told to use offensive tactics, charioteers will charge the enemy in an attempt to break their formations, after which they'll stay and fight. The charioteers will charge as often as they can, but the horses do need to rest between attacks. If engaged directly, the charioteers will respond in kind. @PEMPLOY SPECIAL TACTICS. The charioteers special tactic is to harass. When told to harass, charioteers charge the enemy, fight for a little bit, and then retreat. When the horses are rested, they repeat the maneuver. @PSHOW ALL FORCES. Clicking on the Magnifying Glass brings up a list of @84all&your&military&forces. From there, you can issue general instructions to your entire military. @PYou cannot issue military commands while the game is @3paused.

message.title: Symphonia Ithikos
message.content: Atlanteans are bound by the Symphonia Ithikos, which prohibits internecine warfare. Any Atlantean leader that attack or raids another Atlantean ally will be swiftly punished. All Atlantean allies will instantly become the attacker's rival. If you, as an Atlantean leader, decide to attack or raid one of your compatriots, don't count on any help from other Atlantean leaders. All other Atlantean leaders will refuse to take part in such a murderous folly.

message.title: Orange Tree
message.content: Oranges grown on Orange Trees are enjoyed as food. To harvest oranges, you must have an @109Orange&Tenders'&Lodge. @POrange trees must be placed in a @113meadow. They do not need to be planted along a road. @PThe orange harvest starts in November and lasts for two months. Any oranges left on the trees after the harvest go to waste.

message.title: Science Tab
message.content: Select the Science Tab to keep your Atlanteans well-informed about the latest scientific discoveries. @PWhen you select the Science Tab, the buttons for the types of science building that you can construct in a city will appear. The possible buttons are @133Bibliotheke, Astronomy, Technology and @138Museum. Clicking Astronomy will bring up a list of two buildings: @134Observatory and @135University. Clicking Technology will also bring up a list of two buildings: @136Inventors'&Workshop and @137Laboratory. @PThe Science Tab also helps you to keep track of the scientific activity in your city. The types of scientific pursuits are listed on the tab, along with an assessment of how adequately served the science needs of your citizens are. For more information on science in the city, click the small magnifying glass. More detailed information will appear, including the specific number of science buildings the city has. @PTo keep track of a specific type of scientific pursuit, use the small buttons at the top of the Science Tab. Click 'Show Scholars' to see all the Bibliothekes and scholars in the city, along with how recently each house in the city has been passed by a scholar. Clicking 'Show Astronomers' will allow you to see the astronomers in your city, along with all the Observatories and Universities. Columns in front of the houses reveal if an astronomer has recently passed. Click the 'Show Inventors' buttons to see the city's inventors, Inventors' Workshops and Laboratories. Clicking 'Show Curators' allows you to see the city's curators, Museums and Universities. Finally, click on 'Show All Science' to see all the scientists and science buildings in the city. You'll also be able to see how adequately educated the residents of each house are.

message.title: Deer
message.content: The docile and tasty deer is the favorite target of the deer hunter. To hunt deer, you must build a @69Hunting&Lodge. Once the Hunting Lodge has employees, the hunt will begin.

message.title: Cattle
message.content: Cattle graze in a meadow until it is time for them to do their duty to the people of the city and become food. Cattle are slaughtered at the @108Corral. @PTo place some cattle in a meadow, first make sure that you have a Corral. Then, select the @77Husbandry&Tab and click the 'Herding' button. Select the 'Cattle' button, and place the livestock. Some of the cattle you place are bulls. Bulls guard the herd of cows from hungry wolves and are never used for meat. @PCattle may be sacrificed to the gods at the city's Sanctuaries.

message.title: Pyramids
message.content: Atlanteans have developed advanced construction techniques, and these techniques are showcased in the construction of Pyramids. The types of pyramids you can build are the Modest Pyramid, Pyramid, Great Pyramid and Majestic Pyramid. The main difference among these pyramids is size. @PTo lay the foundation for a Pyramid, select the @85Aesthetics&Tab and click the Pyramid button. Choose the Pyramid you would like to build from the list provided. Then, guide the Pyramid's footprint to the spot in your city where you would like to build the structure. If the footprint turns into a green ghost of the building, then you have chosen a good spot. Click the mouse button to set the Pyramid in place. If the footprint is red, then something is preventing you from placing the Pyramid in the selected location. Either clear any obstructions, or find a new spot for the Pyramid. For more information on building a Pyramid, consult the entry on @73building&pyramids&and&other&large&buildings. @PTo build a pyramid, you need the services of artisans from an @45Artisans'&Guild. You also need supplies of marble (@131black, @42white or both), @127orichalc and @41wood. For more on building pyramids, click @73here. @PYou can have only one of each Pyramid type in your city.

message.title: Shrines
message.content: A Shrine is dedicated to a specific god. There are three types of Shrine: the Minor Shrine, the Shrine and the Major Shrine. @PTo lay the foundation for a Shrine, select the @85Aesthetics&Tab and click the Pyramid button. Choose the Shrine that you would like to build from the list provided. @PTo build a Minor Shrine or a Major Shrine, you'll need supplies of marble (@42white, @131black or both), @127orichalc, @41wood and @48sculpture. You do not need sculpture to build a regular Shrine. For more on the construction of shrines, click @73here. @PYou can only have one shrine of each type dedicated to a god. So, for example, you can have a Major Shrine dedicated to Hera and another Major Shrine dedicated to Artemis, but you cannot have two Major Shrines dedicated to Hera.

message.title: Monuments to the Sky
message.content: Monuments to the Sky stretch towards the stars, which are a favorite topic of conversation among Atlanteans. There are three types of Monuments to the Sky: Small Monument to the Sky, Monument to the Sky and Grand Monument to the Sky. @PTo lay the foundation for a Monument to the Sky, select the @85Aesthetics&Tab and click the Pyramid button. Choose the Monument to the Sky that you would like to build from the list provided. @PTo build a Monument to the Sky, you'll need supplies of marble (@42white, @131black or both), @127orichalc and @41wood. For more information on the construction of Monuments to the Sky, click @73here. @PYou can have only one of each type of Monument to the Sky in your city.

message.title: Altar of Olympus
message.content: The Altar of Olympus is a favorite sight of Atlanteans. @PTo lay the foundation for the Altar of Olympus, select the @85Aesthetics&Tab and click the Pyramid button. Choose 'Altar of Olympus' from the list provided. @PTo build the Altar of Olympus, you'll need supplies of marble (@42white, @131black or both), @127orichalc and @41wood. For more information on the construction of the Altar of Olympus, click @73here. @PYou can have only one Altar of Olympus in your city.

message.title: Temple of Olympus
message.content: The Temple of Olympus reminds your people of the gods' lofty home. @PTo lay the foundation for the Temple of Olympus, select the @85Aesthetics&Tab and click the Pyramid button. Choose 'Temple of Olympus' from the list provided. @PTo build the Temple of Olympus, you'll need supplies of marble (@42white, @131black or both), @127orichalc and @41wood. For more information on the construction of the Temple of Olympus, click @73here. @PYou can have only one Temple of Olympus in your city.

message.title: Pyramid of the Pantheon
message.content: The Pyramid of the Pantheon celebrates all gods. @PTo lay the foundation for the Pyramid of the Pantheon, select the @85Aesthetics&Tab and click the Pyramid button. Choose 'Pyramid of the Pantheon' from the list provided. @PTo build the Pyramid of the Pantheon, you'll need supplies of marble (@42white, @131black or both), @127orichalc, @48sculpture and @41wood. For more information on the construction of the Pyramid of the Pantheon, click @73here. @PYou can have only one Pyramid of the Pantheon in your city.

message.title: Observatory Kosmika
message.content: The beautiful Observatory Kosmika keeps watch over the skies. @PTo lay the foundation for the Observatory Kosmika, select the @85Aesthetics&Tab and click the Pyramid button. Choose 'Observatory Kosmika' from the list provided. @PTo build the Observatory Kosmika, you'll need supplies of marble (@42white, @131black or both), @127orichalc and @41wood. For more information on the construction of the Observatory Kosmika, click @73here. @PYou can have only one Observatory Kosmika in your city.

message.title: Museum Atlantika
message.content: The Museum Atlantika is a testament to the thirst for knowledge on Atlantis. @PTo lay the foundation for the Museum Atlantika, select the @85Aesthetics&Tab and click the Pyramid button. Choose 'Museum Atlantika' from the list provided. @PTo build the Museum Atlantika, you'll need supplies of marble (@42white, @131black or both), @127orichalc and @41wood. For more information on the construction of the Museum Atlantika, click @73here. @PYou can have only one Museum Atlantika in your city.

message.title: The Birth of Atlantis
message.content: Your great father, Atlas, is intent on building the continent of Atlantis into a mighty nation, unsurpassed by any the world has ever seen. He has turned to you for help in achieving this goal. This is a fairly easy adventure that consists of seven parent city episodes and two colony episodes.

message.title: The Capital City
message.content: @PMy dearest child, for a long time now you have enjoyed the benefits that come to the offspring of a king. Now, it is time for you to assume the responsibility that your high birth demands. Each of my nine brothers deserves a kingdom, and, as the eldest, I have pledged to personally assist them to found their kingdoms. First, I am going to help Gadirus, my own twin, build his city. While I am away, I am entrusting you to construct a fair and mighty city here near the hill where I was born and raised. Poseidon himself dug the water-filled trenches that encircle the hill, protecting it from enemies. The city that you build will become the capital of all of Atlantis, so be sure that the city befits its stature. Good luck!

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PNews of your progress in the city of Atlantis has reached me here in Gades, and I applaud your efforts. Hopefully, your uncle, Gadirus, will prove as successful in Gades as you have been in Atlantis. As you continue to work, keep in mind your familial obligations. If Gadirus or any other of your uncles requires your aid, do not hesitate to give it to them. If you help them, they will most certainly help you in your times of need.

message.title: All Creatures Great and Greater
message.content: @PGreetings from the city of Euaemos! Your uncle, Euaemon, has settled into his new city, but some of the things that I have spotted in the Atlantean countryside have given me cause for concern. In my travels, I've noticed monsters and beasts of enormous size and fearsome disposition roaming the countryside. As we begin to establish ourselves here, we're all bound to have closer encounters with these creatures. @PIt seems that our activities on Atlantis have caught the eyes of the Olympians. Some are quite pleased with our activities, but, as usual, Hera is seething with jealousy. Angrily, she barked, 'Finders-keepers does not apply on Olympus! All of the gods should have an equal chance of being patron of Atlantis. When the patronage of Athens was up for grabs, did some god just take it? No! There was a competition! Besides, all I've got are some crummy cities. Why does Poseidon get a whole continent to call his own? I want a continent, too!' With that, she spun on her heel and stormed out of the room, muttering and gesturing all the while. Watch out for Hera. When she's upset, she always takes out her frustrations on some unsuspecting innocent. @PAphrodite, on the other hand, seems thrilled with Atlantis. She's visited me several times already, always while I was helping one of your uncles build some large building. As I toiled away under the hot sun, my chest, arms and other regions glistening with sweat, I heard Aphrodite coo, 'How magnificent! How rugged!' I'm not sure if she was referring to the beauty of the countryside, the imposing edifice under construction, or me! Regardless, I think she could be very useful if you build her a Sanctuary to call her own. @PI have forwarded you the plans that our scholars drew up for a magnificent new structure called a Pyramid. On paper, it looks to be quite impressive. Why don't you build one and see how it turns out?

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PI could not be more proud of you! You have overcome some impressive challenges! How did you ever manage to kill that Minotaur? I heard that Hera paid you a little visit, too. @PFrom the descriptions I've received, the new Pyramid sounds absolutely awe-inspiring. I bet that you could build them on an even grander scale. @PMeanwhile, our problem with gigantic animals is worsening. While building the city of Ampher, a ten-foot tall iguana, sent by that runt Hermes, almost ate me for lunch. If I, one of the strongest men in the world, can almost fall victim to these huge animals, then how will we ever convince ordinary mortals that our continent is a safe place to live?

message.title: Big Game Hunting
message.content: @POur problem with oversized creatures has come to a head. We have found the perfect place to build your uncle Mneuseus' city, but the area is ferociously guarded by a giant, malevolent gopher. That fool Hermes was spotted in the area, so I suspect he is to blame for our gopher problem. Luckily, Artemis became very excited when she heard of all the giant creatures here, so maybe she can help us with our trouble. @PUntil we find an effective way of handling our big animal problem, there is nothing for you to do but to continue building up Atlantis into the most glorious city ever.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThanks to Artemis and Atalanta, our extra-large animal problem is solved! I am happy to say that we did our part in controlling these creatures, too. Using orichalc, our scientists devised the most amazing weapon called Atlantean Fire. There is nothing more majestic than watching blazing red Atlantean Fire fly through the air and hit its target. When Atlantean Fire strikes its victim, it adheres to the unsuspecting subject, causing quite a lot of pain. That gopher sure didn't like Atlantean Fire much. Can you believe that orichalc, which decorates Pyramids so beautifully, can be transformed by our scientists into a deadly weapon? You should really try it out for yourself! Just build a Tower or Frigate Wharf. Once these buildings have received some orichalc, the workers there will make Atlantean Fire. You'll be thrilled with the result! @PIt seems that several, smaller beasts have escaped Artemis and Atalanta's nets and snares. Luckily, our own armies have had little trouble killing these hideous half-man, half-horse creatures.

message.title: War and Ethics
message.content: @PThe half-men, half-horse monsters have done the unthinkable. They have attacked and completely destroyed Euaemos. I credit the gods with your uncle Euaemon's successful escape, but we must prepare ourselves against further attack. The gods have already done so much for us; I think that we can handle this particular monster problem ourselves. Take care to fortify Atlantis lest these murderous brutes set their sights on you.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PWhat have we done? How were we to know? These half-men, half-horse beings that we took for horrible beasts were a race of intelligent beings called Centaurs, and we have utterly destroyed them. These Centaurs had built a beautiful city at Cennia, with a gorgeous shrine to Dionysus, and even one to my own father, Poseidon! How were we to know? @PThe learned scholars say that we should take pains to discover everything we can about other creatures and peoples before we fight them. They believe that this horrible tragedy could have been averted. This seems reasonable, but isn't there something else we can do to prevent us from sinking into barbarism again?

message.title: The Symphonia Ithikos
message.content: @PFor days and days I have been tortured by what we have done to the Centaurs. I have beseeched my father to provide some solace and have sacrificed bull after bull to persuade him to speak. Finally, he brought me to Olympus to discuss the matter. To my surprise, the Olympians were fuming with anger. They decried our arrogant act and demanded an explanation for our actions. They said that only the gods could decide which species could live and which could die, that it wasn't the place of some upstart Atlantean. I assured the gods that the Atlanteans weren't trying to usurp their power, and that we knew that we had made a horrible mistake when we killed the Centaurs, a mistake that we hope never to repeat. But, we are destined to repeat our error if we continue to be subjected to attacks by vicious monsters and dangerous animals sent by jealous gods. @PAfter I finished speaking, the gods withdrew to an inner room. When they emerged, father Poseidon said, 'We gods have carefully considered your words, son, and find that they have merit. So, we propose a pact. If you foreswear war and bloodshed except in the defense of your lands, we gods will never launch an attack on the continent of Atlantis, nor will we loose our monsters on it.' I judged the pact to be fair and just, and quickly accepted the terms. The agreement will certainly prevent us from repeating the mistake we made with the Centaurs. 'One word of warning, son,' Poseidon said. 'If the Atlanteans ever break this pact, I can personally assure you that no good will come of it.' @PWith the sacred pact in hand, I returned to Atlantis to meet with the scholars. The scholars proclaimed the agreement well-reasoned, but suggested that we put our own, personal stamp on the pact to truly make it Atlantean. And so, to the sacred vow to make no more war, we added our own pledge to uphold our values of Science and Knowledge and named the whole the Symphonia Ithikos. To underscore the permanence of this pact, I want to inscribe it on a magnificent tablet. Perhaps one of the gods knows of a suitable material on which to carve this holiest of holy text. @PSurely, father Poseidon is largely responsible for this wonderful pact, and building a magnificent Sanctuary to my father in the center of the city of Atlantis would be an ideal way of honoring him. But before you can build this amazing edifice, you must find a cornerstone. Not just any stone will do; it must be the finest block of stone ever seen.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PWhat a wondrous place the Crimson Isle is! And dangerous, too! With its constant earthquakes and fierce monsters, it's no surprise that only heroes are brave enough to go there. The beautiful cornerstone quarried there will be perfect for Poseidon's Sanctuary. And, the best artisans in our land have already begun to inscribe the Symphonia Ithikos on the gorgeous tablet of orichalc that was found on the Isle. The orichalc tablet, strong and durable, will last forever, just as all Atlanteans' commitment to the Symphonia Ithikos will last for eternity. @PYour skills are needed in another part of our great continent. The time has come to establish a colony and, since I am still busy helping your uncles build their kingdoms, I need you to found the city for me. As soon as you get it up and running, you'll be able to return to Atlantis and begin constructing the Sanctuary for Poseidon.

message.title: The Citadel of Poseidon
message.content: @PEveryone on Atlantis has happily embraced the tenets of the Symphonia Ithikos. Certainly, the path we have chosen, that of peace and knowledge, will lead us all to greater glory. The gods have been upholding their side of the pact, too. Except for a few rogue monsters, I haven't seen any more outrageously sized animals since we entered into this agreement. As long as we Atlanteans honor this pact, no harm will come our way. If we ever fail to live up to our promise - I don't want to imagine the horror that would befall us. @PNow, it is time for you to focus on celebrating the glory of your grandfather, Poseidon. You have the sacred cornerstone that you need for his Sanctuary; now oversee the construction of what will surely be the most magnificent building any mortal or god has ever laid eyes upon. Perhaps the central isle of your city would be the ideal location for the Sanctuary. After all, it was on this isle that your grandfather first saw your grandmother.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PPoseidon is very proud of you today, and so am I. The Citadel of Poseidon is even more beautiful than I had imagined that it could be. All of your uncles have been patting me on the back and telling me that I've done a remarkable job raising you, and that you will certainly do a fine job when you climb to Atlantis' throne. @PThat time may come sooner than you think. Don't fret, I am not at death's door. In fact, it's quite the opposite. Since I visited Olympus, I have not been able to get the splendid home of the gods out of my mind. Jokingly, I asked my father what I needed to do to live on Olympus myself. To my complete shock, my father said that he longed to have me, the most capable and intelligent of all his sons, by his side on Olympus. He gave me a list of things I need to do to enter the Pantheon, and he promised to begin negotiating with the other gods to allow me into their number. @PIn the meantime, your skills are again needed in another part of the kingdom.

message.title: Atlas, the God
message.content: @PMy plan to become immortal is almost complete, but I need your help to realize this amazing dream. To attain immortality, I must eat ambrosia, the food of the gods. Be on the lookout for an opportunity to find some for me. @PTo cement my place among the gods, I want you to build a Pyramid, more spectacular than any other Pyramid that has ever been built. Call this Pyramid the Pyramid of the Pantheon, and see to it that it is decorated with sculptures of the gods that have given us everything. @PI am about to cross the threshold into a new kind of life, and you are, too. When I become immortal, the kingdom of Atlantis will be yours to rule.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe moment has arrived. The delicious ambrosia has made me immortal - though I could have used some nectar to wash it down. Now, I am to be welcomed as a god by all the Olympians, and you are to be crowned as supreme ruler of the kingdom of Atlantis. As I leave this world behind, I have no doubt that you will continue to lead Atlantis well, perhaps even surpassing my excellence. Remember all that I have taught you, and remember to uphold the Symphonia Ithikos. I will always be watching over you and Atlantis. @PBy the way, I am quite pleased with the Pyramid of the Pantheon. I especially like the sculpture of me that you commissioned and added to the mighty edifice. Well done!

message.title: People of the Sea
message.subtitle: This location is the perfect spot for a trade center, but no one knows what lurks just off Atlantis' shores.
message.content: @PExpect the unexpected in the western wilds of our land. No Atlantean has ever settled here, yet the location of the new city you will build is ideal. It has been blessed with many resources, and it is well-suited to become an important trade center. The only trouble is some mysterious ocean dwellers who have been punishing the coastline with raids. If these people become a problem for you, please remember the Symphonia Ithikos and react to them with quiet restraint. You may defend your city in any way you see fit, but remember that attacking these sea folk is taboo. I have already sent some emissaries to find out more about these ocean dwellers and to try to establish peaceful relations. Please be patient until our emissaries can do their work. @PI am helping your uncle, Elasippus, start his city not far to the north of where you are, so please honor him by sending any materials that he may request.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe Symphonia Ithikos has worked perfectly! The Oceanids may never be our best friends, but they have agreed to trade with us, and each side has absolved the other of any past slights. The Oceanids have generously offered to approach our cities in trade boats, rather then in their usual method, to make our transactions easier. You have done very well with Evenestus, but it is time to leave Eggudico in charge there and return to Atlantis.

message.title: The Hungry Sphinx
message.subtitle: Blessed with ore and marble, Leucippium is an artisan's fantasy, with one slight twist.
message.content: @POnce you have the city here at Leucippium up and running, Atlantis will never lack a good supply of construction materials. But, there is a small quandary that we haven't yet solved. Our problem takes the form of a Sphinx who resides in the area. Following the tenets of the Symphonia Ithikos, I sent scholars to find out more about her. The Sphinx responded to our scholars' questions with a question of her own. When our learned men failed to answer her correctly, she leapt upon them and swallowed them whole! Now, she's roaming the countryside, eating everyone and everything that doesn't answer her correctly. If only someone could figure out the answer to her riddle, maybe she would leave us alone.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PIn accordance with the Symphonia Ithikos, we defended our fair city from the horrible Sphinx, who would simply not listen to reason. We owe the safety of our city to the brave Atalanta, who was clever enough to devise the answer to the Sphinx's riddle. The Sphinx was so shocked that Atalanta solved the riddle, she did not even see Atalanta's deadly arrows screaming towards her. @PThe materials that Leucippium produces will supply lots of cities around the continent with the materials they need. Leave Leucippium in the hands of Nauklarida and return to Atlantis. You have more work to do.

message.title: Adventure Complete
message.content: @PFondest greetings! I am happy to say that immortality agrees with me, and I am doing quite well conducting godly acts. I see that the crown of leadership fits you perfectly. You are masterfully leading the kingdom of Atlantis, and all of your uncles, dutifully leading kingdoms of their own, have told me that they are thrilled with your performance. @PBest of all, you are setting a fine example for your people by honoring the Symphonia Ithikos. All in Atlantis are following suit, and we gods could not be more pleased with the result. @PWith you at the helm, the future of Atlantis is bright! I am proud to be your father.

message.title: Enlightenment in the West
message.content: With Atlantis safely settled, the thirst for knowledge draws the Atlanteans westward. This adventure is above average in difficulty and consists of four parent city episodes and three colony episodes.

message.title: Westward Ho!
message.content: @P'Order! Order please! Will the Council please come to order! Azaes, Diaprepes, stop fighting over the last piece of steak! The cooks will bring out more!' With that, Atlon, the High King of Atlantis, called to order the Council of Atlantis, a meeting of the rulers of the ten Kingdoms of Atlantis. 'And now, a report from Stevros, head of the Grand Westward Expedition.' A burly, well-tanned fellow stood up and spoke: 'Crikey! The things I saw west of here will amaze you! I came across a new land, filled with astounding animals like ocelots, otters, manatees and geckos! And the trees! Big, leafy green trees like mangroves, beechnuts and mahoganies blanketed the land. And how did I learn about all these animals and plants? From the people! They call themselves Mayans. Ain't they beauties?' @PThe Council unanimously decided that more exploration of these western lands was needed, and that one of the rulers of Atlantis should personally oversee the voyages. As the leader of the western-most kingdom, you were chosen to direct the expeditions. Unfortunately, the old capital of your Kingdom is not at all suited to support the far-reaching journeys. A new city must be built that will facilitate long trips across the ocean. @PAfter all the matters facing the continent of Atlantis were addressed, the Council adjourned with a recitation of the Symphonia Ithikos. By the sacred pact, forged between Atlanteans and the gods by Atlas himself, all Atlanteans pledge to hold high the values of science and knowledge and renounce warfare and bloodshed except in self-defense.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PWith Autoch thriving, it is time to strike out and establish a colony in a new land. Who knows what amazing things will be discovered? Plexaure, one of your trusted advisors, has agreed to watch over Autoch while you set off on a new adventure. @L@PBefore you start your journey, remember that the Symphonia Ithikos only affords you protection from the gods as long as you remain on the continent of Atlantis. Atlanteans in other parts of the world are not immune to attacks by gods and monsters.

message.title: Help from Above
message.content: @PIf Autoch is to become a center of exploration, it must grow larger and more prosperous. Unfortunately, the land around the city isn't very fertile, and Autoch will never become a mighty city unless some alternate sources of food and other necessities can be found. Thankfully, the gods provide for those who cannot provide for themselves. Athena, Demeter and Dionysus all crave your worship and have promised to enrich the land if you build Sanctuaries for them. Of course, immortal King Atlas has always enjoyed putting things together, and he will gladly help you build the Sanctuaries for the other gods if you first build one to honor him.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PWhat beautiful sights there are to see in Autoch. Massive Sanctuaries grace the city, reminding all of the grandeur of the gods. Of course, the gods themselves are frequent visitors and a joy to gaze upon. Who could be sad when Athena, with her brisk, efficient march, blesses Olive Presses and Growers' Lodges? And Demeter, with her overflowing basket, is truly a vision to behold. Then there's Dionysus, majestically stumbling as only he can, toasting the health of all the people he passes. Truly, Autoch is a wonderful place. But, your explorations are not yet done, and you must once again leave Autoch in the hands of Plexaure and build a new city in a far-off land.

message.title: The Grand Collection
message.content: @PThe Council of Atlantis is all abuzz over your latest discoveries. The Mayan artifacts that you brought to Atlantis are wonders to behold, and the Council has decreed that all Atlanteans should see these fantastic pieces for themselves. Unfortunately, Atlantis does not have a building suitable for displaying the entire collection. Therefore, a great museum, which will draw people from all over the ten Kingdoms, must be built. @PThe glee over your latest finds was tempered by some slightly disconcerting news. While you were away founding the colony, Diaprepes and Azaes both began to stockpile massive numbers of weapons in their respective cities. It seems a little unusual, but these two cousins have always been competitive. Maybe they are just having a contest to see who could make the most weapons the fastest. @PMeanwhile, Demeter, in her never-ending quest to find new and interesting crops, has heard of a legendary field, filled with silver-colored stalks of corn called the Argent Maize. In some ways, the Argent Maize reminds Demeter of her daughter, Persephone. Silver calls to mind Hades who, through a cruel trick, forces Persephone to spend half the year with him. The tall, ripe stalks, on the other hand, suggest the summer, when Persephone is once again at her mother's side. So, with longing in her heart, Demeter yearns to have the Argent Maize to call her own, so that she may be reminded of her daughter during the times of the year when Persephone must live in the underworld. Expect Demeter to call upon you to harvest the Argent Maize for her.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe Museum Atlantika towers above the city, and its splendid architecture is, in itself, worthy for inclusion in a museum. The new artifacts retrieved from the Mayans are on display, and Atlanteans from all over the continent have flocked to your city to see the fine Mayan metalwork, the intricately patterned fabric and the remarkable yet simple tools used in everyday Mayan life. The latest exhibit in the Museum is an ear of the Argent Maize that Demeter kindly gave to you in thanks. @PWhile everyone in Atlantis is amazed by your latest discoveries, it won't be long until they yearn for more. The time has come to see what else is in the world.

message.title: The Twin Kingdoms' War
message.content: @PHow could they? How could Azaes and Diaprepes be so rash? Have they forgotten the sacred words of the Symphonia Ithikos, words that they have vowed to uphold to the death? Following some misguided notion, these cousins of yours have decided to declare war on each other, in direct violation of the commands of Poseidon and of the Symphonia Ithikos. Neither will listen to reason, and the other rulers of Atlantis are growing nervous, fearing that the war may soon spread to other kingdoms in Atlantis. So, in defense of the continent, which will surely be devastated if the cousins aren't stopped, an army must be sent to quiet Azaes and Diaprepes.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe war between Azaes and Diaprepes is over, and they have been whisked back to the city of Atlantis, where Atlon will make sure that their differences are resolved before he allows them to resume leading their kingdoms. The soldiers of Autoch performed quite well in the battles, a remarkable feat considering their lack of experience in the ways of war. Hopefully, no other Atlanteans will ever have to know the cruelties of war.

message.title: Water, Water and Urchins
message.subtitle: A small archipelago, situated on prime trade routes.
message.content: @P'Well, hello there my cute little urchin,' Aphrodite purred, blowing you a kiss in greeting. 'Don't you think the land around Biminis is beautiful, just like me? With all the pretty water and... ooh! the urchins! How I love urchins, with their adorable little spines. They're so tasty, too! I simply must have a Sanctuary here, and you are just the one to build it for me!' @PWith that, the goddess disappeared. No one can refuse Aphrodite, and as your assistants scouted around for a suitable place to build the Sanctuary, they noticed signs that the Oceanids had been here. The Oceanids produce all manner of goods, so perhaps they can be convinced to trade with Atlantis.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @P'Thank you very much, my sweet mortal, for my fine Sanctuary,' Aphrodite exclaimed while jumping up and down. 'And, I just love visiting the Fountain of Youth! I think I'm looking younger everyday, and I already looked very young! Soon, I'll look like a baby! Tee hee hee! I'm going to go eat some urchins now. Ta ta!' @PWhy an immortal goddess needs a fountain that grants immortality is beyond the ken of mortals. But if Aphrodite is happy, then everybody is happy. After meal upon meal of urchins, the time has mercifully come to return to Autoch. New trade relationships with the Mayans have been established, and trade with the Oceanids is going swimmingly. Autoch can be sure that it will always have a supply of... urchins. Hooray.

message.title: Land Stained Red
message.subtitle: This mysterious red land glistens in the sun.
message.content: @PCrimson Isle. The very name strikes all Atlanteans with feelings of awe. Back in the early years of Atlantis, only the bravest of heroes ventured onto the island. These heroes told stories of the dangerous monsters, fearsome beasts, earthshaking disasters and amazing orichalc deposits found there. It was on the Crimson Isle that the sacred cornerstone for the Citadel of Poseidon was found, and Achilles himself came here to mine the orichalc upon which the Symphonia Ithikos is inscribed. The time has come to bring civilization to the island and to tame all the wild things.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe Crimson Isle certainly lived up to its billing as a dangerous, wild place. Bellerophon was more than equal to the task of handling Echidna, and he is looking forward to taming some of the other wild beasts on the island. With Bellerophon in residence, the hardy settlers will be able to focus all their time on mining orichalc. The orichalc supply on the island seems never-ending, and no city in Atlantis will ever have to go without the metal again.

message.title: The Glory of Pyramids
message.subtitle: An ideal spot for gorgeous Pyramids.
message.content: @PThe Mayan lands are lacking just one thing: big, beautiful pyramids! Cuello is the perfect place to build a few pyramids, and the Mayans are sure to be astounded by the grandeur of these impressive structures. They'll probably want to learn how to build pyramids of their own, and maybe they'll even adopt our values of peace and science! Regardless, when the Mayans see all the wonderful goods that come from Atlantis, they are bound to want some of their own. @PRumor has it that Ares has been spotted in these parts, and that he has been inciting some Mayans to resist us. Hopefully, Ares and the Mayans won't cause too much trouble.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe mighty Pyramids are amazing sights to behold, and the Mayans are thrilled with them. Already, they are adapting the Atlantean design to build Pyramids of their own. The Mayans are quite pleased with you, and are impressed that you were able to stand up to Ares and his nasty dragon. Even the Mayans who were resistant at first have warmed to us, and have ceased to cause us any trouble. Now, it's time to return to Autoch to tell the people of Atlantis all about our success here.

message.title: In the Name of Science
message.subtitle: The perfect spot to build a research center to foster the free exchange of ideas between the Atlanteans and Mayans.
message.content: @PThe world of the Mayans is unlike any that has been seen before. The rich jungles are full of the most amazing plants and animals - the monkeys are the best. The Mayans share our love for astronomy, and Atlanteans have already learned much from their observations. @PThe ways of the Mayans are still shrouded in mystery. They indulge in ritual human sacrifices that are quite barbaric. They also become quite excited when a child is born with a limp, saying that it is the sign from the great god. Their great god's name is Heff or Hanahpu or something, and they say that he is a master builder, and even built a man made completely of bronze. Their god sounds familiar somehow... @PIf we are to learn all we can about the Mayans, a city must be built here at Copan. Copan will serve as a research center, where Mayans and Atlanteans can come together and discuss ideas. We hope to teach the Mayans much, and trust that we will learn from them in return.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.subtitle: The perfect spot to build a research center to foster the free exchange of ideas between the Atlanteans and Mayans.
message.content: @PHephaestus was incensed when you uncovered his little lie. Imagine, telling the Mayans that he was the supreme god when he knows darn well that Poseidon, Zeus and a host of other gods are above him. The Mayans have been set straight, and Hephaestus has hobbled back to his forge. @PThe research center at Copan is thriving, and the Mayans are teaching us new things about their world every day. In turn, we are sharing Atlantean life with them. But, there are matters in Autoch that require your attention, so it is time to return.

message.title: Adventure Complete
message.content: @PAll is well in Atlantis. New specimens from the Mayan Colonies arrive every day and are prominently displayed in the Museum Atlantika, much to the delight of Atlanteans everywhere. Autoch is a booming center of commerce, and traders from near and far come to the city to ply their wares. And, after years of being at odds, Azaes and Diaprepes have finally resolved their differences. The Symphonia Ithikos is upheld, and the world is at peace.

message.title: Life in the Mediterranean
message.content: The Mediterranean Sea is the final frontier. What people live along its shores, and what resources can be found to enrich life on Atlantis? This adventure is average in difficulty, with 4 parent and 2 colony episodes.

message.title: Entering the Mediterranean
message.content: @P'And so it is resolved,' said Atlon, the High King of Atlantis and head of the Council of Atlantis. 'We must settle the lands to our east to take better advantage of our trade relationship with the Phoenicians. For the first time in hundreds of years, new Atlantean ground will be broken.' As the members of the council cloaked themselves and gathered their belongings in preparation for the ritual bull hunt, they uttered the words of the Symphonia Ithikos by rote. @PThe Phoenicians changed everything in Atlantis. Life here had remained the same since the Mayan colonies were established many, many years ago. No one minds the status quo too much, because everyone's needs are met. That is, they were met until the Phoenicians somehow navigated their ships through the narrow strait that separates the Atlantic Ocean from the Mediterranean Sea and the lands to the east. Everyone here loves the Phoenicians' goods, and the demand for more is high. And so, the Council resolved that a new city be founded at Lixus, on the banks of the narrow strait, to facilitate trade with the Phoenicians. And, they decided that you should be the one to establish the new city. @PSo, to Lixus you go. The strait there is, as advertised, extremely narrow. It is also guarded by the ferocious Scylla. Scylla was once a beautiful nymph pursued by our father, Poseidon. When Amphitrite, Poseidon's wife, got wind of the affair, she turned Scylla into the monster that she is today. No wonder she's mad at Poseidon's people! Atlanteans will never be able to navigate the strait until Scylla is gone and some way is devised to widen the passage.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PHercules isn't called the strongest man alive for nothing! With his bare hands, he single-handedly widened the channel between the Mediterranean Sea and the Atlantic Ocean. The strait, which will forever be known as the Pillars of Hercules in honor of the hero, is still narrow, but it is now navigable. The crafty Odysseus also solved our Scylla problem, and the strait is safe. @PNow, all manner of ships can sail between Atlantis and the lands of the Mediterranean. It won't be long now until Phoenician goods flood Atlantean Agoras.

message.title: Exploring the Sea
message.content: @PThe Phoenicians have already made good use of the newly widened Pillars of Hercules. Now, it's time to follow suit. The lands around the Mediterranean have been settled for a long time, and while the civilizations living there couldn't possibly be as advanced as Atlantean society, they probably still have plentiful goods to offer. An eager band of adventurers has consented to explore the area and forge relationships with the peoples that they meet. In the meantime, Lixus should be built into a bustling city, both to support trade and to impress the foreign cultures that visit the Atlantean city.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe Mediterranean explorations were quite fruitful indeed! Goods flow easily between the Mediterranean nations and Atlantis, and profits in Lixus are way up! As expected, the cultures encountered couldn't hold a candle to the Atlanteans. The Egyptians are much like the Mayans were hundreds of years ago: primitive and in desperate need of Atlantean beneficence. The Greeks, on the other hand, are an entirely different ball of wax. They are, by far, the most haughty civilization, if you can even use that term when referring to them, that we have ever met. After displaying our superior knowledge and showing them our excellent Atlantean goods, the Greeks ordered us off their land while making threatening motions with their spears. It's so sad when an entire culture is too insecure to realize that a superior people can only help them. @PMeanwhile, the Phoenicians have taken great advantage of the widening of the Pillars of Hercules. They have criss-crossed the Atlantic, even trading with our Mayans directly. We're certainly glad that Atlantis can be of such a great help to those money-centered Phoenicians. @PNow that we know what is out there in the Mediterranean, it is time to establish an Atlantean colony further to the east to increase profits from trade.

message.title: Phoenician Strife
message.content: @PEnough is enough! The Phoenicians have taken complete advantage of us, usurping our trade relationships with the Mayans and even disrupting trade on Atlantis! They have cut us almost completely out of the trade equation, which is unfathomable, given that we were the ones that opened up the Pillars of Hercules in the first place. If the Phoenicians refuse to honor our centuries-long relationships with the Mayans, then we must do what we can to defend ourselves from this Phoenician threat to our continued prosperity. We have already taken the step of charging a toll for passing through the Pillars of Hercules, and some Phoenicians have quite rationally agreed to pay us. But, the city of Carthage flouts our authority and, in addition to refusing to pay the toll, has taken to piracy! They have boarded our ships and stolen our goods! If the pirates of Carthage continue to disrupt trade, it won't be long until Atlanteans everywhere are without the basic goods they need to survive. We spoke to the more reasonable Phoenicians about their rebellious countrymen, but they have refused to intervene. Though we Atlanteans are a peaceful people, we will not brook a threat to our homeland. We will teach Carthaginians that we Atlanteans are to be respected and obeyed. It is for their own good, and the good of Atlantis. @PAres has heard of our plight. Knowing that we are not as skilled in the ways of war as some other, more barbaric cultures are, the god has agreed to help us put Carthage in its proper place, provided we show him the respect that he deserves.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PCarthage has now fallen in line, like the rest of the Phoenicians. Now, all Phoenician traders are respectfully paying the toll, understanding that what is good for Atlantis is good for everyone. Just in case any Phoenician has any question about the toll, one of our many frigates out on the waters is sure to answer it for him. The Oceanids, however, are refusing to pay the toll and have ceased trading with us. The Oceanids have always been a little odd, and we won't miss their goods. @PA second colony along the Mediterranean will cement our position with these new-found cultures.

message.title: Plague
message.content: @PThe Mediterranean is pleasant enough, but it's no Atlantis. Our efforts to civilize Egypt have gone quite well, and the Egyptians are slowly adopting our ways. The Phoenicians haven't caused any trouble since Carthage was taught a lesson, and trade is flourishing. But the Greeks! They have proven to be even more primitive than we had first thought. They have continued to rebuff our efforts to introduce them to Atlantean life. Don't they understand that adopting our ways will only make their lives easier? It's too bad about the Greeks, really. Not only are they primitive, they are dim-witted, too. Then, there are those horrid Centaurs. Thank Atlas that they have decided to leave us alone. @PLixus is doing quite well, and goods are flowing freely into and out of Atlantis. Still, there is a foreboding sense of danger ahead. Many of the traders that have arrived here lately have looked a little peaked, and some of them report that a plague is spreading around the east. The sickness has decimated the populations of many cities, and some cities are functioning only on their most basic levels, barely providing food to their residents. It certainly wouldn't be surprising that illness would break out, especially given the squalid conditions that some of the people around there live in. Well, that particular bridge will be crossed when we come to it. In the meantime, the needs of Lixus must be addressed. We must continue to be prosperous and productive to serve the needs of Atlantis.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe plague was much worse than feared, and it decimated many Mediterranean cities. Thank Poseidon, Lixus escaped any serious harm, as did our homeland on Atlantis. Trade with the east is slowly being reestablished, but goods from the east are much harder to come by. Our eastern trade partners claim that the plague wiped out a large portion of their population, and that they just can't produce as much as they used to. If only these people were more quick to learn, they would be masters of Atlantean efficiency and wouldn't be having these problems. @PSuspiciously, the Greeks seem to have escaped this plague completely unharmed. They threw themselves upon the mercy of Apollo, and that nursemaid of a god apparently took pity on them. Or, perhaps the Greeks escaped the plague through pure, dumb luck. That would be typical of them. Still, it will only be a matter of time before we Atlanteans, with our superior culture, whip the Greeks into shape. They cannot resist our beneficial ways forever.

message.title: Showing the Way
message.subtitle: A land of fertile river banks surrounded by desert, amongst a people that would benefit from our knowledge.
message.content: @PThe Egyptians seem to be a fairly bright people, but they desperately need our help. On Atlantis, we dedicate ourselves to the surety of science. In Egypt, the people give themselves up to the vagaries of a river. Their entire lives depend upon the flooding of the Nile, and if it doesn't flood exactly as anticipated, the Egyptians are lost. Granted, the Egyptians have not had many problems producing massive amounts of wheat thus far, but it will only be a matter of time before the flood fails and the Egyptian people starve. @PTo lift the Egyptians out of their primitive state, we must show them the glory of Atlantean culture. A city at Saqqara that showcases the best of Atlantean architecture will greatly impress the simple Egyptians. Once we capture their attention, we will have no trouble instructing them on the proper way to live.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe Egyptians have already learned a lot from us. They are awed by our fantastic pyramids, and we have left a few Atlanteans behind to serve as advisors to them on their construction projects, as well as on other aspects of Atlantean life. In return for showing them how to build wondrous pyramids, the Egyptians have agreed to supply Atlantis with wheat at a reasonable price. Egypt is all we could have asked for.

message.title: Near the Hellenes
message.subtitle: Located on the borders of Greek territory, this site may give Atlanteans inroads to Greece.
message.content: @PIf a child refuses to take a spoonful of honey, then only the child suffers. If a man refuses a generous gift of jewels from a loyal friend, then only the man suffers. The Greeks have refused the sweetness and richness of Atlantean life, and only the Greeks suffer. There is a limit to Atlantean patience. We have extended our friendship and our help to the Greeks time and again, and time and again they have refused. So be it. It makes no difference to us. @PStill, the Atlantean desire to help is strong. A city will be built here in Syracuse, on the outskirts of Greek territory. Perhaps if the Greeks see for themselves the greatness of Atlantean culture, they will mend their ways and join us. But, judging by what we know of the Greeks so far, that is unlikely. Alas, it is not in the Atlantean nature to give up easily, so try we must.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PHorrors! Who would have thought that all the old stories about the ancient times in Atlantis were completely true? We have seen Centaurs, and they are every bit as ugly as legend describes. The barbarians attacked us, but we dispatched them easily enough. In fact, at the sight of the Atlantean emblem on our armor, they began cowering in fear. They didn't bother us too much again. @PSome of the softer Atlanteans among us felt sorry for the Centaurs, and declared that they would right a past wrong. Envoy after envoy went to Centaur territory to propose peace, but none ever came back. What else can we do? @PThe Greeks are still resisting us, and are none-too-happy that we are near their land. As our immortal first king Atlas would have said, 'Like it or lump it.'

message.title: Adventure Complete
message.content: @PAs we reestablish trade with cities in the Mediterranean, we have taken special care to teach the people better hygiene practice. It is, after all, the Atlantean thing to do. They are bound to be extremely grateful and increase the flow of goods as much as is practicable. It is refreshing to see that so many of the people in the Mediterranean have so quickly adopted the spirit of Atlantean law. @PThen, there are the Greeks. These stubborn people will just not listen to reason, or perhaps they just don't understand reason. No one has ever resisted us before, and we are at a loss to understand why the Greeks are resisting us now. Ah, well. @PThankfully, the Centaurs are leaving us alone. They are far too unpleasant to gaze upon, and if the Greeks can't understand the Atlantean way, then the half-animal Centaurs will be completely confused by us. They are not worth our effort. @PRegardless, the Mediterranean project is a smashing success, and the majority of the area is under our influence. We are masters of the Mediterranean Sea.

message.title: Atlantis Reborn
message.content: Hard times have fallen on Atlantis. Food and goods are hard to come by, and its people struggle to survive. This adventure is difficult and consists of six parent city episodes and two colonies.

message.title: Reconstruction
message.content: @PDateline - the Mediterranean. The great plague that has laid waste to many of the lands around the Mediterranean is over, but its crippling effects remain. The streets of Egypt and Phoenicia are littered with the remains of the unfortunate dead. The many farms and workshops that were once filled with happy and industrious workers are silent, and very few goods and foods are being produced. @PThe effects of the plague are not limited to the Mediterranean. In Atlantis, the lack of Egyptian and Phoenician products is taking a toll. The shelves of Atlantean Agoras are nearly bare, and people from Gades to Autoch are waiting in long lines for the goods that they so desperately need. Spirits are sinking fast, and many lament that Atlantis will never again see the glory of its golden years. @PTo salve his people's wounded spirits, Atlon, our glorious High King of Atlantis, has sent his eldest child to the eastern-most region of Atlantis. There, a great city will be built, which will embody the best of the Atlantean yesteryear. The city will be called Cleitos, in honor of the mother of our immortal king Atlas, Cleito. The people of Atlantis will be able to point to this city with pride and know that Atlantis still reigns supreme.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PDateline - Cleitos. Atlanteans everywhere are dancing and singing in the streets, for Cleitos truly is a remarkable city. It is a bastion of science, and people from all over the ten kingdoms clamor to see the mighty city for themselves. @PBut, what's this? Trouble with our Egyptian friends? It seems that the Egyptians, who owe much to the brave explorers who brought Atlantean knowledge to the Nile's shores, are withholding much-needed wheat from Atlantis, and have been raising the prices on goods important to Atlantean survival. Great King Atlon himself has vowed to pay a visit to our Egyptian friends to remind them of all the wonderful things that Atlanteans have brought them.

message.title: The Greater Mediterranean Co-Prosperity Sphere
message.content: @PDateline - Saqqara. Bushel upon bushel of tender stalks of Egyptian wheat sit on the docks, ready to be sent to Atlantis. Atlanteans have the all-powerful King Atlon to thank for this bounty. Escorted by a fleet of mighty frigates, our king journeyed down the Nile to meet with the Egyptians. Together, they discussed all the benefits that the Egyptians have already reaped from their relationship with Atlantis. Noting their error in judgement, the Egyptians quickly revised their exportation policies and agreed to turn over their surpluses of wheat at a most reasonable price. In a gesture of goodwill, King Atlon promised the Egyptians that Atlantis would continue to sell its finest goods to them. With the influx of Egyptian supplies, life in Atlantis is slowly beginning to return to normal. Still, some goods are scarce, and the cities of the ten kingdoms are turning to Cleitos to provide for them. @PMeanwhile, in the dangerous waters of the Mediterranean Sea, vile Carthaginians have boarded yet another Atlantean trade ship. Roughly tossing aside our brave merchants, the Carthaginians have seized cargo, stealing food from the mouths of Atlantean babes. The plague has been hard on the people of Carthage, and they have reverted to their old, barbaric ways. The other cities in Phoenicia refuse to call a halt to Carthage's insolent behavior and have mounted an insurrection of their own, increasing the selling prices of their goods to astronomical heights. The king has asked his capable and daring eldest child, the ruler of Cleitos, to address the Phoenician issue. @PThe treacherous Mediterranean is offering even more trouble. The peoples around the Aegean who have not seen the wisdom of Atlantean ways are stirring and seem to be contemplating aggression towards Atlantis as well. Though mighty Atlantis has little to fear from the primitive Greeks, Centaurs and Amazons, King Atlon himself is casting a wary eye towards them and may personally step in to stop this latest threat to Atlantean well-being.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PDateline - Carthage. The Carthaginians are again seeing reason, thanks to our astute military men. They have sworn to forego piracy, and all the cities of Phoenicia have been persuaded to sell their goods at more reasonable prices. Order in the Atlantean world is restored. @PMeanwhile, the people of Atlantis have gathered to wish a bon voyage to King Atlon. The King, impressively adorned in a peacock-feather raiment, is sailing to Greece. There, he will reason with king Pelops of Argos, to convince him that Greece will reap great rewards if it joins with Atlantis.

message.title: Night Falls on Atlantis
message.content: @PDateline - Atlantis. Sorrowful Atlanteans from throughout the ten kingdoms have journeyed to the city of Atlantis for the funeral of our great King Atlon, who died in pursuit of peace. He once again tried to show the Greeks that uniting with us would make their lives much more fruitful and fulfilling. The Greeks stubbornly refused to listen and, cursing loudly and taking up their spears, chased King Atlon from their lands. On his way back from meeting with King Pelops, our most benevolent king was foully struck down by a hideous Centaur. As he was taken into custody, the Centaur assassin snidely claimed that he thought that our most exalted king was a peacock! @PAlong the funeral procession route, Atlanteans' grief is mitigated only by their outrage over this most heinous crime. Damophilos, a miner from Mestonia, echoed the thoughts of many Atlanteans, 'The Greeks must be behind the murder of our noble king! They were the only ones who knew that the peace-loving King Atlon was in the Aegean! It would be just like the Greeks to conspire with the misshapen Centaurs!' @PSo, as our glorious king is laid to rest, Atlanteans everywhere call for the destruction of Argos. Only when Argos is gone will Atlantis be safe from the Greek menace. Some Atlanteans are turning to our immortal king Atlas for guidance, and others are turning to the king's eldest child, the magnificent ruler of Cleitos, to thwart Greek aggression. Our soldiers at the outpost of Knossos are preparing themselves, in case they are called upon to address the Greek problem.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PDateline - Hyperborea. Grunting and grimacing under the weight, the hero Hercules holds up the world, freeing our immortal king Atlas. Having been tricked by Atlas into taking up the burden, the hero could be heard saying, 'Why couldn't I have a little less brawn and a little more brain?' @PWith the weight of the world off his shoulders, Atlas marched to Greece to help the Atlantean cause. After Argos was defeated by the Atlantean army, Atlas destroyed the city completely. The Greeks are running scared and have scattered to the more mountainous regions of their land. Even our ancient enemies, the Centaurs, are in hiding. @PNews of our smashing victory in Greece quickly spread throughout Atlantis, and people are again in the streets, celebrating the glory of our well-trained army and of our immortal king. All say that this momentous victory marks the rebirth of the Atlantean golden age! @PAnd so, on the piers of Cleitos, ships are being prepared to sail forth into the Mediterranean. A colony will be established to help ensure Atlantis' continued peace and prosperity.

message.title: Benevolent Ares
message.content: @PDateline - Cleitos. Storm clouds once again threaten the fine people of Atlantis. Goods are again scarce, and people are beginning to go hungry. People fear that our weakened state will prove irresistible to our foes, and they will once again threaten Atlantean peace. @PIn Atlantis' darkest hour, the god Ares, like a beam of radiant sunshine, has come to our rescue. In a secret location near Cleitos, he is working with our scientists, developing a super weapon that will defend Atlantis' shores from all comers. All Ares asks in return is that a Sanctuary be built in his honor. @PThe weapon is already almost complete, but it is missing one key component. Ares says that only a brave and agile hero will be able to retrieve the final piece of the weapon from deep in the heart of Africa.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PDateline - Cleitos. Oh, the humanity! Chaos! Chaos in the streets of Cleitos, and in the city of Atlantis. @PSomehow, a single, rogue Greek infiltrated Cleitos defenses and - oh, unspeakable horror - happened upon our best scientists, who were just about to complete Ares' secret weapon. Cruelly, this Greek infidel slaughtered our scientists, all of whom died heroes' deaths in defense of Atlantis. Then - gods help us - the brigand aimed the weapon at our heart, the city of Atlantis, and fired! In the aftermath, the Greek scoundrel managed to escape. @PIn Cleitos, clean-up of the carnage is just beginning. The bodies of the dead, which are scattered about on the floor like a child's rag dolls, are being prepared for proper burial. And, in the center of the room where the secret weapon stands, workers are dismayed to discover that the Greek dog has damaged the weapon! Some mysterious, sticky substance has clogged the gears! As the science world prepares to mourn its dead, scientists are already hard at work trying to decipher their fallen comrades' notes. @PIn the city of Atlantis, the unhappy target of the secret weapon, people are shell-shocked and outraged. The Citadel of Poseidon, the magnificent Sanctuary honoring the father of all Atlanteans, is no more. What was once a beautiful building is now a heap of rubble, and the sacred tablet inscribed with the Symphonia Ithikos has cracked down the middle. Atlanteans everywhere shudder to think of the damage that would have resulted had the weapon been finished. @PAmidst this great tragedy, Atlanteans are once again rising up to move forward. The docks of Cleitos are busy, preparing ships to set sail to a new colony site.

message.title: Defending Atlantis
message.content: @PDateline - Cleitos. Atlanteans prepare for war. Soldiers are sharpening their spears and polishing their armor as they pack their belongings for their journey into the Mediterranean. On the home front, men, women and children are doing their parts to ensure Atlantis' success against the Greek horde. Families are doing their best to make their supplies stretch, but food and goods will only stretch so far. Demand for more remains high. @PAlong our coasts, the waters of the Mediterranean are surging through the Pillars of Hercules, lapping at our shores. There are gods at work here. The Greeks are Zeus' people, and he is pushing the waters back towards Atlantis, in what is sure to be a futile attempt to prevent our ships from sailing to Greece. Certainly, our father Poseidon will not stand for Zeus' usurpation of his watery realm. Poseidon will be avenged. @PYet, our mission remains clear. Shoulder to shoulder, Atlanteans march in defense of Atlantis. They march to free our brethren in Carthage and Memphis who are cruelly subjugated by the Greek menace. They march to safeguard our people from the hated Centaurs who, throughout our history, have always sought to oppress us. They march knowing that one day soon, the people of Greece will no longer stand in Atlantis' way. When their march is complete, future Atlanteans will never know hardship and will be able to live in freedom and peace.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PDateline - the Mediterranean Sea. After long and hard-fought battles around the Mediterranean, weary Atlantean soldiers are making their way home. Their noble efforts have not gone unrewarded. Thanks to their bravery, Greece's grip on our friends in Egypt and Phoenicia is loosened, and the Greeks have retreated all the way back to their homeland. Even the ill-formed Centaurs have been forced from their city in Mount Aulip and are hiding deep within the mountains. @PScientists on the home front have nearly finished repairs on the secret weapon. Soon, it will be time to fire it at Mycenae and thwart the Greek threat forever.

message.title: The End of the Threat
message.content: @PDateline - an orange grove on Olympus. 'People of Atlantis, hear my voice. I have watched as my husband has left my side for Greece, to cavort with the maidens there. Day after day, year after year, he has forgotten his duty to me, his wife. I will stand for this no longer. To rid myself of the pesky and attractive Greeks, I will help you in your war. I will divert Zeus' attention so that you can use your secret weapon against the hated Greeks. But, to keep Zeus completely distracted, I will need the services of the hero Jason. When I am ready to set my plan in motion, I will visit you.' @PWith Hera's words in their hearts, Atlantean soldiers are again ready to strike out into the Mediterranean to remove the Greek threat once and for all. Sailing the seas, their chests puffed out with Atlantean pride, they know that the end is near and that they will soon be able to return to their homes for good. The secret weapon is aimed and at the ready. The scientists are only waiting for the command to fire it upon Mycenae. After the weapon is fired, brave Atlantean soldiers will march into Greece to extinguish the Greek threat once and for all.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PDateline - Cleitos. 'Huzzah! Huzzah! All hail the mighty Atlantean army! All hail the brilliant Atlantean scientists! All hail the powerful gods!' Happy shouting fills the streets of all Atlantean cities today! The Greeks are defeated once and for all, and Atlantis is again safe! @PAlready, plentiful supplies have been distributed through Atlantis, and Atlantean homemakers no longer need to make goods stretch. Andromache, the wife of an Atlantean charioteer, had this to say: 'Thank the gods that there is finally enough meat to go around. I was running out of things to do with oranges. Orange a la king, orange casserole, orange surprise, orange tetrazzini... if I never have another orange, it'll be too soon.' @POur men returning from the front report that the weapon caused significant destruction throughout Greece. Said one soldier: 'The weapon did an astounding amount of damage. On our way to Mycenae, we passed streams of bedraggled men and women whose homes had been destroyed. The cities that we passed through were in ruins, obliterated by the chain of earthquakes and tidal waves that the weapon set off. Mycenae itself was in shambles. The city was ablaze, and there were gaping holes in its Walls. Thanks to the weapon - and to science - defeating the Greeks was much easier than it could have been, sir!' @PAnd so, the world begins to clean up the mess that the war made and start anew. Atlantis is on the verge of a new golden age!

message.title: Just When You Thought It Was Safe...
message.subtitle: Located near Greece, this site is the perfect spot for a fortified city.
message.content: @PDateline - Thera. The news from the Mediterranean is bleak, but Atlanteans are doing their best to keep their spirits up. The pestilent Greeks have regrouped and, with the help of the ignoble Centaurs and Amazons, have swarmed through the Mediterranean, conquering city after city. Those dastardly Greeks completely destroyed the beautiful Atlantean city of Knossos. Refugees from the city tell of the harrowing experience: 'There I was, asleep in my bed, when some brute knocked down the door to my house. He said his name was Achilles, and that he was here to send the Atlantean cur home. I assured him that I was home, but he didn't listen. I just barely escaped with my life!' @PHere on Thera, preparations are underway to build a fortified city. Our fine Atlantean soldiers will be able to sail from Thera to the Greek mainland when the time comes to end the Greek threat and free our Phoenician and Egyptian friends from Greek tyranny. @PThe journey to Thera was difficult, and it was only due to the superior firepower of Atlantean frigates that we arrived on the island safely. Ordinary merchant ships are not as successful sailing through the treacherous Mediterranean, so goods from home may be hard to come by. Thera will need to fend for itself.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PDateline - Thera. The intimidating fortress here is a testament to Atlantean military might. Not even the most foolhardy Greek would dare attack it. @PBack on the home front, things have taken a turn for the worse. Even the richest Atlantean, forced to wear old and tattered clothes due to a fleece shortage, is beginning to look like a beggar. Hungry children roam the streets, looking for the smallest crumb of food. As long as Greece has Phoenicia and Egypt under its boot, Atlanteans will continue to suffer.

message.title: Hope Among the Ruins
message.subtitle: A rich and fertile land that can serve as Atlantis' bread basket.
message.content: @PDateline - on the waters that were once Autoch. There is nothing left. The entire kingdom of Autoch and all the Atlanteans living there have sunk beneath the sea, never to be seen again. Atlantis is again in mourning, grieving over the loss of the fine people of Autoch. @PWho's to blame for this tragedy? Hephaestus, the lackey of the Greeks. The bandy-legged god of volcanoes caused a massive eruption at the center of Crimson Isle, an eruption more furious than any recorded by Atlantean scholars. A flood of molten lava swept over Crimson Isle, and nothing but charred ashes remains. After the eruption, tidal wave after tidal wave pounded the coast of Autoch until the whole region finally succumbed to the sea. @PNow, Atlantis is completely cut off from our Mayan friends to the west, and Atlantis is deprived of the Mayan goods that we have come to rely on over the years. Without these valuable goods, Atlantean cities are suffering. Workshops have shut down due to the loss of raw materials, and hunger has become a constant companion in some cities. @PYet, take solace, Atlanteans! The new city at Malaca will provide! Certainly, it won't be long until the wise ruler of Cleitos has the city up and running, and the overflow of goods will be quickly sent back to Atlantis! Hold on a little longer, Atlanteans!

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PDateline - Cleitos. The city of Cleitos has always been a welcome sight to poor Atlantean eyes. And now, with the bounty of goods sent from Malaca, Cleitos is truly a vision of hope. @PAtlanteans across the continent are praying to the gods that Atlantis has seen its darkest hours. The kingdom of Mestonia was shaken to its very core by an intense earthquake, and the people living there have evacuated the kingdom, flooding into other Atlantean cities. The leaders of the Atlanteans cities are keeping the immigrants fed, clothed and employed, but everyone will breathe easier when some other sources of much-needed food and goods are found.

message.title: Adventure Complete
message.content: @PDateline - Atlantis. A new day has dawned, and the ten kingdoms of Atlantis are in full bloom. Well-fed children play in the city's streets, and Atlantean men and women are able to devote their lives to scientific pursuits. In the city of Atlantis, the great Citadel of Poseidon is being rebuilt and is more glorious than it had been before. Throughout the Mediterranean, happy Egyptians and Phoenicians work hard for the greater glory of Atlantis, providing Atlantean industries with the raw materials that they need to produce exquisite goods. With the Greeks and Centaurs gone, there is nothing left to fear. Atlantis is at peace, and the new Golden Age has begun!

message.title: Proetus and Bellerophon
message.content: A good leader keeps promises made to allies and old friends. Unfortunately, keeping promises can have some unpleasant consequences. This adventure is easy and consists of six parent city episodes and one colony episode.

message.title: Boys Will Be Boys
message.content: @P'Proetus always gets the bigger piece. It's not fair,' Acrisius whined when he heard his father's news. After dozens of years of skilled leadership, King Abas, was stepping aside and dividing his kingdom between his twin sons. Proetus indeed received the bigger piece, having been given the lands of Tiryns, Heraeum and Midea. Acrisius received the kingship of Argos, the prestigious capital city of the kingdom. 'Now listen, sons,' Abas said. 'In addition to ruling over the lands, you must also honor all the pacts that I have made with fellow leaders during my kingship. This includes honoring the promise to protect Glaucus, king of Corinth.' @PYou, too, have a pact with King Abas. Long ago, when both you and Abas were in your youths, you promised to always look after each other's lands and progeny. Hopefully, Abas' sons will be as faithful to the vow as Abas was himself. Acrisius and Proetus' help could be invaluable as you prepare to establish a new city at Lycia. Lycia would be an ideal place to found a city, if it weren't for some undesirable neighbors. Hostile tribes of Amazons live nearby, and the people of Solymi resent all foreign intrusions. Then, there's the small matter of the fierce Chimera, who has been spotted in the area. Having the King's sons on your side would make facing these challenges much easier. Perhaps one of your daughters would be willing to enter into marriage with one of Abas' sons and solidify the union between the two families. Certainly, it's a matter to be considered as you begin to construct Lycia.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThough the town of Lycia has begun to thrive, trouble abounds in the world. Chimera is making life miserable in the nearby countryside, and some fear that she is heading straight for Lycia. In Argos, King Abas has finally succumbed to death. His sons, rather than embracing each other in grief, have deepened the rift between them. Giving into his greed, Acrisius has ousted Proetus from the lands that his father bequeathed to him. Proetus has come to Lycia and, calling upon the pledge that you made to his father so many years ago, has asked for your protection and help in reclaiming what is rightfully his. In the wake of King Abas' passing, how can you refuse?

message.title: In Memory of Abas
message.content: @PThe celebration of the wedding between Proetus and your daughter, Stheneoboea, was dampened only by a sense of injustice. Acrisius still has not relented and holds Proetus' lands in his jealous grip. The time has come to restore Proetus to his kingdom, and for your daughter to live as a queen. Since gentle entreaties to Acrisius have failed, perhaps less gentle arguments will have more sway with the petulant boy. If Acrisius and Proetus cannot take it upon themselves to fulfill their father's wish that his kingdom be divided between them, then, in honor of the dead king, you will see to it that Abas' instructions are carried out.
