When you have set things straight, Proetus will again lead Tiryns, Heraeum and Midea, and Acrisius will lead Argos.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PAt last, order has been returned to the world. Proetus is again in control of his kingdom, though the city of Heraeum was destroyed in the fighting. Acrisius has retained control of Argos, as was his due, but he is not particularly pleased with your role in the proceedings, even calling you a 'meddling old dodger!' Glaucus of Corinth, who has allied himself with Acrisius, is also determined to oppose you. Perhaps, with time, ruffled feathers can be smoothed over. @PProetus and your daughter have settled comfortably into their new home at Tiryns. Yet, Proetus has revealed to you that he is still uneasy. Tiryns is still vulnerable to attack, and it is only a matter of time before Acrisius or his ally, Glaucus of Corinth, mounts another charge against the city. Only walls built by the famed Cyclopes could possibly defend Tiryns, but the Cyclopes have been completely unresponsive to Proetus' requests. Hera appeared to Proetus and offered to serve as an intermediary... provided that something is done for the goddess in return. That's when Proetus remembered the old pact made between you and his father so many years ago.

message.title: A Question of Etiquette
message.content: @P'More wine,' Bellerophon bellowed as he gnawed on the bones of some unfortunate beast. 'Hurry up now, chop chop!' For nine long days and nine long nights, the peaceful quiet of Lycia has been interrupted at frequent intervals by shouted demands of 'More wine' and 'More beast.' Just who is this confounded Bellerophon, anyway? After helping him atone for his misdeeds, Proetus sent him packing here to Lycia in quite a hurry. Ever since, the lout has been consuming food and wine at an alarming rate, flirting with your daughters and offending those with more delicate sensibilities. It was while he was draining yet another amphora of wine that Bellerophon slapped his forehead and proclaimed, 'Oh, yeah! I was supposed to give you this note from Proetus!' Finally, some explanation for why Proetus sent you this dubious gift. The contents of the note, however, did not make matters much clearer. It read, 'Please do me a favor and kill the person who hands you this note.' @PProetus neglected to add, 'Remember the oath you made to my father,' but at this point, that goes without saying. Rules of etiquette prohibit you from killing Bellerophon, a guest in your home, outright. If only Bellerophon could accidentally fall off a roof, or perhaps someone's sword could slip and - completely by mistake - just happen to run him through. Or, maybe he could be convinced to take on Chimera, who has been such a headache to everyone around Lycia. @PAfter describing Chimera to Bellerophon, and underscoring just how famous he would become if he managed to kill the beast, Bellerophon eagerly agreed to the challenge. He claimed to have a plan and was ready to take the first step. Of course, there was one caveat. There's always a caveat. A home must be built for him in Lycia, and it must be stocked with the best wine and other desirable sundries. One does what one must do.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PUnbelievable. Truly unbelievable. Bellerophon has come flying into the city on the back of the mighty Pegasus! Athena apparently likes this obnoxious young man and told him of a Golden Bridle that could break the winged steed. Still, maybe Chimera will manage to kill him anyway. @PSeeing Bellerophon dead has become even more important now. Proetus sent along another note, inquiring about the health of Bellerophon, and relaying that the rogue had the gall to make advances toward Stheneboea. Being the virtuous woman that she is, she of course refused him. Just thinking about that coarse, disgusting excuse for a man suggesting anything untoward to the gentle, refined Stheneboea.... It will be a welcome day indeed when Chimera mauls him to death!

message.title: If You Can't Beat Him, Join Him
message.content: @PBellerophon announced, 'I am nearly ready to defeat the ferocious Chimera and take my rightful place among the famous heroes of Greece! But, before I undertake this most amazing of feats, I demand... nay, I insist... that you outfit another Hall for me!' If building him a second home will quicken his departure from the earth, then a second home it is. @PMeanwhile, your daughter Philonoe has been spending quite a lot of time in Bellerophon's company, and she claims that Stheneboea is lying about Bellerophon. Philonoe maintains that Stheneboea tried to seduce Bellerophon and Bellerophon gallantly resisted her. Regardless of who is lying and who is telling the truth, the sooner that Bellerophon is removed from the city, the better. There are other pressing matters facing you. The Amazon and Solymi threats have escalated, and they must be dealt with forcefully. Maybe, if by some miracle Bellerophon defeats Chimera, he can be sent to war against the Amazons and Solymis. The Amazons are pretty good shots, after all.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PBellerophon just won't die. Against all odds, he defeated Chimera without even receiving so much as a scratch! He didn't accidentally get in the way of an Amazon arrow or Solymi spear. Even some of your own soldiers, sensing your disdain for Bellerophon, tried killing the cad, but even they were unsuccessful! Bellerophon couldn't possibly be one of the immortals, but it certainly is beginning to seem that way. @PNow, Bellerophon has approached you to ask for your daughter Philonoe's hand in marriage. How can you refuse a man that has killed the most ferocious monster seen in Greece for some time, successfully dodged the spears and arrows of two enemies, and outfoxed your own soldiers' plan to kill him? If you did refuse, Bellerophon would probably find a way to marry Philonoe anyway. Oh, well. Maybe allying yourself with this seemingly indestructible man may bring you benefits after all. Proetus will just have to be satisfied with the good effort made to kill Bellerophon.

message.title: Revenge
message.content: @PJust as things settle down, they stir up again. Proetus has sent yet another note, and, as always, his note did not contain good news. Of all the women in Greece, Dionysus offered Proetus' daughters - your granddaughters - the honor of entering into his cult. Foolishly, your granddaughters refused, fearing the effects of drinking too much wine. Now, Dionysus has driven your granddaughters mad, and they are roving the countryside, raving like lunatics. Fortunately, a wise doctor named Melampus knows how to cure the women, but his price is quite high. Proetus doesn't have the money and, citing that cursed oath, has asked you to raise the funds. @PHere in Lycia, preparations are under way for the marriage of Philonoe and Bellerophon. Philonoe, in her sweetest, most pleasing voice, has asked that you build another home for Bellerophon in the city. After all, she said, Bellerophon has been living a bachelor's life for some time and, well, you know how bachelors are about keeping up their houses! She said that cleaning out Bellerophon's Hall would be harder than cleaning the Augean Stables! How can you say no to your adorable daughter. @PNot everything at home is happy, however. Echidna, incensed over the death of her daughter, Chimera, is slithering toward the city, intent on revenge.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PBellerophon may not be a bad person to have around after all! He defeated Echidna without even breaking a sweat, and the city is safe from the monster's wrath! Now, he has been overheard saying that for Philonoe's sake, he wants to resolve his problems with Sthenoboea. Maybe those two will work out their troubles yet. @PDoctor Melampus, touched by your devotion to your granddaughters, has said that he will waive his usual fee if, in return, he is allowed to marry the fairest of the granddaughters. Your granddaughter could do worse than to be a doctor's wife.

message.title: The Wheel of Fortune Spins
message.content: @PA tragedy has struck. Hopes were very high when Bellerophon, in what seemed to be a friendly gesture, offered to take Stheneoboea for a ride on Pegasus. As the pair soared upward, Pegasus suddenly bucked, and beautiful Stheneoboea plunged to her death. Ever since Bellerophon slipped the Golden Bridle onto Pegasus, the winged horse has been as docile as a sheep. Could Bellerophon have caused Pegasus to buck, or was it just an unfortunate accident as Bellerophon claims? @PPerhaps there will be some good news yet to emerge from all this grief and sorrow. At long last, Melampus has revealed the cure for your insane granddaughters: build a Sanctuary to Apollo, the God of Healing. Surely, Apollo will look upon your granddaughters with pity and cure them of their ailment. @PMeanwhile, Bellerophon, with sword rattling, has had the gall to accuse you of trying to kill him! He says that it is all clear to him: Chimera, Echidna, your own soldiers' attempted ambush... he claims that the list goes on an on. He has threatened that if you do not build another home for him, he will make your life most unpleasant once he assumes his seat on Olympus. Assumes his seat on Olympus? Maybe soaring to such great heights on the back of Pegasus has robbed Bellerophon's brain of some much-needed oxygen, because he sounds insane. Refusing a dangerous, crazy man his wish would be futile and potentially deadly. Maybe building him another hall would quiet him.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe Wheel of Fortune has finally spun, and those who were once on the bottom are now at the top, and those who were at the top are now at the bottom. At long last, the news from Proetus is good! Building a Sanctuary to Apollo, as Melampus had suggested, worked, and now your granddaughters have full possession of their senses. As promised, your fairest granddaughter has wed Melampus and, as a wedding gift, Proetus has given Melampus one-third of his kingdom. @PBellerophon, too, has experienced a reversal of fortune. The brash man thought that he belonged with the gods on Mount Olympus, and he was led to believe that he had Hera's support. Little did he know that Hera had had quite enough of his shenanigans, and that she knew Zeus would rapidly punish a mortal who dared approach the home of the gods. As surely as Helios drives the sun across the sky each day, Zeus indeed quickly put Bellerophon back in his place. The mighty god sent a gadfly, which bit Pegasus on the hind quarter. Reeling from the sting of the bite, Pegasus reared back, throwing Bellerophon off. Bellerophon plunged back to earth but, as usual, managed not to die. Now, Bellerophon, bitter and broken, is wandering Greece alone. Thanks to the gods, he has finally left Lycia for good.

message.title: The Favor
message.subtitle: Almost everyone has deserted the ruins of Heraeum, everyone but one resident famous the world over for her unique hairstyle.
message.content: @PWhen Proetus mentioned that he needed a favor, and that it involved Hera, you might have guessed that you would find yourself here in Heraeum to rebuild the goddess' city and to dedicate a Sanctuary to her. At least Heraeum has plentiful supplies of marble and some wood available to use for constructing the edifice. But, as always in Greece, nothing can ever be entirely good. The deadly Medusa has taken up residence here and threatens to cause problems. Luckily, Perseus, the famous hero, has agreed to take care of the snake-haired monster, provided that you build him a fine lodge outfitted with his favorite things.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe goddess Hera is thrilled with her new Sanctuary and, as promised, has convinced the Cyclopes to build walls for Tiryns. Proetus is thrilled and extremely thankful for your help, and has even done you the honor of comparing you to his own father. With the restoration of Heraeum, old Abas' wishes have finally been carried out to the letter. @PAbas would have been proud of Proetus, who has been acting the part of a good king. Your daughter reports that Proetus has taken in the most beautiful young man, a son of Glaucus of Corinth. The man had accidentally killed his brother, and Proetus has agreed to help him atone for his sin. @PMeanwhile, all in Heraeum are talking of the fantastic sight that they have witnessed. When Medusa was killed, a magnificent winged horse sprang forth from her body - no one even knew that she was pregnant! This amazing horse, called Pegasus, quickly flew off towards Corinth. People have reported that everywhere this horse alights, a spring bubbles forth from the ground. Will wonders ever cease?

message.title: Adventure Complete
message.content: @PSome time has passed since you received any bad news or strange requests from Proetus. In fact, he has managed to forge an uneasy peace with Acrisius, and Melampus is leading his portion of the kingdom admirably. Now that things in the world have settled down, you've been able to focus your full attention on Lycia, which has developed into a fine city. For all the trouble that Bellerophon caused, his help in ridding the land of Chimera has certainly helped Lycia become the city that it is today. @PAnd what of Bellerophon? At last report, he was still wandering Greece, and all who see him turn their backs upon him. Some report that they have heard him planning to recapture Pegasus, but he certainly won't be able to find anyone - mortal or god - to help him reclaim the beast. Finally, Lycia's Bellerophon troubles are over.

message.title: Two Worlds Collide
message.content: In a world torn apart by oppression, a strong leader must arise to throw off the yoke of servitude. This is a very challenging adventure that consists of six parent city episodes and two colony episodes.

message.title: Rebel Base
message.content: @POnly the Atlanteans could be so cruel. Their brutal army swept into your city from Knossos, their base on Crete, and began their mission of destruction. In the fray, families were torn apart, mother from father, brother from brother, sister from sister. When the Atlantean army was done, there were only a few people left standing. @PWhen our Greek forefathers first met the Atlanteans, they were a weak little bunch always spouting off about peace and science. Several decades ago, however, something changed. They began to use science to develop new weaponry, which is respectable enough, and began using their new weapons to subjugate their neighbors. Bit by bit, they took over most of the lands in and around the Mediterranean and built strongholds at Syracuse, Knossos and Carthage. They even built a fort at Lixus that acts as a cork, preventing any unauthorized ships from entering or leaving the Mediterranean Sea. But then, after making some ludicrous demands, they had the gall to invade Greece, an affront that cannot go unanswered. They have already conquered many of our cities with their strong weapons and superior numbers, but we are Greek, and we are stronger. @PFirst, we must build a mighty city in Mycenae, a rocky area whose mountains offer us natural protection against our foes. The mountains will not likely be enough, however. We should also build extensive fortifications to protect our city from those Atlantean curs. From here, we will be able to resist the Atlantean onslaught until we are ready to strike.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PMycenae is a powerhouse! The Atlanteans could not tear our city down and have retreated for the time being. Regrettably, our Greek compatriots have not fared so well. Sparta and Athens are now firmly in the Atlanteans' grip, and we alone survive to stand up to those horrid Atlanteans.

message.title: The Battle of Knossos
message.content: @PWithout an ally in the world, we stand proud against the Atlanteans. The time has come to strike back at our foe. The Atlantean base at Knossos is the key to their attacks on Greece. Without this important military outpost, the Atlanteans will have a much more difficult time making war on the Aegean, at least for a little while. Unfortunately, Knossos is heavily fortified by massive Towers that launch fire, which seems to stick to its target and is resistant to stopping, dropping and rolling. @POf course, the wiser Olympians are on our side. Hermes has discovered a way to weaken the Atlantean defenses at Knossos, making reference to something called orichalc - whatever that is. He says we'll have to find a brave and strong hero to carry out his plan.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PGods be praised! Knossos has fallen! After Achilles weakened Knossos' defenses, our brave soldiers marched in and destroyed the city. The Atlanteans are stunned by our daring victory, and word of our remarkable achievement is spreading like wildfire throughout the Aegean. The Amazons and Centaurs, realizing that we represent the best chance of throwing off the yoke of Atlantean domination, have sided with us. They have vowed to help us in any way that they can to defeat the Atlantean menace. Even the famous heroes of Greece have taken notice of our valor and are eager to come to our city provided, of course, there are suitable accommodations waiting for them when they arrive.

message.title: The Wrath of Poseidon and Sons
message.content: @PThe seas around Greece have been roiling and surging, threatening to overtake the land. Poseidon is livid. The Atlanteans are Poseidon's people, and he is well aware of what we have done to them at Knossos. It's only a matter of time before the God of the Sea, father to monsters and master of earthquakes, makes his displeasure with us felt. @PThough Poseidon is vexed with us, we will push forward. With Knossos destroyed, the time has come to release our Greek compatriots from Atlantis' iron grip. Hoplites may not be enough to combat the Atlantean armies stationed on the Greek mainland. Skilled and powerful horsemen have the best chance of defeating the Atlantean foe. We can't have horses without wheat, however, and the crop is scarce in Greece. Most of the farms have been abandoned or destroyed by the Atlanteans. If all else fails, you may have to raid some other cities for supplies. All's fair in love and war, after all.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe last several years have been more difficult than any recorded in history. Poseidon sent earthquakes and tidal waves to scourge the land, and Mycenae will never be the same again. The angry god even sent his sons, Atlas and the Cyclops, to make life even more difficult. Despite all of these hurdles, Sparta and Athens have been ripped away from the Atlanteans and are part of the Greek nation again. @PWith the Atlantean hold on Greece shaken, the time has come to expel the Atlanteans from another region of the world and push them out of the Mediterranean.

message.title: The Cleitos Project
message.content: @POur spies have returned from their harrowing reconnaissance mission to the Atlantean city, Cleitos, and they have some truly frightening news. They report that those dastardly Atlanteans have built an enormous weapon. This weapon is capable of causing widespread damage, and it doesn't even have to be anywhere near its intended target. After our string of triumphant victories, they must be too frightened to meet us in honorable combat. Other than its effects, our spies were unable to uncover anything else about the weapon or how it works. Fortunately, the gods are with us, and they have provided us with the information our spies could not. Hephaestus, the master craftsman, has devised a way to sabotage the weapon. Only a crafty hero will be able to slip past the fortress at Lixus, penetrate the defenses of Cleitos, and get near the weapon without notice. The quicker this weapon is neutralized, the easier it will be for us to defeat Atlantis once and for all. @PWhile we work on sabotaging this weapon of doom, our allies are valiantly battling Atlantean aggression. Like any war effort, though, supplies are consumed at a rapid rate, and the demand for more is always high. We need to rally to our allies' aid by providing them with the goods that they need to continue this glorious war against Atlantis. Other cities still under Atlantean rule have been secretly sending us gifts in the hopes that we will free them, and many of our new allies have been sending us gifts in gratitude for our help.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @P'Well, champ, let me tell you about this secret weapon thing,' Odysseus began. 'It was easy enough to penetrate the defenses that the Atlanteans had surrounding it. Those Atlanteans always have their head in some book, and they were so intent on their scholarly studies that they didn't even notice me. So, there it was, all shiny and red and with lots of buttons. Since no one was paying any attention to me, I spun some dials and pressed a few of the buttons. Next thing I know, the earth starts shaking! Of course, this gets the attention of all the book-loving scientists, and they started coming after me. Without wasting another minute, I poured about a dozen hives-worth of honey right into the weapon. By this time, the scientists were on top of me. Of course, scientists don't fight nearly as well as heroes do, and I was able to single handedly vanquish them all. There must have been a hundred of them. @P'Anyway, slugo, you ought to get out there in the Mediterranean and attack while the attacking is good. Though I wasn't able to destroy the thing completely, I at least gummed up the works for a little while. Since Atlantis is crawling with scientists, it won't be long until one of those little fellows figures out how to fix that big, red shiny thing.'

message.title: Attrition and Survival
message.content: @PIt is the calm before the storm. The wicked Atlanteans have regrouped in numbers beyond our imagining, and even now are preparing their massive war machine to reclaim all that we have wrested away from them. They have repaired their fearsome weapon that Odysseus had damaged, and strengthened Lixus so that no one, not even a hero, can ever set foot uninvited on Atlantis again. Some of our spies report that the Atlanteans have already recaptured Carthage and have fortified the city with their mysterious Atlantean Fire. We can only hope that the reports are false. Yet, one can't help but think that the Atlanteans' mastery of Carthage is like the first rivulet of water through a chink in an old dam. The chink starts out small at first, but then grows and grows until the dam breaks and an ocean of water is flowing through, demolishing everything in its path. The Atlantean horde is like that rivulet of water, bound to grow stronger and more deadly with each passing day. @PWe must stand firm against this rising tide. Our enigmatic seers have spoken of the years ahead and foretell great hardship, when Greece is buffeted on all sides. And yet, the seers say that those who are strong enough to withstand the Atlantean threat will be rewarded, that a great hero will emerge to lead Greece through the coming times that will be both cruel and fortuitous. They also say that Zeus, in a rage over the Atlanteans' behavior, will, when he is ready, come to the aid of the Greeks. @PWhile we wait for this conquering hero, we must stiffen our sinews in the face of this latest Atlantean threat. The Centaurs of Mount Aulip have vowed that they will die before becoming Atlantean slaves again. Let their vow be an example to us as we prepare for bloody battle.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PBattered, but not beaten, we still stand. The Atlanteans have defeated most of our allies, and our dutiful colonies, and all who lived in them, have fallen victim to Poseidon's rage. @PYet, amidst all this carnage, there is a glimmer of hope. The massive fortress at Lixus has been destroyed, which is a considerable blow to Atlantean power. We have Dionysus and Perseus to thank for the fall of Lixus. When Dionysus heard of the fate of the Centaur city at Mount Aulip, he smote the people of Lixus the only way that Dionysus knows how: by drenching them in wine until they were all falling down drunk. With the Atlanteans thusly indisposed, Perseus swept in with the head of Medusa, turning the besotted citizens of Lixus to stone. @PIf we are to take advantage of this most fortunate event, we must act quickly. It will only be a matter of time before the Atlanteans repopulate Lixus and restore the fort.

message.title: Zeus' Retribution: the Fall of Atlantis
message.content: @PWith a flash of light, Zeus appeared to our seers: 'My dear Greeks, I have been watching your war with the Atlanteans for some time, and I have grown tired of the Atlanteans' bullying antics. My brother Poseidon has also grown too big for his britches - or whatever it is he wears. It is high time that Poseidon and his promise-breaking people are put in their place. I am devising a plan that will let you defeat the Atlanteans once and for all, and give them a taste of their own, bitter medicine. With the destruction of the fort at Lixus, a cunning hero will again be able to make his way to Atlantis, where he can carry out my plot. I must spend a little more time ironing out the details, but I will come back to you soon. Bide your time here in Mycenae a little longer, and victory will be yours.' @PZeus' words are a clarion call. We must once again rise up, weapons in hand, and face the wretched Atlantean foe. We will be ready. When the Atlanteans attack, they will be greeted by the sound of our blood curdling battle cries, and escorted from our city at the ends of our spears. If our allies fall, we will not quiver in fear, but redouble our efforts to defeat our enemy. Angry gods and ferocious monsters will stand no chance against us. We will outlast their assaults and turn them back with the aid of the gods and heroes of Greece. All in the world will learn that the Greek people are not to be trifled with.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe world as we knew it is gone. The daring Odysseus, following Zeus' instructions, dashed into the city of Cleitos, aimed the weapon at the heart of Atlantis and fired it. As Odysseus raced from Atlantis, a huge fireball exploded on the continent, triggering massive earthquakes and tidal waves on the land. From the safety of his ship, Odysseus looked back towards Atlantis. He couldn't be sure, but it looked like it was sinking into the ocean. @PThe cataclysmic effects of the weapon extended well beyond the continent of Atlantis. Shock waves from the explosion emanated from Atlantis to the rest of the world. When the shock waves reached Thera, it roused a giant volcano, which had long been slumbering. The volcano erupted, and the sky filled with ash and fire. Thera was completely destroyed. @PGreece did not fair much better when the shock waves reached our shores. Many cities were destroyed by floods, and a large portion of our army perished in the disasters. Yet, we are still here, and soon it will be time for Greece to start anew. Our greatest stories are yet to come.

message.title: Inroads to Egypt
message.subtitle: This site, the location of a former Atlantean base, would make an excellent outpost from which to liberate Egypt and its fierce warriors.
message.content: @PThe city that rises here on the ashes of the former Atlantean stronghold will serve as a symbol of what will soon happen the world over: What was once Atlantean will become Greek. From here, we will have an easy time assaulting the Atlantean power base in Egypt. This old and proud society, renowned for its military prowess, has long been under Atlantean rule, and some of them have been yearning for freedom. Other Egyptians, however, are resistant to change. Saqqara, one of the oldest Atlantean cities in Egypt, has long since become accustomed to the Atlanteans' domination. The people of Saqqara fear that liberation from the Atlanteans will only mean exchanging one master for another, and would rather continue under Atlantean rule than to face the unknown. But, if Saqqara is left to the Atlanteans, it will only be a matter of time before they bring to heel the Egyptian cities that we reclaim. Therefore, it is resolved: Saqqara must be conquered. @POusting the Atlanteans from Egypt will not be easy. In addition to opposition from Saqqara, we can expect Atlantean visitors from a new fortified city that the Atlanteans have established. The city is called Thera, and it already possesses a strong and powerful military force. With support from Lixus, it is well-equipped to withstand any attack, and more than capable of launching huge offensives.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PRejoice! We have freed the Egyptians from their oppressors. Even Saqqara has begrudgingly joined the Greek fold. With their powerful armies, they are sure to be valuable allies as we continue our quest to remove the Atlantean menace. But, like a troublesome weed, the Atlanteans refuse to go away. Their base at Thera is growing stronger by the day, and now it is much too powerful for our army to attack directly. We can only hope to protect the cities that the Atlanteans at Thera decide to harass.

message.title: The Secret Base
message.subtitle: This well-hidden spot provides easy access to the wealthy cities of Phoenicia.
message.content: @PNo one could possibly find us here in this secret Cypriot harbor, not even the craftiest Atlantean. From this obscure location, we'll be able to launch sneak attacks against the Atlanteans and expunge the Atlantean rogues from Phoenicia. If we help the Phoenicians, they will surely repay us with some of their magnificent wealth, and we'll be able to continue to finance the war effort. @PMeanwhile, our Centaur allies from Mount Aulip have sent word that the Atlanteans, citing an ancient grudge, have declared war on all Centaurs. The Atlanteans, calling the Centaurs misshapen brutes, have vowed to wipe them from the face of the earth. Without our protection, our Centaur allies will surely fall. @POur mission is clear: rip the Phoenicians from the hands of the Atlanteans and ready ourselves to defend our Centaur allies. @L@PThe area would be perfect if it weren't for the lack of food in the area. We will have to turn to others for the nourishment that we need.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe grateful Phoenicians are celebrating our names today. We have ushered the hated Atlanteans out of their cities, and the Phoenicians are again trading their wares freely and earning considerable amounts of cash. As we prepare for battles ahead, the money that our Phoenician allies will supply will help us sharpen our swords and strengthen our shields. With the Phoenician contribution to the war chest, our defeat of Atlantis is a certainty.

message.title: Adventure Complete
message.content: @PAnd thus, you begin again. Many, many years ago, before you began the resistance against the Atlanteans, you were one of a handful of survivors of a brutal Atlantean attack. Now, as then, you are one of few left, but the world has changed. With the help of Zeus and the heroes of Greece, the Atlanteans have been crushed once and for all. Slowly, Greek land, scorched and scarred by war, will be restored to its former splendor. Greek society will again thrive, and the few war-torn cities that dot the countryside will grow into powerful and noble city-states that will become the stuff of legend. The Atlantean Age is over, and the Greek Age is born.

message.title: The Labors Begin
message.subtitle: Tiryns
message.content: @PThe seer emerged from the oracle at Delphi and uttered these words: 'I see two people walking together towards greatness. One of these people is a hulking man, stronger than anyone else in the world. The other person is incredibly good-looking and extremely smart. Hercules is the muscle bound man, a son of Zeus who has incurred the wrath of Hera, Zeus' wife. She drove Hercules to madness, and he killed his wife and children. Since that fateful day, he has traveled around Greece, doing good deeds to atone for his sins. @P'The incredibly good-looking and smart person is you. You are destined to become the ruler of a great dominion, and some of the immortals will call you friend. But that day is some time from now, and you have much to do before that beautiful day dawns. Along the way, your fate and Hercules' fate will be intertwined. His enemies will become your enemies; his friends, your friends. Your path to glory begins with establishing the city of Tiryns in Argolis and introducing it to the world.' @L@PYou'll have plenty of time to build Tiryns into a thriving metropolis later. If you try to build a large city now, you will have difficulty feeding everybody.

message.title: Gods in the World
message.subtitle: Return to Tiryns
message.content: @PWhile you were busy establishing a colony, Hercules was headed for Troy where he whisked Hesione, princess of Troy, out of the jaws of Poseidon's gruesome Kraken. How did Hesione manage to find herself in this scrape? Her father, King Laomedon, refused to keep his promise to pay Apollo and Poseidon for building the walls of Troy. So, the gods punished Troy with plagues and floods, and the only way for Laomedon to save his city was to sacrifice his daughter. @PNow, Poseidon and Apollo are enraged that Hercules has meddled in their affairs. . . and they are well aware of your connection to this hero! And the Kraken, whose taste buds were primed for a bite of human, is very hungry. Elsewhere in the world, the Centaurs, who are always on the look out for a new source of wine, have taken notice of you and your kingdom Trouble might not be far off!

message.title: War with the Centaurs
message.subtitle: Tiryns
message.content: @PDid you hear the one about Hercules and Pholus? It seems that the hero had wandered deep into the Centaur territory of Erymanthus in pursuit of a boar when he grew quite thirsty. The Centaur Pholus was willing to share his wine with Hercules, and they were soon raising flagon after flagon of the beverage. It wasn't long before a horde of other centaurs decided to join the party. One thing led to another, as things usually do when there's wine involved, and Hercules slew many of them in self-defense. The Centaurs, of course, are none too pleased and are plotting their revenge against Hercules and anyone associated with him.

message.title: The Tables Have Turned
message.subtitle: Tiryns
message.content: @PIt seems ages now since you first heard how your fate would be intertwined with Hercules'. Many of the friends you had then are now your enemies, and one of your oldest enemies has become your friend. Nemea is now an ally, thanks to the exploits of the great Hercules, who killed a ferocious lion that was attacking the city. Grateful Ronphus, Nemea's ruler, has begun rebuilding his decimated city. @PThe Amazons and Centaurs, who were once your friends, continue to cause trouble, and the time has come to exert your dominance over them. Capturing Mount Pelion, a prominent Centaur stronghold, will send them a loud and clear message that you are not to be trifled with. @POf course, the more things change, the more they stay the same. Apollo, Poseidon and Hephaestus still have nefarious plans to exact revenge on you. It is time to call Zeus, Hercules' father, to ensure that these warring deities will never be able to harm the city again.

message.title: The Amazon World
message.subtitle: This far off land, located on the outskirts of the Amazon kingdom, is rumored to have rich deposits of copper ore.
message.content: @PTraders from the Amazon city of Cyme have told you about this spot, and it is exactly as they described: rich in copper ore. Certainly no one from Greece has ever ventured into this area, and it is rumored that the Amazon capital is nearby. If the gods hear that you've discovered the city, one of them just might ask you to find something else...

message.title: The Hydra
message.subtitle: It's strange that no one has settled at Lerna. It's well-known for its fertile land and fish-filled lake. What could be keeping people away?
message.content: @PLerna is a place of great beauty, with fertile land perfect for the cultivation of olive trees and grapevines and a lake filled with plentiful fish - a perfect paradise except for one tiny little multi-headed problem. The hideous Hydra stalks the shores of the lake, destroying anything that comes in its path. Only your friend Hercules is strong enough to dispatch this creature, and rumor has it Aphrodite is looking for a hero to help her find some vegetable or fruit or something. The gods can be so hard to understand.

message.title: The Fallen God
message.subtitle: Rocky Lemnos looks like the world turned inside out. Silver and marble, which usually reside deep inside the earth, have risen to the surface.
message.content: @PPoor Lemnos was in the wrong place at the wrong time. Once, Hephaestus enraged Zeus by disobeying him. Zeus cast Hephaestus to the earth from high atop Mount Olympus. Unfortunately for Lemnos, Hephaestus landed right on top of it, and the impact stirred up the land so that what once used to lie beneath it was now on top of it. @PWhen Hephaestus tried to stand up after his fall, he found that he had been lamed! It was useless for Hephaestus to try to retaliate against Zeus - after all, tangling with Zeus was what got him into this mess in the first place. So, Hephaestus decided to take his anger out on the island that broke his fall, and he has been pounding the land ever since. @L@PDue to the strange geography of Lemnos, getting food to your people can be very time consuming. If your population grows too large, you'll have trouble feeding everybody.

message.title: Episode complete!
message.content: @PYou have taken the first step on your journey to fame! Now, it's time to leave Tiryns in the hands of your capable deputy, Eurystheus, and spread your influence to another area of the world.

message.title: Episode complete!
message.content: @PThanks to Perseus, the Kraken has been slain, and Tiryns is once again safe! Now that the city is peaceful again, it is time to set forth and found a new colony.

message.title: Episode complete!
message.content: @PYou've managed to secure Tiryns from danger for now, but the Centaurs are bound to have more tricks up their sleeves...or wherever it is that Centaurs hide their tricks. Now, the thrill of building a new city beckons. Eurystheus will keep an eye on the city while you establish another colony to provide the supplies that Tiryns needs.

message.title: Episode complete!
message.content: @PWith Mount Pelion serving you, your empire has again grown! Zeus now guards the city, and Apollo, Hephaestus and Poseidon have gone away to see if they can cause trouble someplace else. All is well in the kingdom of Tiryns!

message.title: Episode complete!
message.content: @PEphesus thrives, and Artemis certainly got what she wanted, but now the entire Amazon nation is incensed at the theft of Hippolyte's Girdle! These fierce women will follow you to the ends of the earth to make your life miserable!

message.title: Episode complete!
message.content: @PHercules has removed the hideous blemish that defaced Lerna! The Hydra has been dispatched, and the shores are now safe. Aphrodite smiles this day, for she has the Golden Apples of the Hesperides in her clutches.

message.title: Episode complete!
message.content: Lemnos is flourishing, providing valuable goods for Tiryns, and Aphrodite has calmed Hephaestus...for now.

message.title: Rescuing a Hero
message.content: @PZeus has put a curse on your family, the house of Aeolus, decreeing that it shall never rule an empire. There is only one way to lift the curse, and you will need the help of three of Greece's most famous heroes. Theseus purportedly knows more about this curse, but Hades is holding the hero captive in the Underworld, and the great god will loose Cerberus upon anyone who dares to interfere with his plans for Theseus! @PMeanwhile, all of Greece is talking over the Centaurs' latest antics at Pirithous' wedding. Intoxicated as usual, the Centaurs ruined the ceremony when they tried to carry off the bride! Now, the Centaurs are on a drunken rampage through Greece, looking for more wine, and leaders of cities everywhere are jealously hoarding their supplies of the beverage. You would be wise to do the same should you receive some.

message.title: Return of Theseus
message.content: @PThe immortals are quite busy these days! Dionysus has become aware that you were instrumental in freeing Theseus from the Underworld! The god is quite pleased by this news, because he needs Theseus' help. Who knows? Maybe if you can convince Theseus to help Dionysus, the god of the vine might reward you. @PUnlike Dionysus, Artemis is completely fed up with mortals. It seems that a goddess cannot bathe anywhere any more without some mortal peeping at her. The goddess is so completely disgusted that she's decided to release her entire collection of oversized stags, boars, horses, lions and hares into the world to vent her fury on all mortals. @L@PIf you ever find yourself in need of Theseus' help, you should know that his Hall must be located close to the city's Palace. After you build the Hall, right-click on it to see if you have built it close enough.

message.title: A New Hero Arrives
message.content: @PBefore Theseus left your city, he told you a sad story: 'Once, two children, Phrixus and Helle, were in grave danger and tried to escape across the sea on the back of a golden, winged ram. Helle lost her grip on the animal and plunged into the sea, but Phrixus managed to hold on. When he arrived in Colchis, he sacrificed the ram to Zeus and gave King Aeetes, Colchis' ruler, the fleece. Retrieve the Golden Fleece, and Zeus' curse will be lifted, but returning the Fleece to Greece - hee hee, that rhymes! - won't be easy. You'll require the services of a third, great hero.' @PIn other news, Hercules has been busy scaring birds away from Stymphalus. These weren't your garden-variety sparrows! These were huge, ravenous birds that weren't picky about what they put in their beaks: animals, crops, humans - everything tasted good to them. Luckily, Hercules managed to drive the birds away with Hephaestus' castanets - though no one is sure if it was the noise of the castanets that scared the birds off, or the flamenco that Hercules performed as an accompaniment. Regardless, Agapenor, the leader of Stymphalus, is very thankful for Hercules' help. @L@PWhen you honor Athena with a Sanctuary, she will plant a sacred grove of olive trees for your citizens, and you can ask her for gifts of olives and olive oil. You will certainly need her help to succeed here.

message.title: Iolcus Thrives
message.content: @PIolcus is on the verge of becoming the pre-eminent power in all of Greece. With a colony to call your own, you have begun to build a kingdom. Now, you must spread your influence throughout Greece, making friends with those who treat you with respect and putting down those who oppose you. As you near the end of your journey, Iolcus will shine forth, and its power will not be eclipsed. @PIt is now time to thank Zeus for lifting the curse on your house and enabling you to become a great leader. Building a Sanctuary in his honor is sure to please him, and he will smile upon you.

message.title: The Way of the Sickle
message.subtitle: Located on Sickle Island, Corcyra is a beautiful and fertile land that is sacred to both Demeter and Dionysus.
message.content: @PThe island of Corcyra is Dionysus' gift to you for helping him retrieve the Horn of Amalthea. The island is the home of his nurse, Macris, who is also one of Demeter's favorite nymphs. As a result, this land is doubly blessed - it is perfect for the cultivation of both grapes and wheat. Dionysus is feeling generous and might reward you even further if you build a Sacred Grove in his honor.

message.title: The Way of the Sword
message.subtitle: Corinth's central location within Greece makes it the perfect site for a strong military base.
message.content: @PBeing an adventurous hero is a double-edged sword. On the one hand, there's the thrill of dangerous challenges in far off lands. On the other hand, things become tiresome and dull quickly. It wasn't long before Jason's eyes wandered away from his wife, the sorceress Medea, to a new, more exciting visage. Jason, completely smitten with the new woman, left Medea. Now, Medea is in a rage. She has already killed her sons by Jason and the father of Jason's new wife. Still bloodthirsty, she has decided to exact revenge on you, too. After all, if you had never sent Jason to retrieve the Golden Fleece, she would still be in Colchis. The sorceress was last seen racing toward the Amazon city of Lemnos in a chariot pulled by two fiery dragons to find solace with the warrior women!

message.title: Episode complete
message.content: @PThanks to you and Hercules, Theseus has returned from the Underworld and is again roaming the Greek countryside looking for adventure. He has sent word to you that the key to unlocking Iolcus' full potential lies in the far-off land of Colchis.

message.title: Episode complete
message.content: @PDionysus is indeed quite grateful that you have helped him retrieve the Horn of Amalthea, and there may be still more reward from Dionysus in the future. The god has been spotted on Sickle Island, the home of his beloved nurse Macris, and he has been overheard saying that he is preparing a place for you, if you want it.

message.title: Episode complete
message.content: At last, Jason has brought the Golden Fleece safely back to Greece! He has returned from Colchis with King Aeetes' powerful daughter, Medea, as his wife. @PZeus has lifted the curse on your house, and it is now time to begin your own journey and build a kingdom. The road before you forks. Will you choose the way of the sickle and build an economic powerhouse, or will you choose the way of the sword and build a military machine? Corcyra, a fertile island, promises many resources that will help Iolcus thrive. Corinth will provide you with a strong foothold from which you can exercise your might over all of Greece.

message.title: Episode complete
message.content: Now, Iolcus is truly a powerful kingdom. Nearly all of the cities in Greece call you either friend or master, and Zeus looks with pride upon the city of Iolcus and its capable leader.

message.title: Episode complete
message.content: @PDionysus has indeed blessed you, granting you his city of Eretria. Corcyra is bustling, and it is time to return to Iolcus. You have entrusted your new city to Alcinous and hope that he proves to be a capable and resourceful leader.

message.title: Episode complete
message.content: @PCorinth's loyal fighting men are more than capable of defending their homes from harm. Now it is time to return to mighty Iolcus and establish the city's dominance in Greece once and for all. Your trusted general, Corinthus, will lead the city in your absence.

message.title: A New Way of Life
message.content: @PIn a time of darkness, Discord reigned in Greece and the people lived apart from each other. Now, a new day is dawning, and the time has come for a leader to rise up and, for the first time, draw the people together, uniting them in a mighty city. Zeus himself has selected you to achieve this remarkable feat and has pointed you to a site in the Argolid. The city's name will be Argos. People will flock to the city in the hopes of learning a trade and feeding their families, and they will expect you to provide for them. @POther would-be leaders in Greece are also trying to start new cities. Some of them will achieve a modicum of success, while others will fail completely. You might encounter them in your journeys.

message.title: The City Grows
message.content: @PArgos is beginning to thrive, and you are learning more about the bounties that the land offers. The time has come to build a Palace that will serve as the staff around which the scattered people of Greece will gather. It is also time to begin collecting taxes from your people to help pay for the services that your city provides. @PUp on Mount Olympus, the Tribunal of the River Gods has just come to order. 'We have come to a decision in this dispute,' the head of the Tribunal announced. 'And, though both parties presented convincing cases, we have no choice but to award Argos to Hera, wife of Zeus. Sorry, Poseidon.' As Hera jumped up and down in glee, Poseidon's brow furrowed, and his face became stormy. Under his breath, he vowed that if he couldn't have Argos, no one could! You might have to turn to Hera's husband for protection from the ruler of the sea!

message.title: The Hero Perseus
message.content: @PPoseidon continues his onslaught on Argos and is determined to destroy the city, and word around the Agora is that the god might also enlist the aid of one of his consorts to turn your city to stone! Only Perseus, who is off founding the city of Mycenae, will be able to help you slay this monster. But even this worthy hero won't be able to defeat the creature by himself. He will need some magical items to vanquish this unsightly foe. @L@PSome clever herders have discovered how to tame the wild goat. At a Dairy, the goat's rich milk can be made into succulent cheese that your citizens find quite tasty.

message.title: The Gorgon, or The Bad Hair Day
message.content: @PJust as you are about to bring Argos into its full glory, some long-promised trouble has reared its ugly head. That ugly head belongs to Medusa, a consort of Poseidon, who has taken up the god's cause and vows to crush Argos! If you don't find a way to vanquish the Gorgon, she might soon turn your entire city to stone! @PAs you find a way to slay the horrible beast, you must continue to guide Argos to its destiny. Diverse people continue to come to your city from far and near, and they will want diverse gods to worship. You should also take care of your colonies, making sure that they both enjoy all the resources available to Argos. The city will be a shining example of what can be achieved when people band together.

message.title: Artemis' Revenge
message.subtitle: Calydon is a rich and fertile region, noted for its fine vineyards. But, nothing is ever as good as it seems.
message.content: Life has been tough on Artemis lately. First, her beloved Kernyeian Hind, a majestic stag, was wounded by Hercules who was trying to capture the animal. Then, the people in and around the region of Calydon refused to worship her properly. The depressed Artemis turned to her menagerie of animals for solace and, when she saw her mighty boar, snorting and snarling in his pen, her eyes lit up, and a small smile played across her face...

message.title: The Eastern Frontier
message.subtitle: No one knows much about the land of Miletos, located across the sea, far to the east. But, many great nations thrive in this land, so it must have much to offer. Hopefully, all the nations surrounding this site will be friendly...
message.content: @PNo Greek has ventured this far east before, across the great sea, and you'll have to tread very softly to start a city in this land. Great nations shoulder against each other here, and they'll be suspicious of you, a newcomer. Cassiopeia, Queen of Ethiopia, will be particularly annoyed that you have come near her territory. But she has much bigger things to worry about. Ever the proud mother, Cassiopeia boasted that her own daughter, Andromeda, is more beautiful than Poseidon's daughters, the Nereids. Now, Andromeda is to be fed to the Kraken, and Cassiopeia is devastated. If you can find a way to rescue Andromeda, the powerful Cassiopeia will certainly appreciate it, and you may gain a valuable friend. @PThe fleet-footed Hermes has also been spotted in the area, looking for Perseus. The god says that he's seen an item in his travels that Perseus might find useful... @L@PWhile the Kraken roams free, life along the water might be difficult, and trade might be prone to disruption. Look to other cities, even your rivals, for the things you need. Worshiping the gods also can be a boon to you, as many of their sanctuaries have valuable resources of their own.

message.title: Episode Complete!
message.content: @PArgos is on its way to becoming a great city, and even the residents of Mount Olympus have begun to take notice!

message.title: Episode Complete!
message.content: @PIn spite of Poseidon's animosity, Argos continues to grow. But, to become a truly powerful kingdom, Argos must expand its borders.

message.title: Episode Complete!
message.content: @PWith your help, Perseus has obtained a shiny shield and some fine headwear that will prove invaluable to him and to you. Argos' stature is continuing to rise, but for the city to reach its apex, you must again expand its borders. It would be wise to establish this colony in an area of the world distant from your first colony to avail yourself of the resources of different regions. Your two colonies, however, will be so far from each other that their only contact with each other will be through Argos.

message.title: Episode Complete!
message.content: @PThrough deft use of Athena's Mirror Shield, Hades' Helmet of Invisibility, and Hermes' Winged Sandals, Perseus has slain Medusa, saving Argos from a cold fate! You have guided Argos to its zenith, inspiring other leaders around Greece to gather people together and start cities of their own.

message.title: Episode Complete!
message.content: @PIn spite of the many attacks by Artemis' Boar, you have built a thriving colony that will ensure that Argos never wants for luscious grapes. The city will also provide sculpture from the Centaur outpost of Mount Pelion. And, the boar that was a frequent and unwelcome guest will forever bear the name of the city and henceforth be known as the Calydonian Boar.

message.title: Episode Complete!
message.content: @PMiletos makes a fine addition to your empire. The city is well respected by Cyprus, Egypt and Phoenicia, all of which eagerly trade with Miletos to obtain the finest Greek goods. Through Miletos, Argos will have access to the valuable goods that these three nations provide. Queen Cassiopeia is eternally grateful for your role in saving her daughter from a horrible death, and she has cast her lot with yours. As you leave Miletos, she has graciously offered to look after the colony in your absence. @PPerseus now has in his possession the Winged Sandals. The footwear could come in very handy in the near future.

message.title: The Oath
message.content: @PThe conversation at the dinner table turned from the subject of the city you were on the verge of establishing to the fair Helen, beloved of everyone in Greece, who was about to choose a husband. Odysseus said, 'Let us all swear an oath to protect Helen from harm and to support the man whom she chooses as a husband! We owe her no less! We shall name the oath after Helen's father and call it the Oath of Tyndareus!' All shouted in assent, and Odysseus administered the oath to each person. Everyone was too busy celebrating to notice that Odysseus did not take the oath himself, but the hero wouldn't have less than noble intentions. @PNow that the festivities are over, you must return to your land to begin building the kingdom of Aulis in earnest. Soon, your city will match the cities that your friends Agammemnon, Odysseus and Ajax lead! You can count on your friends sending you 'city-warming' presents to help you start your city!

message.title: The Beauty Contest
message.content: @PAt the wedding of Thetis and Peleus, Paris of Troy was asked to award a golden apple to the most beautiful goddess. The contestants were Athena, Hera and Aphrodite. 'Very nice, ladies. That concludes the talent portion of our competition. Now, the interview: if you are crowned most beautiful goddess,' Paris asked the women, 'what will you do?' Hera replied, 'If I win, I'll use my title to bring world peace and to help all the little animals.' 'If I win,' Athena said, 'I'll make sure that everyone has olive oil and bake everyone a batch of cookies!' Finally, Aphrodite said, 'If you choose me, I'll arrange for you to take Helen, the most beautiful woman in Greece, as your wife. I hope I win, because I just love golden apples!' Paris carefully considered each goddess' answer, but, intrigued by the prospect of being married to the most beautiful woman in Greece, chose Aphrodite. It wasn't long before Paris found Helen, tore her away from her husband, and brought her back to Troy. @PNow, Menelaus has declared war on Troy, and everyone bound by the Oath of Tyndareus is rallying to his side, and other leaders have taken up Troy's part. Calchas the seer had this to say about the impending war: 'Though rescuing fair Helen may seem simple, be forewarned that many obstacles will stand in your way. Many will be old and gray by the time they return home.' @PAgammemnon and his soldiers have already left Greece to attack Troy, but Troy's walls, built by Apollo and Poseidon, are incredibly strong. Only an intense, continual siege will be enough to break through the walls, and this type of onslaught will only be possible if the Greeks have a camp close to Troy. But, maybe Agammemnon will be lucky... @POn the home front, you must prepare for further attacks on Troy by asking other cities to give what they can to you to support the war effort.

message.title: The Hero Odysseus
message.content: @PJust outside the walls of Troy, the Greek army captured an old man named Helenus. Like most old men in Greece, Helenus was a great seer, and he weighed in with his two drachmas: 'Did anyone mention the Palladium yet? There is an object held within Troy's walls, an object that Poseidon himself gave to the city when he was building its walls. Troy will never fall as long as it has possession of this object. You'll need to retrieve this object if you want to win the war.' @POnly Odysseus, grandson of the master thief Autolycus, will be able to retrieve this magical object, and the great hero has been acting quite strangely lately. He is the only great leader who has yet to participate in the war effort against Troy, pointing out that he never swore the Oath of Tyndareus. Later, he was spotted laughing hysterically, sowing salt into earth around his Palace, rendering it infertile. Crazy or not, Odysseus is the only one who can help. Maybe if you offer him plenty of wine and olive oil and a lovely Hall to call home, he'll come to Aulis, though who knows what will happen to Ithaca if he leaves the city behind...

message.title: The Ingenious Plot
message.content: @PIt's just crazy enough to work. Odysseus' plan to break through the walls of Troy is ridiculous, but thus far, more traditional methods have failed. Odysseus' plan is to build a huge wooden animal and fill it with the most skilled soldiers in the Greek army. The Trojans will drag the wooden animal into the city themselves, and, under cover of night, the soldiers will attack the city from within. Then, you can send more soldiers to attack Troy. This two-pronged attack is sure to succeed. Now, the only thing left is to decide which animal to build. A badger? No, too small. A rabbit? No, it's been done. A puppy? No, too cute. What about a horse?

message.title: Achilles the Warrior
message.subtitle: Tenedos is the perfect site for a military base, but is not well-suited for much else.
message.content: @PCalchas the seer had this to say: 'To successfully conquer Troy, you'll need the help of the hero Achilles. Achilles was once a willing participant in the war, but Agammemnon managed to offend him somehow...heroes can be so touchy. You'll have to gently convince him to return to the fray, and maybe the gods will help you convince Achilles to fight.' @PWhile you try to convince Achilles to return to the fighting, you should build Tenedos into a strong military base that will help you conquer Troy. Since it is devoid of natural resources, you'll have to rely on others to acquire the goods you need for the city. You can always ask your friends for the supplies you need, and you can of course raid your rivals. Naturally, Troy won't stand idly by and let you build a military stronghold in its backyard. The Trojans just might turn to their favorite son, Hector, to cause you trouble. Of course, the big, strong Hector is a favorite with Aphrodite... @L@PRemember that Calchas also prophesied that many men will be old and gray before they return home. Building a military base that can challenge Troy will take a long time.

message.title: The Great God Zeus
message.subtitle: Anything built here, deep in Ionia, will certainly draw the attention of gods and mortals alike.
message.content: @PThe seer from the oracle have yet another prophecy: 'Thus far, Zeus has been on the sidelines of this great war. Build him a Sanctuary, and he will gladly join your side. The Trojans won't stand a chance. Build a Sanctuary to the great goddess Athena, too, and she will protect the city from harm.' @POf course, building a Sanctuary to Zeus in the heart of Ionia is bound to rile up the gods that have taken Troy's side, and they won't be too thrilled about the Sanctuary to Athena, either. They won't hesitate to make your life miserable and do what they can to prevent you from constructing the Sanctuary. It would be wise to begin construction on the Sanctuaries as soon as you can. The sooner you have both these gods firmly in your corner, the better off you'll be. @L@PYou may need to rely on your allies or even your rivals for the things you need to make the city thrive.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PAulis is well on its way to becoming one of the greatest cities in all of Greece! Yet, there is a hint of trouble in the air. Helen has chosen to wed King Menelaus of Sparta, and the happy couple have settled into their home. While everything seems to be exactly as it should be, word around Greece is that Helen might not be safe.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe walls of Troy have thus far withstood the Greek attack. All of Greece's leaders have agreed that building a base of operations in Ionia will be the only way to carry the day at Troy and return Helen to her husband. @PMeanwhile, rumblings of discontent have been heard in the cities that great leaders have left behind to fight Troy. In Mycenae, Agammemnon's wife Clytemnestra has been whispering seditious tales in the ears of anyone who will listen...

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe crafty Odysseus has retrieved the Palladium, the first step in weakening Troy. He has been heard talking about an ingenious plan to break through the walls of Troy, though one must remember that Odysseus doesn't always make a lot of sense. @PWith Odysseus away from Ithaca, scores of suitors have descended upon the city, hoping to convince the fair Penelope, Odysseus' wife, to reject her sometimes batty husband and choose another. Choked by the vast number of suitors in the city, Penelope has had no choice but to remove Ithaca from the world's stage until she finds a way to deal with all the suitors.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PYou have sacked Troy, and Helen has been returned to her husband in Sparta. Now, all the Greek leaders are headed back to their kingdoms, all of which have suffered in their absences. Only your city of Aulis has managed to retain its previous glory.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PTenedos has grown into a powerful military base that is sure to help you conquer Troy. Agammemnon will stay on here to direct some of the military efforts, even though his own city has fallen into disarray under the leadership of his wife, Clytemnestra. Rumor has it that Clytemnestra has even taken a lover and no longer offers support to the war effort. @PIn one of Tenedos' first triumphs, the city of Lyrnessus was taken. The city incurred heavy losses in its fall, though, and its defenses are weak. Now, it is time to return to Aulis.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: Many cities in Ionia have taken notice of the beautiful Sanctuary dedicated to Zeus in Pergamum. Seeking to worship the greatest of all the gods, Ascania has declared its desire to be your loyal subject forever. Many of their soldiers have even given up on the fighting life to worship Zeus.

message.title: Unlikely Beginnings
message.content: @PThe land here is desolate and bare, but then so is most land in mountainous Greece. It's as good a place as any to establish a city, and you have your good friend Theseus to help you. He's out and about in Attica, visiting other small cities in the region and convincing them that they should place themselves under your wing. Though the city of Athens itself might not have the resources to prosper, perhaps it can grow into a mighty city once it is banded together with its neighbors. @PThere's only one problem with claiming land in Attica. Minos, king of Knossos and master of the Minotaur, calls this land his own and won't take too kindly to someone trying to build a new city upon it.

message.title: Breaking the Bonds
message.content: @PMinos and his Minotaur, son of Minos' queen Pasiphae and a bull, still plague Athens. The time has come to cast off these burdens for good to prove that Athens can stand on its own two feet. You must call Theseus, who is still traveling around Attica, back to the city, for only he can help you vanquish the Minotaur. You'll also need a sleek and powerful trireme to sail to Crete to defeat Minos.

message.title: Revolt in Ionia
message.content: @PWhat wise sage advised to hold your friends close and your enemies even closer? Hippias, a coward exiled from Athens long ago, has whispered his plans to usurp you in the ear of Darius, King of Persia. Hippias has promised Darius eternal servitude if the king agrees to help him! Now, the battle has started, and Delos has entered the fray, revolting against the Persian city of Sardis. The clarion call has been sounded throughout Greece, and most city-states have agreed to set aside their differences and unite in one Greek front to help Delos and turn back the Persians! Only Sparta and Corinth have turned a deaf ear on the cry of our Greek brother!

message.title: Vengeance
message.content: @PDarius has indeed remembered the Athenians, and now he, his son Xerxes, and the entire Persian war machine are on their way to Greece to avenge the humiliating defeat we handed the barbarians! Darius and the Persian fleet have cut a swath of destruction through the Aegean, and Xerxes and the Persian army, having already put down rebellions in Egypt and Babylonia, are marching towards us from the north. Already, Mount Pelion and Ithome have submitted to the Persians. @PAfter a conference on the Isthmus of Corinth, all city-states in Greece have agreed to unite to face the latest barbarian threat. Even Corinth and Sparta agreed to join the alliance, albeit reluctantly. Even with all of Greece united, putting down the Persian military is a daunting task.

message.title: A Bride for a Hero
message.content: @PYour old friend Theseus has one of the strangest habits. He's never satisfied with his current wife and is always on the lookout for a new bride. Antiope, sister of the Amazon queen, Hippolyte, is the latest woman to catch his eye, and he has abducted her. The Amazon nation is not likely to stand idly by and just let their queen's sister go. @PMeanwhile, strange things are afoot in Sparta and Corinth. Spies report that both cities are mobilizing their military forces for what can only be some troublesome purpose. The Oracle of Apollo will come in handy to help you keep a watchful eye on these cities, but ultimately, Sparta must be subdued if you are going to fulfill your destiny. @PIn the middle of all these troubles is Artemis. The Amazons and Spartans are both her people, and she's bound to do something to help them both out. Ares, too, loves these warlike people, so don't be surprised if he gets involved.

message.title: The Hero's Habit
message.content: @PThe time has come to build Athens into the greatest city Greece - the world - has ever known. Athens will be a center of culture and learning, and the greatest heroes will call the city home. Only a few, monstrous obstacles remain between you and this glorious destiny. Defeating these monsters could open up new possibilities for Athens. @PTheseus' womanizing habits continue to cause problems for those associated with him. He and his best friend, Pirithous, have decided that they must marry daughters of Zeus. Theseus has already made off with Helen from Sparta, and now Theseus and Pirithous are planning to raid the Underworld and steal Hades' wife, Persephone. If Hades wouldn't let Persephone go back to her own mother, he surely won't give her up to Pirithous and Theseus! @PMeanwhile, Hercules has been off in the land of Elis, serving as King Augeas' stable boy. He'll be looking for a new challenge soon, and Demeter might just have one for him. Jealous of Artemis' menagerie of animals, she has been looking for some livestock to call her own.

message.title: The Silver Mines
message.subtitle: This harsh land has little to offer except rich deposits of silver ore.
message.content: @PEstablishing a city here will be a boon to Athens. There is plenty of silver ore to be had here, silver that can be minted into the drachmas that Athens will need to thrive. Living here won't be easy, though, because the land is very unkind.

message.title: Land of Plenty
message.subtitle: This lonely, isolated land is blessed with plentiful wood, bronze and marble.
message.content: @PTheseus' dear friend Pirithous, leader of the Lapiths, happily wed Hippodamia in a sumptuous ceremony that featured the best food and wine that Greece has to offer. When the thirsty Centaurs heard about the ceremony, they couldn't resist the prospect of drinking the delicious wine, and attended the ceremony uninvited. Pirithous and Hippodamia graciously greeted the Centaurs at first, but Centaurs aren't known for their self-control, and they were soon completely drunk. The besotted Centaurs then did the unthinkable: they attempted to kidnap the bride! Pirithous was so outraged he has declared war on the Centaurs, and Theseus has beseeched us to provide Pirithous with the raw materials he needs to make armor to help them in their war. @PAn outpost here in Amphipolis will be perfectly suited to provide the raw materials that Pirithous needs. The Centaurs, however, are well aware of the bounty of the land around Amphipolis and may prove to be unwelcome visitors again.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: In spite of King Minos, Athens is on its way to becoming a great city. Already, several small cities in and around Attica consider you their friend or have placed themselves under your leadership. But, Athens' growth will always be stunted as long as you suffer under the yoke of Minos.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: The people of Athens stand tall and proud today. The man they used to call master is now their humble servant, and his grotesque stepson has been sent away from Greece's shores. News of your achievements has spread through Greece like a wildfire, and Eretria and Odessos, in awe of your accomplishments, have willingly placed themselves under your leadership. Yet, the goods that these new subjects provide to Athens still aren't enough for the city to achieve greatness. It is time to leave Athens behind and establish a new city.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PGreece's borders are secure from the Persian threat... for now. Delos is once again a Greek city, and you had even brought Sardis under your control. But Darius would not allow one of his most important cities to remain a subject to you and has snatched the city back. Darius is so incensed at your actions that he has instructed his servant, under penalty of death, to repeat the words, 'Master, remember the Athenians,' three times, every time the King sits down for a meal. You will certainly meet Darius again, and the oracle has enigmatically advised you to 'trust in a wall of wood.' @PTurning back the Persians brought most of Greece together, yet Sparta and Corinth remained aloof and have even declared themselves Athens' rivals!

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PThe taste of this most unbelievable victory is truly sweet! In spite of the overwhelming odds against us, we've defeated the Persians once and for all. Cities that had been conquered by Persia have returned to the fold, and the Persian city of Hattusas calls you master. @PIn spite of the great victory that the city-states of Greece achieved together, Sparta and Corinth have again turned their backs on you.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: With Sparta defeated, Athens has become the most prominent city in Greece.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: Athens, the golden city, is a jewel in the Greek countryside. People from around the world flock to it to drink in its beauty and partake of its diverse cultural offerings.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: The Laurion mines give Athens the economic stability it so desperately needs.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: With the Centaurs firmly under control, Amphipolis will be a reliable source of the goods Athens needs to build a powerful military.

message.title: Founding of Thebes
message.content: @PFollow a cow? The priestess from the Oracle said to follow a cow? A peculiar command, to be sure, but then the priestess is never wrong. She promised that great things would come to the person who follows her cow until it lays down to sleep, and then builds a city on the spot. This person will be able to achieve something that four powerful men failed to achieve and finally bring Europa back to Greece. The beautiful Europa was abducted years ago by a white bull and has not been seen since. And thus, the priestess' bovine-centric prophecy came to an end. @PThe cow did not choose a very good spot. She fell asleep a short distance from a hideous multi-headed serpent that purportedly belongs to Ares. The monster is always ravenously hungry and eats everything that comes near him! Building a city here won't be easy, but the promised reward is irresistible!

message.title: The Serpent
message.content: @PThe time has come. Ares' multi-headed serpent will not leave Thebes alone, and as the city grows, the monster is bound to cause more trouble, plus you could really use some of that marble it seems to be guarding. For the good of the city, the serpent must be slain. No ordinary human can perform this extraordinary task, however. You will need the help of a hero!

message.title: Ares' City
message.content: @PThe wise goddess Athena offered this advice: 'Ares is indeed going to be upset by the loss of that serpent. He has this thing for serpents - single headed, double-headed, dunder-headed - it doesn't matter, he loves them all. And, he really liked how the sun glistened off all those heads. But, do you know what Ares likes almost as much as serpents? Big, big Sanctuaries built just for him! He likes to conduct what he calls 'ambush practice' in a Sanctuary's twisting halls, but to most it seems like he's playing hide and seek. If you build a Sanctuary for Ares, the god will be thrilled to have a new place to practice the art of war, and he'll forget all about the serpent. He'll even take some of the slain serpent's teeth, sow them in the earth, transforming them into fiercely powerful soldiers called Sparti. These soldiers will do your bidding and help to protect Thebes. Heed my advice, mortal, and good luck.'

message.title: The Wedding Present
message.content: @PThe wedding of Harmonia and Cadmus was a splendid affair. Hephaestus, Aphrodite and Ares were in attendance, along with notable leaders from all over the world. Ares and Aphrodite beamed with pride as they each presented Harmonia with a gift. Aphrodite gave the bride a gorgeous necklace that Hephaestus had made, and Ares presented the bride with a beautiful and ornate robe. But, the gift that you brought to the wedding was the best of all. You brought Europa, and she was finally reunited with her brothers Cadmus, Thasus, Phoenix and Cilix. Ecstatic over the return of their sister, Cadmus and Thasus have become your staunch allies, while Phoenix and Cilix opened their distant cities, Phoenicia and Cilicia, to trade. Harmonia and Cadmus even agreed to present you with the Robe and Necklace, though they thought it best to send you the gifts later, after the gods had left, so as not to offend them. @POnly two things marred the ceremony. The first was the fear that Talos would arrive on the scene at any moment. The second was the shocking lack of wine! Wine has been difficult to come by in Greece lately, except in Mount Cithaeron, which has an abundance of the beverage. The people of Mount Cithaeron are refusing to share their supplies, though, keeping all of the wine for themselves.

message.title: The Wine Crisis
message.content: @PThe situation at Mount Cithaeron has gotten out of control. Nearly all of Greece's supply of wine is hoarded there, and now strange things are happening around the city. There have been reports that the bodies of sheep, goats, and even people, gruesomely torn apart, have turned up nearby. The attacks seem much too vicious to be the work of a wandering pack of wolves or an angry wild boar. The frightening deaths have scared the people of Mount Pelion into hiding, and they have not had contact with anyone for some time. Adrastrus of Argos has stopped trading, choosing not to risk the lives of his merchants for a few measly drachmas and supplies. The only solution to these problems is to invade Mount Cithaeron and see what is going on there for yourself.

message.title: The Maenads' Rampage
message.content: @PFear is crippling nearly all of Greece. The Maenads are everywhere, leaving cities throughout Greece in shambles. Now, Dionysus has rallied his Maenads to attack Thebes to punish you for destroying their home. If things are ever going to return to normal, you will have to find a way to kill these horrible monsters and restore a feeling of safety to the people of Greece so that trade and diplomatic exchanges may be conducted once again.

message.title: The Pretender to the Throne
message.content: @PThe dastardly Polynices of Orchomenos, exiled from Thebes, has stolen the Robe and Necklace of Harmonia! The double-crosser has claimed the throne of Thebes, and promised Adrastus of Argos and Tydeus of Calydon these and other spoils if they help him take your city. You must defeat these villains to keep what's rightfully yours. @PMeanwhile, Hephaestus, the lame god, has caught his wife, Aphrodite, in a forbidden embrace with Ares. Slowly, Hephaestus has put two and two together and finally understood why Ares and Aphrodite had both been so proud of Harmonia at her wedding, and why the gorgeous goddess of the tender passions thought it necessary to spend nine months at a beauty spa some twenty years ago.
