Hotter than the metals that he pounds in his forge, Hephaestus has decided to destroy all that Ares holds dear, whether it be a mortal, a monster or a city!

message.title: The Cretan Princess
message.subtitle: A rugged and forested land, Cydonia is located on Crete, the gateway to the rest of the world.
message.content: @PThe people of Crete are wary of you, and an old beggar man reveals the reason: 'Once, a woman was spotted far off our shores, approaching our island on the crest of a giant, foamy wave. As the woman drew closer, it became clear that she wasn't riding on the sea, but on the back of a great white bull! The bull deposited the woman on our shores, and Talos, a bronze man forged by Hephaestus, guards the woman night and day. The bronze man guards our island, too, preventing invaders from doing us harm. @P'It has been prophesied that a leader from Thebes will come to our island and take this woman from us. We fear that if this leader succeeds, Talos will no longer guard our island. And, since you are from Thebes, you might just be the one that will change our world completely.'

message.title: Episode complete
message.content: @PUnder your leadership, Thebes is beginning to thrive. Yet, the multi-headed menace still plagues the land, and the city will never be truly great as long as it counts the monster as one of its residents.

message.title: Episode complete
message.content: @PThe serpent is gone, yet worries remain. Ares was fond of the serpent, and he cannot be happy that you have arranged for the serpent's death. Athena, the goddess of warriors, crafts and wisdom, has arrived to collect some of the serpent's teeth for some strange and wonderful purpose. Maybe she can shed some light on how to earn Ares' favor.

message.title: Episode complete
message.content: @PAres is shouting for joy over his latest Fortress, and his Sparti stand guard over your city. With Thebes well protected and in the trustworthy hands of your prideful deputy, Oedipus, it is time to set forth and expand the kingdom. The Oracle at Delphi recommends establishing a city at Cydonia in Crete...though she's hinted that fertile fields and great forests are not the only things to be found there!

message.title: Episode complete
message.content: @PJason reduced Talos to a pile of scrap metal by removing the single nail that holds the bronze man's blood inside of him. During the dark of night, however, someone made off with Talos' carcass. Maybe it was a local sculptor, looking for an extra supply of bronze. Then again, it could have been Hephaestus... @PMeanwhile, your stature has grown throughout Greece. Many cities call you friend, and even the great Minos of Knossos has declared himself your loyal subject. All of Greece talks of the beautiful Robe and Necklace of Harmonia that Cadmus has promised you, which are even now on the way to Thebes.

message.title: Episode complete
message.content: @PHorror. Unspeakable horror is what you found at Mount Cithaeron. Madwomen who called themselves the Maenads, drunk on wine, were gleefully tearing apart the bodies of their innocent victims. Forced from Mount Cithaeron by your invasion, these servants of Dionysus have now scattered throughout Greece, continuing their reign of terror.

message.title: Episode complete
message.content: @PEverything has returned to normal. People can leave their homes without fear, contact has been restored between you and other leaders, and goods are once again flowing throughout Greece. Yet, a foreboding sense of doom permeates the air. Perhaps it's because the Robe and Necklace of Harmonia, promised to you so long ago by the honorable Cadmus, have not yet arrived in Thebes. Worse still, you haven't heard from Cadmus for some time. There could still be trouble brewing.

message.title: Episode complete
message.content: @PYou have thoroughly crushed Polynice's attempt to usurp your power, and the leaders that supported him are now firmly under your rule. Not even Hephaestus will threaten Thebes now!

message.title: Episode complete
message.content: The priestess' prophecy has come true! You have wrested Europa from Talos' grip and delivered her back to her brothers in Greece. Talos, however, is enraged that you have taken his charge from him and is following close on your heels!

message.title: A Kingdom Reborn
message.content: @PNot so long ago, Sparta was the greatest city in the Peloponnese. Menelaus and his beautiful wife Helen ruled over all, and people were content. But then, Paris of Troy abducted Helen, and a great war broke out. Through cunning and strength, our soldiers won the war, but things weren't the same when Menelaus returned to Sparta. The city soon crumbled, and only a few ruins remain of what was once a glorious city. @PThe time has come to establish a new Sparta on new land! The new Sparta will rise in glory and power, and one day eclipse the prestige of the old Sparta!

message.title: Sparta on the Rise
message.content: @PIf we are to build a mighty army, our citizens must have some olive oil. We don't seem to have any here in Sparta, but word is that puny city Olympia makes it. We haven't had any fun in so long - let's go take over Olympia and get their olive oil! We could probably get Corinth to join us, and maybe our beloved Ares will come along! Maybe Olympia will get word of our plans and even try to attack us! Wouldn't that be a gas? @PMeanwhile, the cult of Dionysus is on the rise in Greece. Wine does have its purpose - a drop or two can go a long way to quenching one's thirst. But, why anyone would drink to excess is a mystery. Still, the drunken lout seems to hold a strange appeal to others around the country, and they swoon at the mere mention of his name. @PAnd, what is this rising in the east like the sun? We hear rumblings of a new empire that is gaining some prominence.

message.title: War with Persia
message.content: @PThe leader of that upstart empire causing so much trouble for those feeble cities has finally revealed himself. He calls himself Darius, king of Persia, and he is quite the jokester. He has sent word that he claims Sparta, along with the rest of Greece, as a subject! Maybe a mere declaration of superiority is enough for wine-soaked cities like Eretria to surrender, but that silly little ploy isn't going to work on us! @PI don't know why we've been dragged into this, because this is Athens' problem, anyway. The Athenians started a revolt in Ionia, and now that Darius is attacking them in return, they realize that they've bitten off more than they can chew. Gluttony just doesn't get you anywhere! @PHipponax of Corinth has the right idea, though. He's planning an all-out attack on Sardis, the capital of those barbarian Persians.

message.title: All Out War
message.content: @PAthens has really gotten too big for its britches! They have attacked Melos, killing all its men and enslaving its women and children, for refusing to participate in that silly Delian League! It's up to us now to put an end to this foolishness! As soon as we conquer Athens, Amphipolis, Delos and Eretria, we can return the world to normal.

message.title: The First Skirmishes
message.subtitle: Some may say that Taras' fertile fields are lovely sights. We see only grapes and herd animals that will ultimately allow Sparta to develop a stronger army!
message.content: @PTaras looks to be the perfect place to station a Spartan army. Plus, our spies have told us that somewhere in the vicinity is the city of Odessos, Athens' source of wheat. If we can crush Odessos and cut off Athens' food supply, then Athens' downfall is certain. And, our great god Ares has promised to help us find Odessos if we help him to retrieve something he wants!

message.title: The First Skirmishes
message.subtitle: Ithaca is a tree-covered island, perfectly suited to be the base for the Spartan navy!
message.content: @PIthaca is the perfect spot to build a powerful naval base. If Athens has a strength, it is the Athenian fleet. Our army is already vastly superior to the Athenians'; if our navy can overmatch the Athenian navy, Athens doesn't stand a chance! When we have some triremes built, we should test them out by attacking someone! @PUnfortunately, Ithaca, home of the great Odysseus, has its problems. Cyclops is coming to the city, looking for revenge. He is enraged with Odysseus because the hero hurled a pointy stick into the Cyclops' only eye! Luckily for the Cyclops, Athena managed to pluck it out, and he eagerly anticipates settling his score with Odysseus. Scylla, too, is nonplussed with Ithaca's hero. Imagine - sailing past the beast, and only offering six soldiers for her to eat. That's just barely an appetizer! We'll need to find Odysseus to rid the land of these creatures. @PScylla's master, Hermes, is also in the area, making life difficult for the city of Elis. Hermes is extremely attached in an embarrassingly emotional way to Scylla. If Odysseus can turn back Scylla, Hermes is likely to leave Elis alone, and the city will be extremely grateful. @L@PWith so many monsters in the area, you might find that you need to ask for goods from your allies or take them from your rivals.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PSparta is growing, and soon our power will be unrivaled in all of Greece! Before we can attain that height, we must first acquire some resources that our city lacks. Of course, there is a certain Athenian quaintness to trading for the items, but leaders we trade with tend to think we owe them other things as well. Really, why should trade relations have anything to do with helping them through a famine or plague! There must be a better way...

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PWith Olympia firmly under our thumb, obtaining olive oil is easy, and our star is on the rise. While our city is gaining power, we've heard that some cities in the east are having trouble with some foreign empire. If they raised their kids correctly instead of leaving them home with their mothers, they wouldn't be having these troubles!

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PWith their tails between their legs, the Persians were sent packing all the way back to Sardis. But, can you believe how wimpy the Athenian military is? They couldn't even defend their own city! They were lucky that the Persian navy was so pathetically weak and inept, or else they would have never succeeded at Marathon. @PStill, those Athenians are a squirrelly bunch, and we've heard that they are plotting, forming alliances throughout the Cyclades. All of Greece is choosing sides, and smart ones will choose ours.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: The last of the Delian League has fallen to us, and Sparta reigns over all!

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: We have crushed Odessos under our heels, and Athens is beginning to starve. Already, its ally Thermopylai has collapsed, and its citizens have scattered to the four winds. The final battle cannot be too far off!

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: When Odysseus killed Scylla, Hermes predictably went back to his mother, Maia, and bawled his eyes out. What a sissy! Anyway, he couldn't cry and bother Elis at the same time, so Elis is now free from Hermes. In their gratitude, the city has become our subject! Ithaca, once dominated by a pair of monsters, is now dominated by the Spartan fleet! Our new fleet performed very well at Delos, and the city is now under our rule. Soon, Athens and the rest of its allies will fall to us one by one, like olives falling off a tree!

message.title: Adventure complete!
message.content: All that was foretold has come to fruition. In spite of many battles and obstacles, you and Hercules together have risen to prominence. Through his deeds, Hercules has atoned for the murders of his wife and children and has earned immortality from the gods! You, too, have earned a measure of immortality, for people will long tell tales of your many triumphs as leader of Tiryns. They will speak of how you defeated Amazons and Centaurs, faced a monster and even managed to thwart the bad intentions of Apollo, Poseidon and Hephaestus! Your fame is secured!

message.title: Adventure complete!
message.content: You have taken Iolcus from its humble beginnings and built it into the most powerful kingdom in all of Greece, risking the wrath of gods and mortals alike to achieve your destiny. Along the way, you have liberated a hero from the Underworld, slain the fearsome Calydonian Boar, and restored one of Greece's most treasured possessions, the Golden Fleece, to its proper place. Zeus, who had once cursed your family, now blesses you and celebrates your name throughout Mount Olympus!

message.title: Adventure complete!
message.content: @PThrough your leadership, you have forever changed the face of Greece. With Argos, you have shown the people of Greece that they should no longer live isolated from one other, but should put themselves under the protection of a great leader like you, who will provide them with the things they need to enrich their lives.

message.title: Adventure Complete
message.content: Not all the leaders who fought alongside you in the Trojan War have fared so well as you. Sparta has collapsed, and Menelaus and Helen have gone to Egypt to start their lives anew there. Odysseus is nowhere to be found, and the suitors at Ithaca are imposing themselves more and more everyday. Mycenae, too, has collapsed under the treachery of Clytemnestra. Yet, Aulis, through your sage leadership, stands tall and proud.

message.title: Adventure Complete
message.content: In the harshest and most barren of environments, you have managed to build a city that has all the amenities of the richest, most fertile lands. You have led Athens through times of great turmoil from which it has emerged unblemished and strong. Greece's most noble heroes are frequently spotted on the city's streets, and monsters and other unsavory types steer clear of the most notable city in the world.

message.title: Adventure Complete
message.content: Any one of your many achievements would have been enough to rank you among Greece's best leaders. Not only did you defeat Ares' serpent and rescue Europa from Crete, you rid Greece of the horrible Maenad threat and rebuffed Polynice's attempt to depose you! Never has a single ruler done as much for Greece as you have.

message.title: Adventure Complete
message.content: Could there ever have been any doubt that Sparta would once again rise and far surpass its previous glory? From our humble rebirth, we have slowly gained power, and now Greeks everywhere follow our rules. And the first rule of Sparta? Under penalty of death, no one is to worship that foul-smelling, drunken, messy excuse for a god, Dionysus!

message.title: Hercules' Labors
message.content: Together, you and Hercules will begin the journey to immortality. As he performs his legendary labors, you will build a legendary Kingdom that will provide fodder to storytellers for years to come. This challenging adventure consists of seven episodes.

message.title: The Voyages of Jason
message.content: Overcome Zeus' curse to become one of the most celebrated rulers in all of Greece! This challenging adventure consists of five episodes.

message.title: Perseus and Medusa
message.content: The people of Greece are scattered around the country. You will gather them together, like a shepherd gathers his flock, and lead them to a brighter day. This adventure is not too challenging and consists of six episodes.

message.title: The Trojan War
message.content: Lead Greek forces to Troy to rescue the most beautiful woman in the world! This adventure is extremely challenging and consists of six episodes.

message.title: Athens through the Ages
message.content: Lead Athens from its earliest days, through times of war, to the Golden Age! This adventure is somewhat challenging and very long. It consists of eight episodes.

message.title: Zeus and Europa
message.content: Gods, mortals and monsters will all try to prevent you from leading Thebes to glory. This adventure is fairly easy and consists of eight episodes.

message.title: The Peloponnesian War
message.content: Build Sparta's might and lead its military against all comers, whether they be Greek or barbarian! This adventure is quite challenging and consists of five episodes.

message.title: Tutorial: Housing and People
message.content: Welcome to the first Zeus tutorial! This is the Goals screen, where you'll receive basic instructions about how to build and manage cities in the Greek world. This lesson has no specific goals, as indicated by the phrase 'Open play, no episode goals', above. @L@LTo exit this screen, click your right mouse button. To return for further instructions, click the Episode Goals button, which you can see at the bottom of the Control Panel, to the right: @G13 @LSoon you're going to exit this screen, and study a sample neighborhood we've provided. The first things you'll learn about are roads and walkers. @L@L@LRoads and walkers @LWalkers emerge from buildings you place, and are guided by the roads you lay out for them. Click with your right mouse button on any building, walker or location to see what it is, and to get more information about it. Pause the game with the 'p' key. @L@LNow click your right mouse button to exit this screen, and study the sample neighborhood. If you find the play area moves around too fast, use the 'Options' menu to slow the scroll speed. When you're ready to build a neighborhood of your own, return to this screen for instructions. @L@L@LSTEP ONE - Laying out roads @LTo the right of the sample neighborhood, lay out a looping road (like the one you see in the sample neighborhood) by clicking the Roads button: @G14 You can place long sections of road by holding the mouse button down and dragging. For this tutorial, make sure the road loop for your new neighborhood is not connected to the sample neighborhood. @L@L@LSTEP TWO - Housing and Immigration @LThe Population tab gives information about your city's people and housing. From here, place some vacant housing lots inside the block, alongside the road, by clicking the Common Housing button: @G01 Eventually, new workers will move into the vacant lots, turning them into huts. You can place large sections of housing by holding the left mouse button down and dragging. @L@LWhen you have a few occupied huts in your new neighborhood, return here to continue. @L@L@LSTEP THREE - Hazards @LMost buildings need regular maintenance so they don't catch fire or collapse. In the sample neighborhood, a 'superintendent' periodically emerges from the Maintenance Office, tending to the buildings he happens to pass. At the top of the Hygiene and Safety tab, click 'see hazards', and look for a rising hazard column on any building not recently passed by a superintendent: @G02 Click the 'see hazards' button again to return to normal view. You can also tap the spacebar to switch back and forth between normal and special views. When you're done, return to learn how to add a Maintenance Office to your new city. @L@L@LSTEP FOUR - Maintenance @LTo add a Maintenance Office to your new neighborhood, select the Hygiene and Safety tab, then click the Maintenance Office button: @G03 Use the 'see hazards' button again to make sure all your new huts have access to the superintendent. @L@LWhen you've provided maintenance services to your new neighborhood, return here to continue. @L@L@LSTEP FIVE - Water for houses @LIn the example neighborhood a water bearer periodically emerges from the Fountain, carrying water to the houses he passes. To see which houses have water, select the Hygiene and Safety tab, then click 'see water'. Each house passed by the water bearer has a tall column. As water is consumed, this become shorter, until the water bearer visits again. To provide water to your new neighborhood, select the Hygiene and Safety tab, then the Fountain button: @G04 @L@LExperiment with other configurations of roads, housing and working buildings. Use the Clear Land button to demolish buildings or trees when necessary: @G16 @L@LUse the 'undo' button when you make a mistake: @G17 When you're ready to move on, return to this screen and click Next Tutorial. @L @L

message.title: The Emporium
message.content: @PFor centuries, people have flocked to Greece's large and beautiful cities, hoping to lead prosperous lives. In their attempts to provide for their people, leaders have stripped the Greek countryside of its resources, and now these leaders are scrambling to make sure that their citizens are clothed and fed and that their militaries have all the supplies they need. Quickly, they are finding that Greece itself can no longer support its large population. @PYour city at Larisa in Ionia will provide for the city-states of the mainland, and you'll be able to turn a tidy profit. Though Larisa has vast supplies of marble and wood, it is lacking the resources that people need to lead satisfying lives. You'll be able to acquire these items from other leaders, but it would be better if your kingdom could produce them itself. The gods can provide you with some of the goods you need, and you can also establish colonies whose resources will complement Larisa's. When you are ready to establish the first colony, click on the Goals Button and set aside the goods that the colony needs to get started.

message.title: Growing Prosperity
message.content: With a new colony providing you with valuable goods, Larisa is poised to become the wealthiest city in all the world. Already, cities around Greece are wondering how they ever lived without the goods that you provide. If you could provide even more items, then Larisa would be even more profitable. Establishing a second colony that has access to resources that your kingdom currently lacks will only add to Larisa's prosperity. Remember, when you are ready to establish the second colony, click on the Goals button and set aside the goods that the colony will need to get started.

message.title: City of Gold
message.content: With two colonies supplementing Larisa's wealth, nothing can stop you from amassing enormous amounts of money. Other leaders in the world stand in awe of your growing prosperity.

message.title: The Shining City
message.subtitle: Smyrna is a land of metal, rich in both copper and silver ore.
message.content: The ores at Smyrna will significantly bolster Larisa's wealth. Foundries produce bronze which, in and of itself, is valuable, but is even more valuable when it is manufactured into sculpture and armor. Silver is money, pure and simple. Bustling Mints will convert the silver into drachmas, and your treasury will grow. When you have established the industries to your satisfaction, click on the Goals button and set aside the required goods to return to Larisa.

message.title: The Breadbasket
message.subtitle: The fertile fields here are the perfect hosts for livestock and Wheat Farms.
message.content: The island of Naxos is well-known for its meadows, which sheep in particular find tasty. The fleece these sheep provide will help you to ensure that Larisa always has a plentiful supply of this basic necessity. Wheat, too, can be grown here, and it can be used to feed horses and people alike. When you are ready to return to Larisa, click on the Goals button and set aside the specified goods.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: You have decided to leave Larisa for now and establish a colony to supplement the city's resources. After you click 'Proceed,' you will see the World Map, where you can choose a site to establish a colony. To read a description of a colony site, click on it. Choose the one you want to establish first, and click the button next to 'Choose this location?' to proceed. You'll get a chance to establish the other colony later.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: You have again decided to leave Larisa temporarily and establish a second colony. When the second colony is securely in your fold, Larisa will be nearly self-sufficient and dripping in wealth.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: Now that Smyrna's Foundries and Mints are thriving, you have decided to return to Larisa, where the ores and the goods that are manufactured from them will only serve to increase your wealth.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: You have decided that its time to turn your attention back to Larisa and leave Naxos in the hands of your deputy, Elephenor, who will make tribute payments to you in precious fleece.

message.title: Economic Open Play
message.content: Under your leadership, Larisa, supported by its two colonies, will become the richest kingdom in the world! This is an open play adventure, so you won't have to worry about meeting specific goals.

message.title: The Upstart
message.content: @PLike one of the Titans of old, Athens is running roughshod over everyone in Greece, forcing city-states to bend to its will. The Athenians have taken complete control over Greece's trade routes and have fixed the prices of goods to fit their needs, making free trade very difficult. Those who dare to challenge them find themselves crushed, nearly consumed by the Athenians just as Cronus ate his own children. But, just as the fearsome Cronus was toppled, so too shall Athens be. @PThe best way to break Athens' rule is to chisel away at its empire, conquering its weaker allies one by one. Mount Malea is an ideal spot to build a city that will rival Athens' dominance, and the area around the city has many of the resources you'll need for the city - and its citizen-soldiers - to thrive. Athens, its patron goddess Athena, and its stronger allies will certainly make their displeasure with your upstart city felt. @PTo bring Athens to its knees, you'll need a strong navy. Regrettably, the one thing that Mount Malea lacks is a steady supply of wood. You'll need to establish a colony to provide you with this valuable resource. When you are ready, click on the Goals Button on the Control Panel. In the screen that pops up, click to dispatch the goods to the colony and return to the city. In a moment, you will be able to leave your city to establish the colony.

message.title: Glory
message.content: @PNow that you can readily acquire wood from Orchomenos, you can build the triremes you need to become a true world power. The Athenians have grown extremely anxious and have called on their patron, Athena, to help them crush you. And Athena, the dutiful daughter, has asked her father, Zeus, to help her favorite city. Call on all your resources - your allies, vassals and patron gods - to continue to lead Mount Malea on its march towards domination.

message.title: The Great Forest
message.subtitle: Orchomenos is blanketed with thick, green forests, perfect for the construction of triremes.
message.content: @PThe heavily forested valleys around Orchomenos are a sight for sore eyes, for soon these tall trees will become the mighty triremes that will hopefully lead one day to Athens' destruction. The Athenians, of course, are well aware of your intentions and will do what they can to interfere with your plans. Once you have built up the wood industry at Orchomenos to your satisfaction, click on the Goals Button and dispatch goods to Mount Malea to return to the city. In a short time, you'll be able to go back Mount Malea.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PYou have decided to leave your city behind for now and establish a colony to supply you with the wood you need. In a moment, you will visit the World Map to select a colony site. Often, you'll have your choice of colony sites. This time, though, your scouts have determined that only one location, Orchomenos, has the resources that you need. Click on it to see a description of the site.

message.title: Episode Complete
message.content: @PYou have decided to leave Orchomenos and return to Mount Malea where you can continue to chip away at Athens' power, leaving Polynices in charge of the colony. As long as Orchomenos remains your colony in good standing, Polynices will give you wood every year as his tribute payment. You can also ask him for wood, or purchase some from him.

message.title: Military Open Play
message.content: In this adventure, you will lead a fledgling city from its meager beginnings into a military powerhouse, establishing a colony along the way. This is an open play adventure, so you won't need to worry about specific goals.

message.title: Utopia
message.content: Nearly all of the gods collaborated to make the land at Olympia perfect. Demeter made the land fertile so that livestock and farms could thrive. Athena and Dionysus made sure that Olive Trees and Grapevines would be nourished by the soil. Artemis set loose some of her boar, and Poseidon stocked the waterways with fish. Even Hades touched the land, making sure that valuable ores rose to the surface. You are the luckiest of all mortals to be able to build a city on this land!

message.title: Open Play Sandbox
message.content: This land has everything you need to build to your heart's content. There are no goals to be met; everything is up to you!

message.title: Tutorial: Producing Food
message.content: Your people need to eat, and the sea can be a bountiful source of food. In this tutorial we've provided a sample neighborhood which has a working fishing industry, and another neighborhood, to its right, which does not. You're going to add a fishing industry to the neighborhood that needs one, but first study how this works in the sample neighborhood. @L@LFishing @LFishing boats set out to sea from a Fishery, and return with fish, then deliverymen transport the fish to the nearest Granary. Right click to exit this screen and observe this process in the sample neighborhood, then return to learn how to set up your own fishing industry. @L@L@LSTEP ONE - Catching fish @LPlace a Fishery near your neighborhood, (the one to the right of the sample neighborhood), by selecting the Husbandry tab, then the Land and Sea button: @G05 The Fishery must be placed on a straight section of coast. Place it near a fishing spot, so the boats won't have too far to travel: @G18 When you see a boat from your Fishery fishing at the fishing spot, return here to continue. @L@L@LSTEP TWO - Storing food @LFish, like all food, is stored in a Granary. To build a Granary for your neighborhood, select the Distribution Tab, then the Granary button: @G11 Make sure the Granary is connected by road to the Fishery, then watch the Fishery carts deliver fish to it. @L@L@LRoadblocks @LAs more roads are added to your neighborhoods, you may find that walkers such as superintendents and water bearers occasionally wander outside your residential road loop. These roaming walkers don't inherently know where you want them to patrol, but they can be guided with roadblocks, such as those in the sample neighborhood. You probably don't need to add any roadblocks to your neighborhood now, but you can use the Place Roadblocks button to experiment: @G15 Notice that walkers with specific destinations, such as fish deliverymen headed to the Granary, ignore roadblocks. @L@LRemember to click with your right mouse button on any location, building or walker to learn what it is. @LWhen you see some fish in your new Granary, return here and click Next Tutorial to learn how to distribute it to the houses in your neighborhood.

message.title: Tutorial: The Agora
message.content: The Agora @LThe Agora is the central marketplace of a neighborhood, supplying food and other goods to its residents. In the sample neighborhood, a food vendor periodically sets out from the Agora and heads for the nearest Granary, to procure food (ignoring roadblocks). A peddler then emerges from the Agora to roam the streets, delivering food to any houses he happens to pass. Observe this process in the sample neighborhood, then return here. @L@L@LSTEP ONE - Building a Granary @LAdd a Granary to your neighborhood (to the right of the sample neighborhood), by selecting the Distribution Tab, then clicking the Granary button: @G11 After placing the Granary, wait until it has a supply of fish, then return here. @L@L@LSTEP TWO - Building an Agora @LTo distribute fish from your Granary to the Huts in your neighborhood, select the Distribution Tab, then click the Agora button, and select Common Agora: @G10 Place the Agora directly ON TOP OF a road, like you see in the sample neighborhood. Make sure to place it on one of the roads in your residential road loop, so it will be close to the houses it is to serve. @L@L@LSTEP THREE - Adding a Food Vendor @L@LA Common Agora can hold up to three Vendors' stalls, but right now you'll need only one, a Food Vendors' stall. To add a Food Vendors' stall to your Agora, click the Agora button, then select Food Vendor, and place the Stall somewhere on your Agora: @G10 The food vendor will procure fish from your Granary, and once the Stall has a supply of food, a peddler will begin distributing it to your Huts. @L@LUse roadblocks if necessary to ensure the peddler does not stray outside the residential road loop, but make sure roadblocks don't prevent him from reaching your Huts. @LWhen the residents of a Hut have a supply of food, they'll upgrade their dwelling to a Shack, which can hold more people than a Hut. @L@LClick with your right mouse button on houses, to see a list of what items its residents currently have. When you have some Shacks in your neighborhood, return here and click Next Tutorial to continue.

message.title: Tutorial: Culture and Appeal
message.content: Culture @LAs houses develop, they can generally hold more people. Developing the housing you already have is a better way to grow your population than simply building more houses. For houses to develop beyond mere Shacks, residents need access to some cultural diversions. In the sample neighborhood, a College trains philosophers, who then proceed to a Podium to speak. Roaming philosophers then emerge from the Podium, teaching philosophy to any houses they pass. @L@L@LSTEP ONE - Philosophy @LBuild a College and Podium in your neighborhood by selecting the Culture tab, then clicking the philosophy button: @G07 To see which houses have access to philosophy, click 'see philosophers' on the top of the Culture tab. A Shack with access to some Culture becomes a Hovel. @L@L@LSTEP TWO - Athletics @LExercise is important to your citizens. Give some of your city's households access to athletics by selecting the Culture tab, clicking the Gymnasium button, and placing a Gymnasium: @G52 Soon athletes will roam the streets, serving as personal trainers to each household they pass. @L@L@LSTEP THREE - Appeal @LNo one wants to live in an unattractive area. To see how appealing an area is, select the Aesthetics tab, then click 'see appeal' at the top. @LVery appealing areas appear light, while unappealing areas, such as those near industrial buildings, appear dark. @L@LYou can increase the appeal of an area by clicking the Beautification or Recreational areas buttons on the Aesthetics tab, and placing some of the items you see available: @G08 @G09 Of course you can also increase the appeal of an area by relocating particularly unattractive structures to a more appropriate location. @L@L@LCommemorative Monuments @LSometimes, when you achieve something truly spectacular, you'll see a third button on the Aesthetics tab for a Commemorative Monument you can build! @LWhen you've brought Culture to your neighborhood, and made it more appealing, return here and click Next Tutorial to continue. @L @L

message.title: Tutorial: Hygiene and Safety
message.content: Unrest and Plague @LThings aren't always going to be fine and dandy in your city. Many of the things you'll need to do as a leader can make you unpopular, and create unrest among your people. Also, as a city becomes crowded, plague is more likely to strike - and it can strike anywhere. @L@L@LSTEP ONE - Assessing unrest @LThe former leader of this city paid low wages, generating a lot of unrest here. To assess unrest in the city's houses, click 'see unrest' at the top of the Hygiene and Safety tab: @G02 When unrest is really high in a particular household, its disgruntled residents may loiter in the streets, and even become outlaws! @L@L@LSTEP TWO - Dealing with unrest @LIt's best to prevent unrest by treating your people fairly. Sometimes, as in the sample city, you'll find yourself in need of a more immediate solution, namely, a little muscle in the form of some watchmen. Place some Watchposts by selecting the Hygiene and Safety tab, and clicking the Watchpost button: @G53 Observe as a watchman emerges from each Watchpost and roams the city's streets, quelling unrest in the houses he passes, and subduing any outlaws he encounters. When unrest is under control, return here to learn about Hygiene and plague. @L@L@LSTEP THREE - Assessing Hygiene @LTo prevent widespread plague, maintain good city hygiene by ensuring that food, and the services of a healer are available to as many of your citizens as possible. Select the Hygiene and Safety tab and you'll see that in the sample city hygiene is not good, and is getting worse, because there are few Food Vendors, and no Infirmaries: @G02 Click 'see hygiene' at the top of the tab to see which houses have access to a healer, and ate good meals last month. @L@L@LSTEP FOUR - Infirmaries and healers @LThe services of a healer from an Infirmary are important for maintaining good hygiene. Provide this troubled city with healers, by selecting the Hygiene and Safety tab, and placing some Infirmaries: @G21 Infirmaries are very unappealing to live near, so consider their placement carefully, and add some Aesthetic structures if necessary to beautify the surrounding area. @L@L@LSTEP FIVE - Providing food @LThere is plenty of food in the city's Granaries, so just add Food Vendors to the Agoras to supply the city with much needed food: @G10 As the people of this city begin to eat regular meals, and see the healer, city hygiene will gradually improve. If a plague does break out, you can identify infected houses by the green haze hovering over them. When hygiene in the sample city is 'Excellent', you'll know your city is out of danger, and you can continue to the next tutorial.

message.title: Tutorial: Goods for Housing
message.content: Distributing goods @LIn addition to food, households need other goods from the Agora, such as fleece for clothing. The sample neighborhood has a working fleece industry, where shepherds tend the flock, shear sheep, and return to the Carding Shed with fleece. Fleece is then delivered to the nearest Storehouse - only food can be stored in a Granary. @LObserve this process, then return to learn how to provide the residents of your neighborhood with fleece. @L@L@LSTEP ONE - Producing Fleece @LFirst, place a Carding Shed next to a road in your neighborhood by selecting the Husbandry tab, and clicking the Herding button: @G06 Then select 'sheep', and place some sheep in the meadow. You can identify meadowland by the purple tufts of vegetation, which the sheep need to eat. @G40 The closer your Carding Shed is to the sheep pasture, the less distance the shepherds will need to travel to tend the flock. @L@L@LSTEP TWO - Storing Fleece and other goods @LBuild a Storehouse to store fleece by selecting the Distribution Tab, and clicking the Storehouse button: @G12 You can see how much fleece is stored in the city at the top of the Distribution Tab. @L@L@LStockpiling @LWhen you set a commodity be 'stockpiled', no one in the city can use it. Commodities so designated are shown in yellow, in parenthesis, on the Distribution Tab. Later on you may need to give this instruction, but right now you don't, so make sure none of your goods are set this way. @L@LTo stockpile an item, click on its name. To use the item freely, click on it again. @L@L@LSTEP THREE - Distributing fleece @LTo distribute fleece to your neighborhood's houses, you'll need another kind of vendor, a fleece vendor. Place a Fleece Vendors' stall on your Agora by selecting the Distribution Tab, and clicking the Agora button: @G10 The fleece vendor will head for the nearest Storehouse to fetch some fleece, which is then distributed by the Agora's peddler, along with food. @L@L@LFood and Goods in houses @LRight-click on any house to see what food and goods its residents have stored inside. When the residents of a Shack receive some fleece from the peddler, they'll upgrade their dwelling to a Homestead, or even to a Tenement, if its residents have access to two types of Culture. @L@LMake sure you're not stockpiling your fleece, or the fleece vendor won't be able to procure any. When you have a few Homesteads or Tenements in your neighborhood, you're ready to move on!

message.title: Tutorial: Making Olive Oil
message.content: Olive oil is needed by your city's households, and is produced by a two step process. In the sample neighborhood on the left side of the city, olives are harvested from olive orchards, then pressed at the Olive Press to produce oil. Olive oil is then distributed to houses in the same manner as fleece. Observe this, then return to learn how to grow olives for your neighborhood, on the right side of the city. @L@L@LSTEP ONE - Growing Olives @LSelect the Husbandry tab, then click the Orchards button, and plant some olive trees in a meadow: @G19 Olive trees must be grown in a meadow, because this is the only land fertile enough to support crops. Now place a Growers' Lodge, next to a road, so you'll have growers to tend the olive trees. @L@L@LSTEP TWO - Pressing the olives @LSelect the Industry tab, then click the Workshops button to place one or two Olive Presses next to a road: @G20 When olives are harvested, they'll be prepared at the Growers' Lodge then delivered directly to an Olive Press for processing. Surplus olives will be delivered to a Storehouse. @L@L@LSTEP THREE - Distributing olive oil @LAdd an Oil Vendor to your Agora, and the vendor will procure oil from a Storehouse, for the peddler to deliver to your neighborhood. Make sure you're not stockpiling olive oil, or no one will be able to get it! With a supply of olive oil, the Tenements in your neighborhood will become Apartments! @L@L@LLabor, Workers and Wages @LRight click on any working building, such as an Olive Press to see how many employees work there. Without enough population to staff all the working buildings in the city, production will suffer. Make sure not to build too many industries until you have the workforce to support them. On the Industry tab, you can change how much you pay your workers. If you pay too low a wage, you may become unpopular. @L@LWhen you have some Apartments in your neighborhood, you're ready to proceed to the next tutorial.

message.title: Tutorial: Build a City
message.content: Now is your chance to build your first small city from scratch! Also, while prior lessons have been 'open play', with no specific goals, here you'll need to achieve a very specific goal with your city. @L@L@LEpisode goals @LWhen you embark upon a full-fledged Adventure in Zeus, it will usually be divided into phases called 'episodes'. To complete each episode you'll have to achieve specific goals, which are listed at the top of this panel: @G13 When you complete a mission goal, it is checked off in the list above. To complete this episode you'll need to support at least 50 people in Apartments, by providing them with food, water, fleece, olive oil, and two types of culture! @L@LIf you think you're already familiar enough with the basic concepts of city building, you can skip ahead to the next tutorial, the first of the advanced tutorials. @L@L@LGetting started @LStart with a simple road network and some Common Housing, and soon workers will immigrate to the city: @G01 Make sure houses have access to the services of a superintendent from a Maintenance office, and to clean water from a Fountain: @G03 @G04 @L@L@LProviding food @LNext, provide your city's new households with fish to eat, by building some Fisheries, and Granaries to store the fish: @G05 @G11 Place a Common Agora to serve your houses, and add a Food Vendor's stall to procure fish from a Granary: @G10 The Agora's peddler will distribute the food to houses. @L@L@LHygiene and Safety @LIn addition to providing food, keep plague in check by building Infirmaries, to provide households with the services of a healer: @G21 If unrest becomes a problem, place some Watchposts so watchmen can patrol the streets: @G53 @L@L@LAdd a little Culture @LGive your citizens access to some cultural diversions by building Colleges to train philosophers, and Podiums where the philosophers can preach: @G07 A few Gymnasiums will also give your citizens something to do in their spare time: @G52 @L@L@LFleece @LNext you'll need to provide your people with fleece for clothing. Build a Carding Shed or two, and place some sheep in a meadow: @G06 Don't forget to build a storehouse to store the fleece: @G12 and add a Fleece Vendor's Stall to the Agora, to distribute the fleece to your city's households: @G10 @L@L@LOlive Oil @LBuild a Grower's Lodge, and plant some olive trees in a meadow: @G19 Remember to add an Oil Vendor's Stall to the Agora, so the oil can be distributed to your city's households. @L@L@LAesthetics and Appeal @LAs you build your city, improve the appeal of its neighborhoods by adding Recreational Areas, and Beautification structures: @G09 @G08 Before long, your city will prosper! Good Luck! Remember to check back here if you need help. @L @L

message.title: Tutorial - Interface
message.content: Welcome to the first advanced tutorial for Zeus. If you've completed the beginning tutorials, or played one of our city-building games before, this is a good place to start. For a refresher course in any of the basics, like housing, food production and agriculture, consult the beginning tutorials. @L@LIn this tutorial you'll have some fun while becoming familiar with the Zeus interface. See what Zeus has to offer by exploring the thriving city we've provided, and don't worry about money or placing buildings - just try things out, have some fun! If you encounter something you don't understand, return to this screen for more information by clicking the episode goals button: @G13 If you want to begin this lesson over again, click the 'start this tutorial over' button at the bottom of this panel. @L@L@LCategory tabs @LThe Control Panel, which you can see to the right of this panel, contains several category 'tabs', each relating to a particular aspect of building and managing a city. On each you'll find buttons for placing buildings, and summary information for the given category. Some of the category tabs are not available in this lesson - you'll learn about them later. The tabs, from top to bottom, are: @L@LPOPULATION - This tab gives information on housing availability and migration. Use this tab to build houses. @L@LHUSBANDRY - This tab gives information on food availability, and lets you build structures for growing crops, and raising livestock, and harvesting wild creatures for food. @L @LINDUSTRY - Here you set your workers' wage rate, allocate labor, and even shut industries down when necessary. Industrial buildings are used to harvest raw materials, and to manufacture most finished goods. @L @LDISTRIBUTION - This tab lists all the goods available to your city, and how much of each you have stored. Use this tab to place structures which store, distribute, and trade these commodities. @L @LHYGIENE AND SAFETY - This tab gives information on your city's hygiene, and unrest. Use this tab to place structures that keep plague and unrest in check, and provide maintenance services to your city's buildings. @L@L ADMINISTRATION - You'll learn about this tab in a later lesson, 'The Palace'. @L@L CULTURE - This tab covers the Pan-Hellenic Games, and allows you to place buildings that enrich the lives of your people. @L@L MYTHOLOGY - You'll learn about this tab in a later lesson, 'Mythology'. @L@L MILITARY - You'll learn about this tab in a later lesson, 'The Warrior Society'. @L@L AESTHETICS - Use the buildings available on this tab to make your city's neighborhoods more appealing. @L@L OVERVIEW - This tab gives you an at-a-glance summary of what's going on in your city, and also shows you how popular (or unpopular!) you are among your people. @L@LTake some time to look at the information provided on the various tabs. You can also use your mouse wheel to scroll between the tabs. For in-depth information relating to the selected tab, click on the small magnifying glass button. Peruse the various tabs, then return here to continue by clicking on the Episode Goals button: @G13 @L@L@LSpecial city views @LClick the various 'see . . .' buttons at the top of any tab to change the view of the city so you only see certain buildings and walkers. You can even place buildings while viewing the city this way. Tap the spacebar to toggle special views on and off. @L@LFulfilling Requests @LRequests by other cities are listed on the Overview tab too. A green light means you are capable of fulfilling the request. At the start of this tutorial, Mantineia will request 10 slabs of marble. When you have enough marble, a green light will appear next to the request. Click on the request to dispatch it. @L@LThe Overview Map @LThe Overview tab contains a small map of the entire city. Click on this map to jump around the city quickly. To display the overview map in place of the information area on all tabs, click the overview map tab at the top of the control panel: @G22 To return all tabs to normal information display, click the info tab: @G23 You can also use the 'tab' key on your keyboard to switch between these two displays. @L@L@LMessages @LYou'll receive messages about important events concerning your city. You can review your messages by clicking on the View Messages icon: @G24 Below this icon, an abbreviated version of each message is displayed when it arrives. Use the up and down arrows to scroll through these messages, and click on any one to read its full version. To control how messages are displayed when you receive them, choose Options: messages from the menu bar. @L@L@L'Go To' buttons @LWhen an event such as a plague, the arrival of a visitor or an invasion occurs, a 'go to' button appears above the message box, which you can click on to jump to the site of the event. @G25 During this tutorial, an earthquake will occur, which will give you a chance to try this out. @L @L

message.title: Tutorial - Trade
message.content: Trade @LYou can buy goods from other cities, and make money selling your city's products. If you haven't maintained good relations with the leader of another city, or if he is an outright rival, he won't want to trade with you. Click on the View World icon to see which cities will trade with you. In this tutorial, you'll see that Mantineia, an ally, is connected to your city, Megara, by a land trade route (red), and that Cyprus, a distant city, is connected to your city by a sea trade route (blue): @G26 Click on these cities to see what they buy and sell, and in what quantities, then return here to learn about importing and exporting. @L@L@LSTEP ONE - Importing @LMantineia sells bronze, which may be used to manufacture sculpture to sell to Cyprus for a profit! To trade with Mantineia, add a Trading Post to the sample city. On the Distribution Tab, click the Trade Buildings button, then Trading Post: Mantineia: @G27 The Trading Post is something like a large Storehouse. Place it next to a road near the Granary. Right click on the Post, then click the bronze 'not buying' button so it says, 'buying'. Soon traders from Mantineia will visit the Post, and exchange bronze for some of your drachmas. When you have some bronze in the Trading Post, return here to continue. @L@L@LSTEP TWO - Making Sculpture @LWith a supply of bronze you can make sculpture to sell to Cyprus for a profit. On the Industry tab, click the Workshops button, then place a Sculpture Studio in the city: @G20 Soon deliverymen from the Trading Post will start supplying the Studio with imported bronze, so sculptures may be cast. When you have a working Sculpture Studio, return to learn how to export sculpture. @L@L@LSTEP THREE - Exporting @LTo export sculpture to Cyprus, which trades by water, you'll need to build a Pier. A Pier is like a Trading Post for ships. Select the Distribution Tab, then click the Trade Buildings button, and select Pier: Cyprus: @G27 Place the Pier along a straight section of coast, and make sure it's connected by road to your Sculpture Studios. Near one of the fisheries is a good spot. Right click on the Pier, then click the sculpture 'not selling' button so it says 'selling'. The Sculpture Studio will deliver its products to the Pier, where they'll be picked up by Cypriot trade ships for a hefty sum! Export items in a trade building set to 'selling' are reserved for traders only, cannot be used for any other purpose, and are not counted on the Distribution Tab. @L@L@LAnnual Profit @LTo complete this episode, you need to turn a profit of 500 Drachmas in a single year. This 'annual profit' goal is displayed at the top of this panel, on the left. To its right you'll see an assessment of your progress toward achieving this goal. @L@L@LStock Limits @LFor exports, the stock limit dictates how much of the item will be regularly kept on hand, and reserved, for traders to buy. Each trader can carry only a limited amount. If you set the limit too high, the trader may not be able to purchase all the reserved goods in a single visit, and your people may be deprived of some goods they need. @L@LFor imports, each time a trader visits he will drop off goods until the stock limit is reached, after which deliverymen will empty the trading facility. Don't import more than you need, or you could go broke very quickly. For importing bronze in this episode, 12 is a good stock limit. @L@L@LSell enough sculpture and you'll meet the annual profit goal needed to complete this episode, or click 'next tutorial' to move ahead when you think you're ready. @L @L

message.title: Mythology: Building a Sanctuary
message.content: This tutorial is comprised of two episodes. In the first episode you'll learn how to worship Dionysus by building a Sanctuary in his honor. In the second episode, you'll put this Sanctuary to use for your city. @L@L@LThe Gods of Greece @LThe gods crave the worship of mortals like you, and can offer you many things in return for your devotion. Gods will visit your city from time to time, extolling the many benefits they can provide for you should you choose to worship them. @L@L@LSanctuaries @LTo worship a god you must construct a Sanctuary dedicated to him or her. This is no mean feat; constructing a Sanctuary requires marble, wood and sculpture, and the services of artisans. To complete this episode, the first part of the Mythology tutorial, you need to erect a Sanctuary dedicated to Dionysus, called the 'Grove of Dionysus'. @L@L@LSTEP ONE - Quarrying the Marble @LTo build any Sanctuary, the first thing you'll need is marble. Marble may be obtained from a quarry like the one behind the Maintenance Office. To quarry marble, select the Industry tab, click the Raw Materials button, then select Masonry Shop: @G28 Masonry Shops don't need to be right next to the quarry, but the closer they are, the faster their stonecutters can get to the site. Make sure you have a Storehouse ready to accept the quarried marble. @L@LYou'll need eight slabs of marble just to place the base and steps for Dionysus' Sanctuary. @L@L@LSTEP TWO - Placing the Sanctuary @LWhen you have enough marble, select the Mythology tab, click the Sanctuaries button, then select Grove of Dionysus: @G29 Place the Sanctuary wherever you'd like, then return here to continue. Make sure you're not 'stockpiling' marble, or you'll never finish constructing the Sanctuary! @L@L@LSTEP THREE - Hiring Artisans @LArtisans perform all the work of constructing a Sanctuary. On the Mythology tab, click the Artisans' Guild button to place some Guilds close to the construction site: @G30 Artisans will report to work at the construction site, and call for deliveries of marble, wood and sculpture when they need it. @L@L@LSTEP FOUR - Harvesting Wood @LYou have marble and sculpture, but you'll also need wood to aid construction of the Sanctuary. Lumberjacks from a Timber Mill harvest wood from trees. Click the Raw Materials button, then place a Timber Mill along a road: @G28 Soon the Timber Mill will start supplying Storehouses with wood, which the artisans will procure as needed. @L@LAs soon as the Sanctuary is finished, this episode will be complete, and you'll be shown the 'Victory Screen'. From there you can proceed to the next episode of this tutorial, where you'll learn how to put this Sanctuary to use. @L @L

message.title: Mythology: gods, monsters and heroes
message.content: Welcome to episode two of the Mythology tutorial. You'll be shown an introductory screen like this whenever you proceed to another episode within the same Adventure, or when you begin a new Adventure altogether. In this episode, the second and last of the Mythology tutorial, you're going to learn how to battle monsters, summon heroes, and pray to the gods. @L@L@LThe Olympian Gods @LThe gods of Greece have their own agenda, and rarely get along with one another. Whatever adventure you undertake, some gods will support your efforts, while others will seek to thwart you. Those on your side, like Dionysus, periodically appeal to you for worship, encouraging you to build a Sanctuary in their honor. Those who oppose you may not make their presence known, until you do something to offend them. @L@L@LSacrifices and Sanctuary benefits @LA Sanctuary needs regular sacrifices to function, so that its god can appear in the city, walk the streets, and sanctify certain buildings. Each god also provides other benefits. For example at Dionysus' Sanctuary you can grow grapevines, which can be turned into wine at a Winery. You can also pray to Dionysus for wine. @L@L@LTending Grapevines @LYou'll need some growers to tend the grapevines at Dionysus' Sanctuary. Select the Husbandry tab, then click the Orchards button to place some Growers' Lodges along a road, preferably close to the Sanctuary: @G19 Growers from the lodge will tend, prune and harvest the grapes, then deliver them to a Winery or Storehouse. @L@L@LMaking Wine @LA Winery receives grapes from a Growers' Lodge, and presses them into wine. Build a Winery with the Workshops button on the Industry tab: @G20 The Winery will deliver amphorae of wine to a Storehouse, where they may be procured by an Agora's wine vendor. @L@L@LMonsters and Heroes @LIf a Cyclops happens to show up, you can call upon the legendary hero, Odysseus, to deal with the matter. Once you get word that the one-eyed beast is on his way, build a Hero's Hall for Odysseus by clicking on the Hero's Hall button on the Mythology tab: @G31 Heroes are in high demand throughout Greece, so you can't build a Hall unless you really need the hero. You won't be able to call Odysseus until you've prepared the city to meet his high standards. @L@L@LCalling forth the hero @LRight click on the Hero's Hall to see what Odysseus expects of the city before he deems it worthy of his presence. One thing you'll need to call the hero is wine, which you may obtain by praying to Dionysus at his Sanctuary. Don't worry if it takes you some time to get rid of the Cyclops - in this episode he's mostly interested in your sheep, and he'll occupy himself flattening them with his club for a while. @L@L@LRetaliation @LOf course you've got to rid your city of monsters, but don't be surprised if the Cyclops' father, the god Poseidon has something to say about this. @L@L@LGods vs. Gods @LIf a god like Poseidon feels the need to attack your city, only another, more powerful god may combat him. Zeus is the only god strong enough to stand up to his brother Poseidon, but you can't build a Sanctuary for Zeus in this tutorial. Stick around to experience Poseidon's rage, and when you've had enough, you're ready to move on. @L @L

message.title: Tutorial: The Palace
message.content: Citizen Soldiers @LThough you cannot build a standing army, your ordinary citizens will fight to defend the city. Those from the lowest strata of society fight as 'rabble', armed only with rocks to throw at the enemy. In this lesson you're going to learn how to call your people to arms, and command them in battle. To do this, you will first need a Palace from which to command them. @L@L@LSTEP ONE - Building a Palace @LFrom the Administration tab, click the Palace button, and place a Palace on the long section of road near the Infirmary and Podium. The Palace is a large, rectangular building, so before actually placing it, use the 'r' key to rotate it to the orientation you prefer: @G34 Even when going about their daily lives, the people of your city automatically divide themselves into military companies, and place their standards around the Palace. Rabble standards are capped by a fist clenching a rock. To see standards located behind the Palace, you may need to rotate the city using the button at the bottom of the Control Panel. Build the Palace, observe the standards, then return here to continue. @L@L@LSTEP TWO - Moving Standards @LThe standard tells a company where you want it to go, when you call them to arms. To move a company's standard, click on its base, then click again where you want to place it. You may need to rotate the city to select standards located behind the Palace. You can return standards to the Palace in the same way. @L@L@LCalling the Soldiers to Arms @LSimply moving a company's standard into the field is not the same as calling its soldiers to arms. To call a company's soldiers from their homes or 'muster' them, click on the standard then click the Muster button: @G35 The same button is used to send the company's soldiers home when you don't need them. This will not automatically return the standards to the Palace. Keeping soldiers mustered when there's no fighting will make you unpopular, but it's often a good idea to leave standards at strategic locations in the field, as long as you send the soldiers home. @L@LMorale @LIf a company's morale falls too low as a result of combat, its standard will be returned to the Palace, and its men will flee to their homes until they regain their composure. @L@L@LSTEP THREE - Giving Orders to companies @LAfter selecting a company standard, use the buttons on the Control Panel to rotate the company's line, or to tell them to use defensive, offensive, or special tactics: @G37 @G38 @G39 Practice moving standards around and giving orders. @L@L@LInvasions @LIn this lesson, the rival city of Nemea will invade, so that you may have the opportunity to apply your tactical skills to defend the city. You may also bribe invaders to leave the city unharmed, if you don't want to risk the lives of your citizens. @L@L@LAutomatically responding to invasions @LYou can use the Auto-defend button to instruct your military to automatically respond to invasions when they occur, and to stand down when the city is safely out of danger: @G36 This instruction must be given WELL in advance of an invasion, so if you don't intend to control your military forces manually, always leave Auto-defend 'on'. @L@L@LSaving the city @LIf you successfully save the city from invasion, by any means, you'll be able to build a Commemorative Monument from the Aesthetics tab, to celebrate your triumph! @G56 @L@LReturn here when you're ready to learn about the other functions of the Palace. @L@L@LCollecting Taxes @LWith a Palace in your city, you can also collect taxes. On the Administration tab, click the Tax Office button to place some Tax Offices, and soon clerks will begin roaming the city's neighborhoods collecting taxes: @G54 Set the tax rate with the arrows on the Administration tab. A high tax rate could reduce your popularity. Click 'see tax income' to see which houses are visited by a clerk, and how much money their residents pay. When you've collected some taxes, you're ready to move on to the next tutorial. @L@L @L

message.title: Tutorial: The Warrior Society
message.content: Elite Warriors @LIn this tutorial you're going to learn how to create and command the most advanced types of fighting men. Well-to-do citizens who can afford their own armor live in much finer housing than the 'rabble', and fight as foot soldiers called 'hoplites'. The wealthiest individuals, those who can afford to keep their own horses as well as armor, fight as horsemen. In this lesson you'll learn how to support hoplites; you'll learn how to support horsemen in a later tutorial. @L@L@LSTEP ONE - Elite housing @LElite warriors must live in Elite Housing, and no amount of fine goods or culture is going to turn a common household into an elite household! You need some food, fleece and oil just to place an Elite house, and each must be placed in an appealing area. Select the Population tab, click the Elite housing button, then place three Elite houses amongst the gardens near the Palace: @G32 After some people move in, right click on one of the Elite houses to see what its residents need in order to become more affluent. After you do this, return here to continue. @L@L@LSTEP TWO - Armor @LYour recently established Elite households need armor so the men of the family can equip themselves as hoplites. The Grand Agora can hold up to six Vendors, and thus provide all the goods needed by elite households. Add an Arms Vendor to the Grand Agora, by clicking the Agoras button on the Distribution Tab: @G10 Soon the arms vendor will procure armor from the Storehouse, so the Agora's peddler can distribute it to Elite households. A household's supply of armor does not need to be replenished unless its wearer is killed in combat. When some elite households obtain armor, additional 'hoplite' standards, capped with bronze helmets, will appear around the Palace! It takes a few households to make up a single company of hoplites. @L@L@LSTEP THREE - Assessing your Army @LAll your companies are represented at the top of the Military tab by a fist (rabble), a helmet (hoplites) or a horse (horsemen). Click 'see security' at the top of this tab, to view only military buildings and walkers, and to see which Elite houses have armed hoplites living inside. @L@L@LTriremes @LA Trireme Wharf needs wood and armor to produce a Trireme with a complement of marines. To build a Trireme Wharf, click the Military Workshops button on the Military tab, then find a good place on the coast to place the Wharf: @G33 Trireme crews are summoned, and triremes are controlled, via a set of orders buttons similar to those of companies. Operating a trireme requires a lot of manpower, so it's a good idea to send your crews home when they're not needed. @L@L@L Defensive fortifications @LTowers and Walls are manned by citizens from the lowest ranks of society, and can be an effective way to protect your city from invasion. Defensive structures are built from the Fortifications button on the Military tab: @G55 Place Walls at strategic locations to defend your city, or even to encircle your city. You can make Walls as thick as you like by placing an additional wall along an existing one. @L@LPlace Gatehouses at certain points along the Wall, to allow traders and other well-intentioned visitors access to the city. When placing a Gatehouse, use the 'r' key to orient it the way you like. @L@LTowers may be placed onto Walls that are at least double thickness, using the Fortifications button. Towers must be manned, and require a road connection to the Palace. @L@LCalling soldiers en masse @LTo call all your foot soldiers to arms, or call all crews to their triremes, or man all towers, click the 'call all', 'crew all', or 'not manning' buttons on the Military tab. Manning all your city's Towers and triremes, and mustering all your soldiers, will impact the available labor pool, often dramatically. It's best not to call upon your military unless their services are truly needed. @L@LWhen you've successfully defended your city from invasion by Nemea, you're ready to move on to the next tutorial. @L @L

message.title: Tutorial: Preparing for the Colony
message.content: In this tutorial you'll start with an already thriving city, and learn how to establish a colony to serve its needs. There are three episodes in this tutorial. In the second episode, you'll leave the parent-city, Megara, to actually build the colony. @L@LSetting goods aside for the Colony @LYou often have to set aside goods in preparation for starting a colony. To complete this episode, and move on to establish the colony, you'll need to set aside 8 amphorae of wine. Wine is also craved by Elite households (and Centaurs, for that matter). @L@L@LSTEP ONE - Planting Grapevines @LSelect the Husbandry tab, then click the Orchards button and plant several grapevines: @G19 @G40 Grapevines must be planted on meadowland, but do not need to be next to a road. The more grapevines you plant, the more grapes will be harvested, provided you have enough growers to tend them. @L@L@LSTEP TWO - Tending the Grapevines @LOlive trees and grapevines are tended by growers from the Growers' Lodge. Select the Husbandry tab, then click the Orchards button to place some Growers' Lodges along a road, preferably close to the grapevines: @G19 Growers from the lodge will tend, prune and harvest the grapes, then deliver them to a Winery or Storehouse. @L@L@LSTEP THREE - Making Wine @LA Winery receives grapes from a Growers' Lodge, and presses them into wine. Build a Winery with the Workshops button on the Industry tab: @G20 The Winery will deliver amphorae of wine to a Storehouse, where they may be procured by an Agora's wine vendor. @L@L@LSTEP FOUR - Setting aside wine for the Colony @LWhen you begin making wine, you'll see a 'set aside' button at the top of this panel, showing how much wine you have stored. When you have at least 8 amphorae of wine in a Storehouse, click the 'set aside' button above, then right click to EXIT THIS PANEL. Do NOT click the 'Next Tutorial' button if you want to continue to the colony episode. When the month is over, the Victory Screen will announce your triumph, and you'll be able to continue to the colony episode. @L @L

message.title: Tutorial - Colonies
message.content: Putting the Colony to work @LSTEP ONE - Trading with Halicarnassos @LNow that you're back in Megara, place a Trading Post for Halicarnassos, to import wheat and bronze from the colony. These goods will help you build a more powerful military: the bronze may be forged into armor, and the wheat may be used to raise horses for horsemen. @L@L@LSTEP TWO - Making Armor @LElite households need armor so their occupants can equip themselves as warriors. Click the Military Workshops button on the Military tab, select Armory, then place an Armory: @G33 Soon the Trading Post will start delivering bronze to the Armory, where it will be pounded into armor, and delivered to the nearest Storehouse. @L@L@LSTEP THREE - Raising Horses @LThe wealthiest residents of your city can afford to keep their own horses, which they will proudly ride into battle as horsemen. Horses are raised on a Horse Ranch, and brought to elite houses by the Horse Trainer, an Agora Vendor. To build a Horse Ranch, click the Military Workshops button on the Military tab: @G33 Make sure you're importing wheat from Halicarnassos, and it will be delivered to the Horse Ranch from the Trading Post. @L@L@LSTEP FOUR - Horsemen @LHorsemen need armor, wine and of course horses. Add vendors for these items to the Agora by clicking the Agoras button on the Distribution Tab: @G10 When a peddler delivers wine, armor and horses to some Elite houses, they'll transform into Estates, and their residents will become horsemen. When you have four horsemen in the city, you will have completed this episode. @L @L

message.title: Tutorial: Establishing the Colony
message.subtitle: Normally you'll have more than one site to choose from when establishing a colony, but here only Halicarnassos is available. This site offers good soil for wheat farming, and has some deposits of silver and copper ore.
message.content: Getting Started @LEventually this colony will supply Megara with wheat, bronze, and annual tribute payments. You already know the basics of setting up a city, but you'll need to learn about growing wheat to feed this colony, and how to mine silver to make some money. @L@L@LSTEP ONE - Farming @LSeveral different crops may be grown throughout the Pan-Hellenic world, but the soil of this area is only good for growing wheat. To place some Wheat Farms, click the Farms button on the Husbandry tab: @G41 @G40 All Farms must be placed on meadowland, identified by purple tufts of vegetation. Farms must also have access to a road. You may have to build some Water Crossings, from the Administration tab, to access the meadowland. @L@LBuild some houses, and set up some wheat farming to be able to feed your people, then return here to continue. @L@L@LSTEP TWO - Mining Silver @LYou won't get far without a source of income. Halicarnassos offers rich deposits of silver ore, which can be struck into coins. You can see the silver ore in the rock to the north: @G43 To mine silver and strike coins, place a Mint by clicking the Raw Materials button on the Industry tab: @G28 You don't need to place the Mint right next to silver ore. Miners will travel as far as they have to, but the shorter their trip, the faster the Mint will be supplied. Once the Mint is up and running, drachmas will start flowing into your treasury. @L@LWhen you've struck some coins, return here to continue. @L@L@LSTEP THREE - Making Requests @LColonies often need to rely on their parent city for support. To develop some of this colony's housing into Apartments, you'll need fleece and oil. You can't import these items, but you can requisition them from the parent-city, Megara or request them from your ally, Mantineia. Click on the View World button, then click on one of the cities on the map, such as Megara: @G46 When a city is selected like this on the World Map, the World Control Panel shows you information about it, and provides buttons for you to interact with the city. @L@LWith either Megara or Mantineia selected, click the Make Request button, and ask for what you need: @G44 Make sure you have space in a Storehouse to receive any goods you request. @L@LRequesting Military Aid @LWith only rabble at your disposal, you won't be able to defend the fledgling colony very well without some assistance. If a rival seeks to take advantage of the colony's vulnerability, and launches an invasion, you can ask your allies, or the parent city to loan you military forces to defend the colony. Of course, you can always bribe the invaders, if you can afford it. @L@L@LSTEP FOUR - Returning the Favor @LThe more you ask for, the more other leaders will expect in return, in the form of gifts and your fulfilling their requests. Other leaders' requests and demands are displayed on the Overview tab. To fulfill a request, click on it, or select the requesting city on the World Map, then click the Fulfill Request button: @G47 Even if a request is overdue, it's still beneficial to make the effort, and send the items asked for before the request vanishes entirely. @L@L@LGiving Gifts @LTo give a gift, select a city on the World Map, then click the Give Gift button: @G48 Giving gifts and fulfilling requests makes allies and subjects more likely to help you, and makes rivals less likely to attack. @L@LYour rival Nemea may occasionally demand wine during this episode. You may acquire wine by asking Megara, or you may ask Megara to loan military forces to defend the colony, in case Nemea decides to attack. @L@L@LHow other leaders regard you @LYou'll see how each leader feels about you on the World Control Panel, when you select his city. Click on this descriptor for advice. @LTo see how your relationship with this leader got this way, click on the small history scroll: @G45 A 'thumbs up' means the event was looked upon favorably by the leader; a 'thumbs down' means it was not. @L@L@LSTEP FIVE - Mining Copper and Making Bronze @LCopper can be alloyed to make bronze. Copper is mined in a manner similar to silver, but from a different kind of rock: @G42 To mine copper and make bronze, place a Foundry by clicking the Raw Materials button on the Industry tab: @G28 You don't need to place the Foundry right next to the source of copper ore. Miners will travel as far as they need to, but shortening their trip means the Foundry will work more efficiently. @L@L@LSTEP SIX - Setting goods aside for the Parent City @LJust as you needed to set aside wine in Megara to prepare for establishing this colony, here you need to set aside some bronze and wheat for Megara, to prove the colony's viability. When you have enough of these items stored up, click the appropriate 'set aside' button to satisfy the episode goal, and return to the parent city, Megara. @L @L
