message.title: Tutorial - Peace and War
message.content: Politics and Diplomacy @LGreek politics can be both dangerous and lucrative. You need to depend on your allies and subjects if you are to survive and prosper in this world, and find success on your many Adventures. To complete this episode, you'll need to conquer your rival, the city of Nemea, and you may not be able to do this without some help. @L@L@LDiplomatic status @LA city can be your ally, rival, or subject. Subjects are colonies you've established, or vassals you've acquired through conquest. @L@LAllies are generally happy to help you, and will trade with you. Be generous to an ally, and he may provide military support for one of your campaigns, or even conquer a rival on your behalf. @L@LRivals, though not necessarily openly hostile, consider you a competitor, and do not want you to succeed. They will not trade with you, and will not think twice about making unreasonable demands. @L@LSubjects always try to obey your wishes, must pay regular tribute to you, and will trade with you. @L@L@LInteracting with other cities @LWhen you select a city on the World Map, Action buttons appear on the World Control Panel, allowing you to interact with the city. Different actions are possible, depending on what type of city is selected. @L@LConquest @LYou may want to conquer a city because it has something you want, or has threatened or even attacked you . . . or maybe because you just feel like expanding your influence! In this episode, you need to conquer Nemea. To try to conquer another city, select it, then click the Attack button, and enlist forces for the attack: @G50 If you are attacking a rival, any allies willing to join you on the attack will appear in the lower right corner of this screen. If you successfully conquer the city, it will become your vassal. Attacking allies can have disastrous ramifications, whether you win or lose, as your other allies won't easily trust you any more. @L@LSubjects and Tribute @LVassals and colonies have to fulfill all your requests, and pay regular tribute. If your own city is conquered by a rival, you'll have to pay tribute. It is quite possible to find yourself paying tribute to a rival while simultaneously receiving it from a vassal! @L@LConducting Raids @LIf you lack the forces to attempt conquest, you can simply raid a city for plunder. Conducting a raid is not as risky as attempting conquest, but the rewards are not as great nor as permanent as with conquest. To raid another city, select it, click the Raid button, and enlist forces for the raid: @G51 Plunder @LTell your forces what you'd like them to procure as plunder. Each survivor returns with plunder, so the bigger your forces, the more likely they are to survive, and the more plunder you'll receive. Triremes can carry the most, followed by horsemen then hoplites @L@LMaking demands @LJust as you can peacefully request things from allies and subjects, so can you make demands of your rivals. If a rival leader doesn't think you're powerful enough to back up the demand, he won't feel compelled to comply. Sometimes even a rival may respond to a peaceful request, if his regard for you is really high. @L@LOther cities on the World Map display small shield icons, roughly indicating their military capabilities. Coins approximate their economic capabilities. @L@LHave fun conquering Nemea! @L @L

message.title: Tutorial - Big City
message.content: The Wonders of Greece @LThis is the final tutorial for Zeus: Master of Olympus. Here you'll find a large prosperous city for you to explore and study, complete with Sanctuaries dedicated to Apollo and Ares. Ares will patrol the streets, accompanied by his fearsome dragon, and you may consult the Oracle of Apollo to see into the future. @L@LThere are no goals in this lesson, and no pressure to move on. You may want to return to this tutorial often, to see how a certain industry works, or to peruse the interface. You'll even find advice, below, based on the experience of other leaders who have come before you. @L@L@LHints and Tips @L@LSuck up to your neighbors @LGive other leaders gifts of goods or money now and then, especially if you have an excess of goods that you can afford to part with. Pay attention to other leaders' requests and fulfill them when you can. It always pays to have a few favors you can pull in when you're in a jam. @L@LButter up your Rivals @LIf you are very nice to your rivals, even they may be willing to provide you with goods when you are in need of them. @L@LSee into the future @LThe Oracle of Apollo and Zeus' Stronghold contain Oracles that can predict the future. @L@LPray to the Gods @LDon't forget to pray to the gods at their Sanctuaries when you need help. Gods will do anything from filling your Storehouses with goods, to joining you on a military campaign or improving city hygiene. @L@LListen to your people @LCitizens of your city will tell you what they think about living in the city. Right click on them to hear what they have to say. @L@LLay out roads carefully @LThe fewer intersections walkers encounter, the more efficient they will be. Try to plan your neighborhoods so that YOU are deciding where the walkers go and not leaving the decision up to them. Roadblocks are very useful for this purpose. @L@LDecrease Walker Travel Distance @LThe closer workshops are to their sources of raw materials, the higher their annual production will be. Also try to minimize the distance that workers such as Herders, Growers, and Miners have to travel. @L@LUse foresight in city planning @LKeep in mind that usable land is often limited. When constructing new buildings, take care to leave appropriate space for structures you may need to build in the future. Some o' them Sanctuaries is huge! @L@LPace yourself @LTake the time now and then to gauge your situation. In some situations you'll have to build fast and furious to meet goals, requests, or demands. In other instances you won't be able to do everything at once - you'll have to bide your time until the right opportunity presents itself (a new city begins trading with you, a resource or new building becomes available, a gift, a quest, etc.). @L@LUsing Culture Venues @LThe Stadium, Theater, and Podium all act as 'magnets' for their respective walkers, coming from training facilities. Walkers from the Gymnasium, Drama School, and College will head straight for these venues, ignoring roadblocks on their way. Keep this in mind as you try to plan for culture in your city. @L@LWatch your money @LIf you find yourself in financial trouble, decrease imports or increase exports, reduce wages or increase taxes. But remember these are only temporary fixes. Also, don't be afraid to ask other cities for help. @L@LExport, export, export @LHarvest local raw materials or buy them if necessary. Refine them into finished goods and sell them at a profit. This is your best way to make money. @L@LShift labor @LLabor shortages are often unavoidable. In these cases you might want to temporarily shift labor away from less-essential sectors of the workforce to concentrate on your city's immediate needs. Raising wages will draw more workers from your existing population, but don't do this for too long, or you could wind up broke. @L@LSend your Trireme Workers Home @LTrireme Wharves require 100 employees to operate. If you are experiencing a labor shortage, make sure that your triremes are unmanned. @L@LProtect your Palace @LAlways protect your Palace. If enemy armies destroy your Palace, you will be defeated and forced to pay tribute to them. @L@LMoving Your Entire Military @LTo move multiple standards at once, click on one to bring up the orders interface, then drag a box around all of the standards that you want to select. Scroll to the desired location, and click to place all of the standards. This method of multiple selection can also be used to issue commands to several companies at once. @L@LLeave Standards in the field @LLeave company standards at the site of battle after you send your troops home. Often enemies will approach from the same direction. You can save time mustering your troops if you already have their standards at a spot where the enemy is likely to attack. @L@LWorking with Earthquake Cracks @LShort bridges can be built over straight sections of earthquake-cracked land. @L @L @L
